intro.title: Introduction
paras: The First Thirumurai opens the Thiru Arutpa, the Songs of Grace of Ramalinga Adigal, Vallalar. It holds eight poems and 1,861 verses. Two of them are long chains of couplets (kalivenba). The Petitionary Kalivenba runs to 418 couplets, and Instructing the Heart to 705.

The book begins at the feet of God. In thirty-two long verses, Praise of the Holy Feet names them again and again. They dance in the golden hall. They lift up the souls sinking in birth after birth. These are the feet that walked from house to house in Kacchur, begging rice for a hungry devotee. In these songs God goes to the hungry.

The Petitionary Kalivenba is a pilgrimage made in words. Couplet after couplet, Vallalar greets Siva in one temple town after another, along both banks of the Kaveri, in Eelam, in the Pandya and Kongu countries, in the Thondai country and in the North. Then he turns and pleads, and he hides nothing. “In this world, I have never adopted the vow of non-killing,” he confesses. He asks only that the Lord's compassion surround him.

Instructing the Heart is the longest poem. Vallalar talks to his own heart as to a close friend who keeps going astray. He tells it what the body is made of, what wealth does to people, how near death stands. God, he tells it, is the compassionate one who came as a mother to a woman heavy with child, the good Mother who could not bear to see our hunger and fed us rice in the night. And he gives it a rule: “If you see those who do not unswervingly hold the vow of non-killing, consider them as a mere blade of grass and cast them aside.”

The Venba Verses on Love for Siva, the Garland for the Great God and the Appeal to Divine Grace are songs of love and of complaint. Vallalar calls God his Mother and Father. He spins, he says, like a speck of dust in the wind, and asks why the cool grace is held back. He praises the companion who unties the bonds that create forms of caste and shapes him into a form of light.

The book ends at Otriyur, the temple town by the sea at the northern edge of Chennai. The Ruby Garland of Beauty is sung to the Goddess Vadivudai, who dwells there with the Lord. In the Garland of Amorous Hints a young woman tells her friend about the Lord of Otriyur, who comes to her door as a beggar, speaks in riddles and holds out his hand for alms. “What is this, my friend?” she asks at the end of every verse.
One thread runs through all eight poems. It is Jeevakarunyam, compassion for every living being, which Vallalar later taught as the one path to ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace Light, open to all.

Each verse is given in four layers: the original Tamil, an ISO 15919 transliteration, a translation and a short commentary. Editor's notes under three titles give the regions of the temples, the numbering of the printed edition and the theme lines of the last poem. A glossary explains the Tamil terms. The Tamil has been checked against the 1896 printed edition.

intro.title: A Note on Context
paras: These are among Vallalar's earliest songs. They come from the years when he worshipped God through the forms of the Saiva tradition. In them he praises Siva at temple after temple, sings to the Goddess at Otriyur, honors Murugan, and tells his heart to chant the five letters, Namasivaya (the Panchaksharam). “Chant the supreme five-letter mantra of Siva,” he says.

He did not stay there. In the Great Teaching (Perupadesam) of 1873 he told those gathered to place no aim in the religions, Saivism among them, and he named himself as the witness. His hold on the Saiva religion had once been beyond measure. For proof he pointed to this very collection: “The hymns I have sung, gathered in the Thiru Arutpa, are enough.” Why had he held to it so firmly? He answered:
அப்போது எனக்கு அவ்வளவு கொஞ்சம் அற்ப அறிவாக இருந்தது.
“Because at that time I had only so little, such petty knowledge.”

In that same teaching he gave one mantra to all: Arutperunjothi Arutperunjothi, Thanipperunkarunai Arutperunjothi (Vast Grace-Light, Vast Grace-Light, Unique Vast Compassion, Vast Grace-Light). From then on he taught the worship of Arutperunjothi, the Vast Grace-Light, alone. His late songs in the Sixth Thirumurai sing of that Light.

So these poems are an early stage of one journey, and a sincere one. The longing in them is real. The vow of non-killing, the pity for the hungry and the honesty about his own faults are already here. Read them as the first steps of the man who later expanded and evolved even further up until the full realization of the Vast Grace-Light.

tamil: பரசுகம் தன்மயம் சச்சிதா னந்தமெய்ப் பரமவே காந்தநிலயம்
பரமஞா னம்பரம சத்துவம கத்துவம் பரமகை வல்யநிமலம்
பரமதத் துவநிரதி சயநிட்க ளம்பூத பௌதிகா தாரநிபுணம்
translit: paracivamciṉmayam pūraṇam civapōka pākkiyam paramanitiyam paracukam taṉmayam caccitā ṉantameyp paramavē kāntanilayam paramañā ṉamparama cattuvama kattuvam paramakai valyanimalam paramatat tuvanirati cayaniṭka ḷampūta pautikā tāranipuṇam
translation: Supreme Siva, the form of pure consciousness, the perfect whole, the blessing of divine bliss, the ultimate treasure, the supreme joy, the very essence, the truth of existence, consciousness, and bliss, the highest solitary abode, the supreme wisdom, the supreme truth and greatness, the spotless supreme liberation, the supreme reality that is unsurpassed and without parts, the skillful support of the elements and all physical forms.
commentary: Vallalar opens this great poem of praise by naming God as the perfect reality that holds everything together. He calls the Divine the form of pure consciousness and the highest treasure of bliss. Whole and without parts, this reality is still the hidden foundation of every element and form in the world.

tamil: பவபந்த நிக்ரக வினோதச களம்சிற் பரம்பரா னந்தசொருபம்
பரிசயா தீதம்சு யம்சதோ தயம்வரம் பரமார்த்த முக்தமௌனம்
படனவே தாந்தாந்த மாகமாந் தாந்தநிரு பாதிகம் பரமசாந்தம்
பரநாத தத்துவாந் தம்சகச தரிசனம் பகிரங்க மந்தரங்கம்
translit: pavapanta nikraka viṉōtaca kaḷamciṟ paramparā ṉantacorupam paricayā tītamcu yamcatō tayamvaram paramārtta muktamauṉam paṭaṉavē tāntānta mākamān tāntaniru pātikam paramacāntam paranāta tattuvān tamcakaca taricaṉam pakiraṅka mantaraṅkam
translation: The playful presence with form that destroys the bonds of worldly existence, the form of supreme bliss and consciousness, beyond all familiarity, the self-existent eternal dawn, the most excellent, the liberated silence of supreme truth, the attribute-less reality spoken of as the end of Vedanta and Agamanta, the supreme peace, the end of the supreme sound, the natural vision, the external and the internal.
commentary: The Divine is an active presence that shatters our worldly attachments. Vallalar calls it the final truth pointed to by Vedanta (the philosophical end of the Vedas) and Agamanta (the peak of the Agamic scriptures), yet it rests beyond all scriptures in liberated silence. It is the deepest peace inside us. It is also the natural vision we meet in the world outside.

tamil: பரவியோ மம்பரம ஜோதிமயம் விபுலம் பரம்பர மனந்தமசலம்
பரமலோ காதிக்க நித்தியசாம் பிராச்சியம் பரபதம் பரமசூக்ஷ்மம்
பராபர மநாமய நிராதர மகோசரம் பரமதந் திரம்விசித்ரம்
பராமுத நிராகரம் விகாசனம் விகோடணம் பரசுகோ தயமக்ஷயம்
translit: paraviyō mamparama jōtimayam vipulam parampara maṉantamacalam paramalō kātikka nittiyacām pirācciyam parapatam paramacūkṣmam parāpara manāmaya nirātara makōcaram paramatan tiramvicitram parāmuta nirākaram vikācaṉam vikōṭaṇam paracukō tayamakṣayam
translation: The supreme space, the form of supreme Jothi, the vastness, the highest of the high, the endless, the immovable, the eternal sovereignty exceeding the supreme worlds, the supreme state, the ultimate subtlety, the supreme and the beyond, the flawless, the unsupported, the imperceptible, the supreme and wondrous system, the supreme nectar, the formless, the radiant unfolding, the imperishable dawn of supreme joy.
commentary: Jothi (the divine light of grace) is the word to hold onto. Vallalar sees this light as endless space, so vast and subtle that it rules over the highest worlds and needs no support at all. It has no form, and the senses cannot grasp it. It keeps unfolding, a wondrous dawn of supreme joy.

tamil: பரிபவ விமோசனம் குணரகிதம் விசுவம்ப தித்துவ பரோபரீணம்
பஞ்சகிர்த் தியசுத்த கர்த்தத்து வம்தற்ப ரம்சிதம் பரவிலாசம்
பகர்சுபா வம்புனித மதுலமது லிதமம்ப ராம்பர நிராலம்பனம்
பரவுசா க்ஷாத்கார நிரவய வங்கற்ப னாதீத நிருவிகாரம்
translit: paripava vimōcaṉam kuṇarakitam vicuvampa tittuva parōparīṇam pañcakirt tiyacutta karttattu vamtaṟpa ramcitam paravilācam pakarcupā vampuṉita matulamatu litamampa rāmpara nirālampaṉam paravucā kṣātkāra niravaya vaṅkaṟpa ṉātīta niruvikāram
translation: The liberation from suffering, the attribute-less, the lordship of the universe, the highest of the high, the pure agent of the five cosmic acts, the supreme reality, the playful manifestation of the space of consciousness, the inherent nature of all that is spoken, the sacred, the incomparable, the unequaled, the space beyond space, the unsupported, the praised direct realization, the partless, the one beyond imagination, the unchanging.
commentary: God is the single, pure force behind the five cosmic acts (creation, maintenance, destruction, concealment, and grace). The Divine governs the whole universe and frees us from suffering, yet stays unchanging and free of limiting attributes. Imagination cannot reach it. It is known only through direct spiritual realization.

tamil: பரதுரிய வநுபவம் குருதுரிய பதமம் பகம்பகா தீதவிமலம்
பரமகரு ணாம்பரம் தற்பதம் கனசொற் பதாதீத மின்பவடிவம்
பரோக்ஷஞா னாதீதம் அபரோக்ஷ ஞானானு பவவிலாசப் பிரகாசம்
பாவனா தீதம்கு ணாதீதம் உபசாந்த பதமகா மௌனரூபம்
translit: paraturiya vanupavam kuruturiya patamam pakampakā tītavimalam paramakaru ṇāmparam taṟpatam kaṉacoṟ patātīta miṉpavaṭivam parōkṣañā ṉātītam aparōkṣa ñāṉāṉu pavavilācap pirakācam pāvaṉā tītamku ṇātītam upacānta patamakā mauṉarūpam
translation: The experience of the supreme fourth state, the master's fourth state, the pure one beyond both the divisible and indivisible, the sky of supreme compassion, the ultimate state, the form of bliss beyond weighty words and states, the one beyond indirect knowledge, the radiant play of the experience of direct realization, the one beyond thought, the one beyond attributes, the state of deep peace, the form of great silence.
commentary: The peak of spiritual experience is vast silence and boundless compassion. Vallalar calls it the sky of supreme compassion, a grace that indirect learning and heavy words cannot reach. Only direct realization finds it, and there ordinary thoughts and attributes fall away into a deep, radiant peace.

tamil: பரமபோ தம்போத ரகிதசகி தம்சம்ப வாதீத மப்பிரமேயம்
பகரனந் தானந்தம் அமலமுசி தம்சிற்ப தம்சதா னந்தசாரம்
பரையாதி கிரணாங்க சாங்கசௌ பாங்கவிம் பாகார நிருவிகற்பம்
பரசுகா ரம்பம்ப ரம்பிரம வித்தம்ப ரானந்த புரணபோகம்
translit: paramapō tampōta rakitacaki tamcampa vātīta mappiramēyam pakaraṉan tāṉantam amalamuci tamciṟpa tamcatā ṉantacāram paraiyāti kiraṇāṅka cāṅkacau pāṅkavim pākāra niruvikaṟpam paracukā rampampa rampirama vittampa rāṉanta puraṇapōkam
translation: He is supreme knowledge. He encompasses both the presence and absence of knowledge. He is beyond birth and remains immeasurable. He is inexpressible infinite bliss, immaculate, and perfect. He is the realm of consciousness and the essence of eternal bliss. He takes the undifferentiated form of the supreme energy's radiating light and all its beautiful limbs. He is the origin of supreme joy, the supreme reality, the ultimate seed, and the perfect enjoyment of supreme bliss.
commentary: God is the ultimate intelligence and the essence of perfect joy, beyond the cycle of birth. He holds both our knowing and our not-knowing, and no measure reaches Him. Vallalar sees Him as a radiant, undifferentiated light, the original seed of all spiritual happiness.

tamil: பரிமிதா தீதம்ப ரோதயம் பரகிதம் பரபரீணம் பராந்தம்
பரமாற்பு தம்பரம சேதனம் பசுபாச பாவனம் பரமமோக்ஷம்
பரமானு குணநவா தீதம்சி தாகாச பாஸ்கரம் பரமபோகம்
பரிபாக வேதன வரோதயா னந்தபத பாலனம் பரமயோகம்
translit: parimitā tītampa rōtayam parakitam paraparīṇam parāntam paramāṟpu tamparama cētaṉam pacupāca pāvaṉam paramamōkṣam paramāṉu kuṇanavā tītamci tākāca pāskaram paramapōkam paripāka vētaṉa varōtayā ṉantapata pālaṉam paramayōkam
translation: He is beyond measure. He is the supreme manifestation, the ultimate good, supreme perfection, and the ultimate end. He is the supreme wonder and supreme consciousness. He purifies the soul and its bonds. He is supreme liberation. He embodies supreme qualities and stands beyond the nine principles. He is the sun shining in the sky of consciousness. He is supreme enjoyment. He is supreme yoga, protecting the blissful state that rises as a boon to mature realization.
commentary: Picture the soul's bonds being washed away by pure awareness. That is God at work, shining like a sun in the inner sky of consciousness. When spiritual understanding has fully matured, realization rises as His reward and stands guard over the one who receives it.

tamil: பரமசாத் தியவதீ தானந்த போக்கியம் பரிகதம் பரிவேத்தியம்
பரகேவ லாத்விதா னந்தானு பவசத்த பாதாக்ர சுத்தபலிதம்
பரமசுத் தாத்விதா னந்தவனு பூதிகம் பரிபூத சிற்குணாந்தம்
பரமசித் தாந்தநிக மாந்தசம ரசசுத்த பரமானு பவவிலாசம்
translit: paramacāt tiyavatī tāṉanta pōkkiyam parikatam parivēttiyam parakēva lātvitā ṉantāṉu pavacatta pātākra cuttapalitam paramacut tātvitā ṉantavaṉu pūtikam paripūta ciṟkuṇāntam paramacit tāntanika māntacama racacutta paramāṉu pavavilācam
translation: He is the supreme goal and stands beyond all states. He is the ultimate object of blissful enjoyment, completely comprehended and completely known. He is the pure fruit resting at the summit of the supreme experience of solitary non-dual bliss. He is the realization of supreme, pure, non-dual bliss. He is the thoroughly purified culmination of conscious attributes. He is the pure, supreme play of experience where the ultimate paths of Siddhanta and Vedanta merge in perfect harmony.
commentary: All the traditional paths meet in pure, undivided bliss. Siddhanta (the philosophical path focused on the soul's liberation) and Vedanta (the philosophical path seeking the ultimate reality) find their full resolution at this summit. Vallalar speaks of it as absolute joy, actually lived.

tamil: தரமிகும் சர்வசா திட்டான சத்தியம் சர்வவா னந்தபோகம்
சார்ந்தசர் வாதார சர்வமங் களசர்வ சத்திதர மென்றளவிலாச்
சகுணநிர்க் குணமுறு சலக்ஷண விலக்ஷணத் தன்மைபல வாகநாடித்
தம்மைநிகர் மறையெலா மின்னுமள விடநின்ற சங்கர னநாதியதி
translit: taramikum carvacā tiṭṭāṉa cattiyam carvavā ṉantapōkam cārntacar vātāra carvamaṅ kaḷacarva cattitara meṉṟaḷavilāc cakuṇanirk kuṇamuṟu calakṣaṇa vilakṣaṇat taṉmaipala vākanāṭit tammainikar maṟaiyelā miṉṉumaḷa viṭaniṉṟa caṅkara ṉanātiyati
translation: He is the preeminent foundation of truth for all things. He is the enjoyment of all bliss. He is the boundless support of all existence, the embodiment of all auspiciousness, and the wielder of all powers. The peerless Vedas still strive to measure Him, seeking His nature in countless ways: examining how He assumes form yet remains formless, and how He possesses defining attributes yet transcends them all. He is Shankara, the beginningless one.
commentary: God is the boundless foundation of existence and the source of all power. Even the Vedas, the most revered of the ancient scriptures, keep struggling to define Him. They try without end to explain how He takes on form and qualities while staying formless and beyond every attribute.

tamil: சாமகீ தப்பிரியன் மணிகண்ட சீகண்ட சசிகண்ட சாமகண்ட
சயசய வெனுந்தொண்ட ரிதயமலர் மேவிய சடாமகுடன் மதனதகனன்
சந்திரசே கரனிடப வாகனன் கங்கா தரன்சூல பாணியிறைவன்
தனிமுத லுமாபதி புராந்தகன் பசுபதி சயம்புமா தேவனமலன்
translit: cāmakī tappiriyaṉ maṇikaṇṭa cīkaṇṭa cacikaṇṭa cāmakaṇṭa cayacaya veṉuntoṇṭa ritayamalar mēviya caṭāmakuṭaṉ mataṉatakaṉaṉ cantiracē karaṉiṭapa vākaṉaṉ kaṅkā taraṉcūla pāṇiyiṟaivaṉ taṉimuta lumāpati purāntakaṉ pacupati cayampumā tēvaṉamalaṉ
translation: He loves the songs of the Sama Veda. His neck shines like a jewel, He possesses an auspicious throat, and He bears a dark neck. He wears the crescent moon. He dwells in the blossoming hearts of devotees who chant "Victory, victory." He wears a crown of matted hair. He burned the god of love to ashes. He is crested with the moon. He rides the bull. He bears the river Ganges and holds the trident in His hand. He is the Lord, the peerless origin, the Lord of Uma, the destroyer of the three cities, the Lord of souls, the self-existent one, the Great God, and the immaculate one.
commentary: Vallalar now turns to the familiar images of Lord Siva: the crescent moon, the crown of matted hair, the trident, the Ganges, the bull. Beneath these mythological symbols lies a simple truth about devotion. The supreme Lord chooses to live in the blossoming hearts of those who chant His name with genuine love.

tamil: தன்னிகரில் சித்தெலாம் வல்லவன் வடதிசைச் சைலமெனு மொருவில்வன்
தக்ஷிணா மூர்த்தியருண் மூர்த்திபுண் ணியமூர்த்தி தகுமட்ட மூர்த்தியானோன்
தலைமைபெறு கணநாய கன்குழக னழகன்மெய்ச் சாமிநந் தேவதேவன்
translit: tāṇṭavaṉ talaimālai pūṇṭavaṉ toḻumaṉpar taṅkaḷukkaruḷāṇṭavaṉ taṉṉikaril cittelām vallavaṉ vaṭaticaic cailameṉu moruvilvaṉ takṣiṇā mūrttiyaruṇ mūrttipuṇ ṇiyamūrtti takumaṭṭa mūrttiyāṉōṉ talaimaipeṟu kaṇanāya kaṉkuḻaka ṉaḻakaṉmeyc cāminan tēvatēvaṉ
translation: He is the Dancer who wears a garland of skulls. He is the Lord of grace who rules over His worshipful devotees. He is capable of all incomparable miracles. He holds the northern mountain as His matchless bow. He is Dakshinamurthy, the form of grace, the form of virtue, and the one who assumed the eight fitting forms. He is the preeminent Lord of the hosts, the youthful one, the beautiful one, the true Lord, and our God of Gods.
commentary: The classic Siva of Tamil devotion gathers in these lines. He is the cosmic dancer wearing skulls, the universal teacher known as Dakshinamurthy, the master of miracles. Every one of these forms points to a presence overwhelmingly powerful and still full of grace for those who worship Him.

tamil: சம்புவே தண்டன் பிறப்பிலான் முடிவிலான் தாணுமுக் கண்களுடையான்
சதுரன் கடாசல வுரிப்போர்வை யான்செந் தழற்கரத் தேந்திநின்றோன்
சர்வகா ரணன்விறற் காலகா லன்சர்வ சம்பிரமன் சர்வேச்சுரன்
தகைகொள்பர மேச்சுரன் சிவபிரா னெம்பிரான் தம்பிரான் செம்பொற்பதம்
translit: campuvē taṇṭaṉ piṟappilāṉ muṭivilāṉ tāṇumuk kaṇkaḷuṭaiyāṉ caturaṉ kaṭācala vurippōrvai yāṉcen taḻaṟkarat tēntiniṉṟōṉ carvakā raṇaṉviṟaṟ kālakā laṉcarva campiramaṉ carvēccuraṉ takaikoḷpara mēccuraṉ civapirā ṉempirāṉ tampirāṉ cempoṟpatam
translation: He is Shambu, the supreme authority, without birth and without end. He is the firm one with three eyes. He is the skillful one whose cloak is the skin of a mountain-like elephant. He stands holding red fire in His hand. He is the cause of all, the mighty conqueror of death, the all-bewitching one, the Lord of all, the worthy Parameshwara, Lord Siva, our Lord, and the supreme master. These are His pure golden feet.
commentary: God triumphs over death and masters the physical world. Holding fire and wrapped in an elephant's skin, He stands for the destruction of ignorance and ego. Then the lines bring our eyes down to the great symbol of refuge in Tamil poetry, the golden feet of the Lord.

tamil: தகவுபெறு நிட்பேத நிட்கம்ப மாம்பரா சத்திவடி வாம்பொற்பதம்
தக்கநிட் காடின்ய சம்வேத நாங்கசிற் சத்திவடி வாம்பொற்பதம்
சாற்றரிய விச்சைஞா னங்கிரியை யென்னுமுச் சத்திவடி வாம்பொற்பதம்
தடையிலா நிர்விடய சிற்குண சிவாநந்த சத்திவடி வாம்பொற்பதம்
translit: takavupeṟu niṭpēta niṭkampa māmparā cattivaṭi vāmpoṟpatam takkaniṭ kāṭiṉya camvēta nāṅkaciṟ cattivaṭi vāmpoṟpatam cāṟṟariya viccaiñā ṉaṅkiriyai yeṉṉumuc cattivaṭi vāmpoṟpatam taṭaiyilā nirviṭaya ciṟkuṇa civānanta cattivaṭi vāmpoṟpatam
translation: These golden feet are the form of the supreme energy, characterized by worthy non-differentiation and absolute stillness. These golden feet are the form of the conscious energy, possessing the limbs of fitting softness and perfect awareness. These golden feet are the form of the three indescribable energies of will, knowledge, and action. These golden feet are the form of the unobstructed energy of divine bliss, possessing a consciousness detached from sense objects.
commentary: In Tamil spiritual poetry the feet of God are never just limbs. They stand for the active, reaching power of the divine in the world, known as Sakti. Vallalar names them as the very energies of divine will, total awareness and absolute stillness. Through them everything is known, all action begins, and joy without limit is given.

tamil: தகுவிந்தை மோகினியை மானையசை விக்குமொரு சத்திவடி வாம்பொற்பதம்
தாழ்விலீ சானமுதன் மூர்த்திவரை யைஞ்சத்தி தஞ்சத்தி யாம்பொற்பதம்
சவிகற்ப நிருவிகற் பம்பெறு மனந்தமா சத்திசத் தாம்பொற்பதம்
தடநிருப வவிவர்த்த சாமர்த்திய திருவருட் சத்தியுரு வாம்பொற்பதம்
translit: takuvintai mōkiṉiyai māṉaiyacai vikkumoru cattivaṭi vāmpoṟpatam tāḻvilī cāṉamutaṉ mūrttivarai yaiñcatti tañcatti yāmpoṟpatam cavikaṟpa niruvikaṟ pampeṟu maṉantamā catticat tāmpoṟpatam taṭanirupa vavivartta cāmarttiya tiruvaruṭ cattiyuru vāmpoṟpatam
translation: These golden feet are the form of the unique energy that activates the fitting Bindu, Mohini, and Maya. These golden feet are the refuge for the five powers from the flawless Ishana down to the other forms. These golden feet are the essence of endless great powers encompassing both differentiated and undifferentiated states. These golden feet are the form of the holy power of grace, capable of immense and peerless manifestation.
commentary: Every movement and act of creation in the universe starts from these divine feet. Bindu, Mohini, and Maya are traditional terms for the subtle energetic matter that makes up the cosmos. God's energy breathes life into these layers, holding up everything from the highest spiritual forces to the everyday physical world.

tamil: தவாதசாந் தப்பதந் துவாதசாந் தப்பதந் தருமிணை மலர்ப்பூம்பதம்
சகலர்விஞ் ஞானகலர் பிரளயா கலரிதய சாக்ஷியா கியபூம்பதம்
தணிவிலா அணுபக்ஷ சம்புப க்ஷங்களிற் சமரச முறும்பூம்பதம்
தருபரஞ் சூக்குமந் தூலமிவை நிலவிய தமக்குளுயி ராம்பூம்பதம்
translit: tavātacān tappatan tuvātacān tappatan tarumiṇai malarppūmpatam cakalarviñ ñāṉakalar piraḷayā kalaritaya cākṣiyā kiyapūmpatam taṇivilā aṇupakṣa campupa kṣaṅkaḷiṟ camaraca muṟumpūmpatam taruparañ cūkkuman tūlamivai nilaviya tamakkuḷuyi rāmpūmpatam
translation: These twin flowery feet grant endless tranquility and the state of the twelfth center. These flowery feet serve as the heart's witness for the Sakalar, Vijnanakalar, and Pralayakalar souls. These flowery feet attain perfect harmony between the unceasing perspectives of the soul and God. These flowery feet are the very life within the established supreme, subtle, and gross realms.
commentary: The twelfth center is a high state of realization reached in deep meditation. From there the divine presence is the inner witness for every stage the soul passes through. Traditional philosophy groups souls into three states by their spiritual limitations: the Sakalar who are bound by everyday worldliness, the Vijnanakalar who are bound only by ego, and the Pralayakalar who are caught in the illusion of action. By grace the distance between the individual soul and God dissolves into perfect harmony.

tamil: சரவசர வபரிமித விவிதவான் மப்பகுதி தாங்குந் திருப்பூம்பதம்
தண்டபிண் டாண்டவகி லாண்டபிர மாண்டந் தடிக்கவரு ளும்பூம்பதம்
தத்வதாத் விகசகசி ருட்டிதிதி சங்கார சகலகர்த் துருபூம்பதம்
சகசமல விருளகல நின்மலசு யம்ப்ரகா சங்குலவு நற்பூம்பதம்
translit: caravacara vaparimita vivitavāṉ mappakuti tāṅkun tiruppūmpatam taṇṭapiṇ ṭāṇṭavaki lāṇṭapira māṇṭan taṭikkavaru ḷumpūmpatam tatvatāt vikacakaci ruṭṭititi caṅkāra cakalakart turupūmpatam cakacamala viruḷakala niṉmalacu yamprakā caṅkulavu naṟpūmpatam
translation: The divine, beautiful flower-like feet support the boundless, diverse multitudes of moving and unmoving souls. The beautiful feet graciously cause the bodies, the worlds, the cosmic spheres, and the universes to thrive. The beautiful feet act as the absolute agent driving creation, maintenance, and destruction for the worlds, the principles, and their derivatives. The beautiful, good feet shine with pure, self-luminous radiance to dispel the darkness of innate impurities.
commentary: Every living being and the whole physical universe rests on these feet. They are the pure light, shining by itself, that drives creation, maintenance and destruction. Only this light can clear away the soul's deep-rooted ignorance.

tamil: மரபுறு மதாதீத வெளிநடுவி லானந்த மாநடன மிடுபூம்பதம்
மன்னும்வினை யொப்புமல பரிபாகம் வாய்க்கமா மாயையை மிதிக்கும்பதம்
வளரூர்த்த வீரதாண் டவமுதற் பஞ்சக மகிழ்ந்திட வியற்றும்பதம்
translit: marapuṟu matātīta veḷinaṭuvi lāṉanta mānaṭaṉa miṭupūmpatam maṉṉumviṉai yoppumala paripākam vāykkamā māyaiyai mitikkumpatam malipiṟavi maṟaliyi ṉaḻuntumuyir tamaiyaruḷiṉ maruvuṟaveṭukkumpatam vaḷarūrtta vīratāṇ ṭavamutaṟ pañcaka makiḻntiṭa viyaṟṟumpatam
translation: The beautiful feet perform the great dance of bliss in the center of the transcendent space beyond traditional religions. The feet trample the great Maya to bring about the balancing of karma and the maturation of impurities. The feet graciously lift up the souls sinking in abundant births and the grasp of the god of death, drawing them into union. The feet joyfully perform the five cosmic dances, beginning with the lofty Urdhva and Vira tandavas.
commentary: The true divine experience unfolds in a boundless space entirely beyond the grasp of traditional religions. There the Lord's foot crushes Maya (the illusion that blinds the soul) and untangles karma (the cycle of our actions and their consequences). Once those bonds break, grace lifts the soul out of endless birth and death and draws it into joyful union.

tamil: வல்லமுய லகன்மீதி னூன்றிய திருப்பதம் வளந்தரத் தூக்கும்பதம்
வல்வினையெ லாந்தவிர்த் தழியாத சுத்தநிலை வாய்த்திட வழங்கும்பதம்
மறைதுதிக் கும்பதம் மறைச்சிலம் பொளிர்பதம் மறைப்பாது கைச்செம்பதம்
மறைமுடி மணிப்பதம் மறைக்குமெட் டாப்பதம் மறைப்பரி யுகைக்கும்பதம்
translit: vallamuya lakaṉmīti ṉūṉṟiya tiruppatam vaḷantarat tūkkumpatam valviṉaiye lāntavirt taḻiyāta cuttanilai vāyttiṭa vaḻaṅkumpatam maṟaitutik kumpatam maṟaiccilam poḷirpatam maṟaippātu kaiccempatam maṟaimuṭi maṇippatam maṟaikkumeṭ ṭāppatam maṟaippari yukaikkumpatam
translation: The divine foot stands firmly on the mighty demon Muyalakan. The raised foot bestows boundless prosperity. The feet dispel all harsh karmas and grant the indestructible pure state. The feet receive the praises of the Vedas. The feet shine with the anklets of the Vedas. The red feet wear the Vedas as sandals. The feet shine as the crowning jewel of the Vedas. The feet remain unreachable even by the Vedas. The feet ride the Vedas as a steed.
commentary: Muyalakan is a mythological demon who stands for human arrogance and ignorance. The planted foot crushes that ego, and the raised foot grants liberation. Vallalar makes the Vedas (the ancient sacred scriptures of India) into the Lord's sandals, anklets and steed. The ultimate truth remains completely unreachable by these traditional texts.

tamil: மறையவ னுளங்கொண்ட பதமமித கோடியா மறையவர் சிரஞ்சூழ்பதம்
மறையவன் சிரசிகா மணியெனும் பதம்மலர்கொண் மறையவன் வாழ்த்தும்பதம்
மறையவன் செயவுலக மாக்கின்ற வதிகார வாழ்வையீந் தருளும்பதம்
மறையவன் கனவினுங் காணாத பதமந்த மறையவன் பரவும்பதம்
translit: maṟaiyava ṉuḷaṅkoṇṭa patamamita kōṭiyā maṟaiyavar cirañcūḻpatam maṟaiyavaṉ ciracikā maṇiyeṉum patammalarkoṇ maṟaiyavaṉ vāḻttumpatam maṟaiyavaṉ ceyavulaka mākkiṉṟa vatikāra vāḻvaiyīn taruḷumpatam maṟaiyavaṉ kaṉaviṉuṅ kāṇāta patamanta maṟaiyavaṉ paravumpatam
translation: The creator god Brahma holds these feet in his heart. The heads of countless crores of Vedic sages surround these feet. These feet shine as the crest-jewel on Brahma's head. Brahma offers flowers and praises these feet. These feet graciously grant Brahma the sovereign life and authority to create the worlds. Brahma cannot see these feet even in his dreams. That very Brahma worships these feet.
commentary: Brahma, the traditional Hindu god of creation, gets his whole authority to make the worlds from these feet. He wears them as the jewel on his head and praises them with flowers. Still he cannot see them, even in a dream.

tamil: மால்விடை யிவர்ந்திடு மலர்ப்பதந் தெய்வநெடு மாலருச் சிக்கும்பதம்
மால்பரவி நாடொறும் வணங்குபத மிக்கதிரு மால்விழியி லங்கும்பதம்
மால்தேட நின்றபத மோரனந் தங்கோடி மாற்றலை யலங்கற்பதம்
மான்முடிப் பதநெடிய மாலுளப் பதமந்த மாலுமறி வரிதாம்பதம்
translit: mālviṭai yivarntiṭu malarppatan teyvaneṭu mālaruc cikkumpatam mālparavi nāṭoṟum vaṇaṅkupata mikkatiru mālviḻiyi laṅkumpatam māltēṭa niṉṟapata mōraṉan taṅkōṭi māṟṟalai yalaṅkaṟpatam māṉmuṭip pataneṭiya māluḷap patamanta mālumaṟi varitāmpatam
translation: The flower-like feet mount the great bull. The divine Lord Vishnu worships these feet. Vishnu praises and bows to these feet every day. These feet shine with the eye of great Vishnu offered as a flower. These feet stood firm while Vishnu searched for them. These feet wear a garland made of endless crores of Vishnu's heads. These feet rest upon Vishnu's crown. These feet dwell in Vishnu's heart. These feet remain exceedingly difficult for even that Vishnu to know.
commentary: Vishnu, revered as the preserver of the universe, worships these feet so completely that he once offered his own eye as a flower. Like Brahma, he keeps them in his heart. And like Brahma, he cannot take in how vast they are.

tamil: மால்கொளவ தாரங்கள் பத்தினும் வழிபட்டு வாய்மைபெற நிற்கும்பதம்
மாலுலகு காக்கின்ற வண்மைபெற் றடிமையின் வதிந்திட வளிக்கும்பதம்
வரையுறு முருத்திரர்கள் புகழ்பதம் பலகோடி வயவுருத் திரர்சூழ்பதம்
வாய்ந்திடு முருத்திரற் கியல்கொண்முத் தொழில்செய்யும் வண்மைதந் தருளும்பதம்
translit: mālkoḷava tāraṅkaḷ pattiṉum vaḻipaṭṭu vāymaipeṟa niṟkumpatam mālulaku kākkiṉṟa vaṇmaipeṟ ṟaṭimaiyiṉ vatintiṭa vaḷikkumpatam varaiyuṟu muruttirarkaḷ pukaḻpatam palakōṭi vayavurut tirarcūḻpatam vāyntiṭu muruttiraṟ kiyalkoṇmut toḻilceyyum vaṇmaitan taruḷumpatam
translation: The foot that Thirumal worships in all his ten avatars to attain the state of truth. The foot that grants Thirumal the power to protect the world, allowing him to remain a devoted servant. The foot praised by the exalted Rudras and surrounded by crores of powerful Rudras. The foot that bestows the natural power upon the fitting Rudra to perform the three cosmic acts.
commentary: Thirumal (Vishnu) and the Rudras protect and transform the universe, yet none of that power is their own. All of it comes from these feet, the grace that is the source of every cosmic power.

tamil: வானவிந் திரராதி யெண்டிசைக் காவலர்கண் மாதவத் திறனாம்பதம்
மதியிரவி யாதிசுர ரசுரரந் தரர்வான வாசிகள் வழுத்தும்பதம்
மணியுரகர் கருடர்காந் தருவர்விஞ் சையர்சித்தர் மாமுனிவ ரேத்தும்பதம்
மாநிருதர் பைசாசர் கிம்புருடர் யக்ஷர்கள் மதித்துவர மேற்கும்பதம்
translit: vāṉavin tirarāti yeṇṭicaik kāvalarkaṇ mātavat tiṟaṉāmpatam matiyiravi yāticura racuraran tararvāṉa vācikaḷ vaḻuttumpatam maṇiyurakar karuṭarkān taruvarviñ caiyarcittar māmuṉiva rēttumpatam mānirutar paicācar kimpuruṭar yakṣarkaḷ matittuvara mēṟkumpatam
translation: The foot that embodies the great ascetic power of the celestial Indra and the guardians of the eight directions. The foot worshipped by the moon, the sun, the celestial beings, the demons, the beings of the middle realms, and the dwellers of the heavens. The foot praised by the gem-bearing serpents, the Garudas, the Gandharvas, the Vidyadharas, the Siddhars, and the great sages. The foot revered by the great Niruthars, the Pisachas, the Kimpurushas, and the Yakshas to receive boons.
commentary: Gods, celestial kings, sages, nature spirits, even demons: every class of being in the old cosmos bows to the same foot to find its strength.

tamil: மன்னுகின் னரர்பூதர் வித்தியா தரர்போகர் மற்றையர்கள் பற்றும்பதம்
மாதேவி யெங்கள்மலை மங்கையென் னம்மைமென் மலர்க்கையால் வருடும்பதம்
மறலியை யுதைத்தருள் கழற்பத மரக்கனை மலைக்கீ ழடர்க்கும்பதம்
translit: maṉṉukiṉ ṉararpūtar vittiyā tararpōkar maṟṟaiyarkaḷ paṟṟumpatam vaṇmaipeṟu nantimutal civakaṇat talaivarkaṇ maṉakkōyilvāḻumpatam mātēvi yeṅkaḷmalai maṅkaiyeṉ ṉammaimeṉ malarkkaiyāl varuṭumpatam maṟaliyai yutaittaruḷ kaḻaṟpata marakkaṉai malaikkī ḻaṭarkkumpatam
translation: The foot grasped by the eternal Kinnaras, the Bhutas, the Vidyadharas, the Bhogas, and all others. The foot that resides in the heart-temple of the leaders of Siva's hosts, starting with the munificent Nandi. The foot gently stroked by the soft, flower-like hands of the Great Goddess, our Lady of the Mountain, my Mother. The anklet-adorned foot that kicked the god of death to bestow grace and crushed the demon beneath the mountain.
commentary: The Divine Mother strokes this foot with her soft hands, and it lives quietly in the heart-temples of Nandi and Siva's hosts. The same foot kicked away death and pressed the arrogant demon under the mountain. Grace is that tender, and that fierce.

tamil: வஞ்சமறு நெஞ்சினிடை யெஞ்சலற விஞ்சுதிறன் மஞ்சுற விளங்கும்பதம்
வந்தனைசெய் புந்தியவர் தந்துயர் தவிர்ந்திடவுண் மந்தணந விற்றும்பதம்
மாறிலொரு மாறனுள மீறின்மகிழ் வீறியிட மாறிநட மாடும்பதம்
translit: vañcamaṟu neñciṉiṭai yeñcalaṟa viñcutiṟaṉ mañcuṟa viḷaṅkumpatam vantaṉaicey puntiyavar tantuyar tavirntiṭavuṇ mantaṇana viṟṟumpatam māṟiloru māṟaṉuḷa mīṟiṉmakiḻ vīṟiyiṭa māṟinaṭa māṭumpatam maṟakkaruṇai yuntaṉi yaṟakkaruṇai yuntantuvaḻvikkumoṇmaippatam
translation: The foot that shines with boundless power like a radiant cloud in hearts free of deceit. The foot that reveals the inner secret to devoted minds and dispels their sorrows. The foot that danced by switching legs to make the supreme joy of the incomparable Pandyan king flourish. The brilliant foot that grants both fierce grace and unique gentle grace to uplift souls.
commentary: Hearts free of deceit are where God reveals the inner secret. Tradition says the Lord once switched his dancing leg simply because a devoted Pandyan king worried the dancer would grow tired. That is how He answers pure love, with gentle blessing and with fierce correction, whichever lifts the soul.

tamil: இரவுறும் பகலடிய ரிருமருங் கினுமுறுவ ரெனவயங் கியசீர்ப்பதம்
translit: iravuṟum pakalaṭiya rirumaruṅ kiṉumuṟuva reṉavayaṅ kiyacīrppatam empanta maṟavematu campantavaḷḷaṉmoḻi yiyaṉmaṇa maṇakkumpatam īvaraca remmuṭaiya nāvaracarcoṟpatika vicaipari maḷikkumpatam ēvalār pukaḻematu nāvalārūrarpuka licaitirup pāṭṭuppatam
translation: The glorious foot that shines with devotees gathered on both sides day and night. The foot fragrant with the natural scent of the words of our munificent Sambandar to sever our worldly bonds. The foot that exudes the musical fragrance of the verses sung by our Appar, the king of givers. The foot that resounds with the music of the sacred songs composed by our Sundarar, who is praised by devoted servants.
commentary: The songs of the great Tamil saints Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar hang around these feet like a fragrance that never fades. Their devotion has soaked into the divine presence itself.

tamil: எல்லூரு மணிமாட நல்லூரி னப்பர்முடி யிடைவைகி யருண்மென்பதம்
எடுமேலெ னத்தொண்டர் முடிமேன் மறுத்திடவு மிடைவலிந் தேறும்பதம்
எழில்பரவை யிசையவா ரூர்மறுகி னருள்கொண்டி ராமுழுது முலவும்பதம்
translit: ētavūr taṅkāta vātavūreṅkōvi ṉiṉcoṉmaṇi yaṇiyumpatam ellūru maṇimāṭa nallūri ṉapparmuṭi yiṭaivaiki yaruṇmeṉpatam eṭumēle ṉattoṇṭar muṭimēṉ maṟuttiṭavu miṭaivalin tēṟumpatam eḻilparavai yicaiyavā rūrmaṟuki ṉaruḷkoṇṭi rāmuḻutu mulavumpatam
translation: These are the feet adorned by the sweet, jewel-like words of our king of Vadavur, who remains untainted by this sorrowful world. These are the soft, graceful feet that rested on the head of Appar in Nallur with its radiant gem-studded mansions. These are the feet that lovingly press onto the heads of devotees even when they protest out of humility. These are the feet that walked all night with grace through the streets of Tiruvarur to please the beautiful Paravai.
commentary: Vallalar recalls the saints to show how close God comes to those who love Him. He wore the poems of Manikkavasagar (the king of Vadavur) as jewels and set His feet on Appar's head to bless him. When devotees protested that they were unworthy, He pressed His feet on them anyway. For a devotee He even walked the streets all night as a messenger of love. The divine serves pure devotion.

tamil: இன்தொண்டர் பசியறக் கச்சூரின் மனைதொறு மிரக்கநடை கொள்ளும்பதம்
இளைப்புற லறிந்தன்பர் பொதிசோ றருந்தமு னிருந்துபி னடக்கும்பதம்
எறிவிறகு விற்கவளர் கூடற் றெருத்தொறு மியங்கிய விரக்கப்பதம்
இறுவைகை யங்கரையின் மண்படப் பல்கா லெழுந்துவிளை யாடும்பதம்
translit: iṉtoṇṭar paciyaṟak kaccūriṉ maṉaitoṟu mirakkanaṭai koḷḷumpatam iḷaippuṟa laṟintaṉpar poticō ṟaruntamu ṉiruntupi ṉaṭakkumpatam eṟiviṟaku viṟkavaḷar kūṭaṟ ṟeruttoṟu miyaṅkiya virakkappatam iṟuvaikai yaṅkaraiyiṉ maṇpaṭap palkā leḻuntuviḷai yāṭumpatam
translation: These are the feet that walked begging from house to house in Kacchur to appease the hunger of the sweet devotee. These are the feet that, knowing the devotee's weariness, waited for him to eat the packed rice and walked behind him. These are the compassionate feet that walked through every street of great Madurai to sell chopped firewood. These are the feet that joyously played on the banks of the Vaigai river, stepping on the mud again and again.
commentary: More stories of the saints, and every one of them brings God down into ordinary hardship. He begged from house to house to feed a hungry devotee. He sold firewood in the streets of Madurai and played in the mud of the Vaigai. No task was too humble when it meant caring for His own.

tamil: எங்கேமெய் யன்பருள ரங்கே நலந்தர வெழுந்தருளும் வண்மைப்பதம்
எவ்வண்ணம் வேண்டுகினு மவ்வண்ண மன்றே யிரங்கியீந் தருளும்பதம்
என்போன்ற வர்க்குமிகு பொன்போன்ற கருணைதந் திதயத் திருக்கும்பதம்
என்னுயிரை யன்னபத மென்னுயிர்க் குயிரா யிலங்குசெம் பதுமப்பதம்
translit: eṅkēmey yaṉparuḷa raṅkē nalantara veḻuntaruḷum vaṇmaippatam evvaṇṇam vēṇṭukiṉu mavvaṇṇa maṉṟē yiraṅkiyīn taruḷumpatam eṉpōṉṟa varkkumiku poṉpōṉṟa karuṇaitan titayat tirukkumpatam eṉṉuyirai yaṉṉapata meṉṉuyirk kuyirā yilaṅkucem patumappatam
translation: These are the generous feet that gracefully manifest to bestow goodness wherever true devotees exist. These are the compassionate feet that immediately grant boons exactly as requested. These are the feet that grant immense golden compassion even to someone like me and dwell within my heart. These are the shining red lotus feet that are my life and shine as the very life of my life.
commentary: Now Vallalar turns from the old saints to himself. God answers at once, exactly as asked, and gives His compassion even to someone like him. He feels that presence living in his own heart, as the very life of his life.

tamil: என்னறிவெ னும்பதமெ னறிவினுக் கறிவா யிருந்தசெங் கமலப்பதம்
என்னன்பெ னும்பதமெ னன்பிற்கு வித்தா யிசைந்தகோ கனகப்பதம்
என்தவ மெனும்பதமென் மெய்த்தவப் பயனா யியைந்தசெஞ் சலசப்பதம்
என்னிருகண் மணியான பதமென்கண் மணிகளுக் கினியநல் விருந்தாம்பதம்
translit: eṉṉaṟive ṉumpatame ṉaṟiviṉuk kaṟivā yiruntaceṅ kamalappatam eṉṉaṉpe ṉumpatame ṉaṉpiṟku vittā yicaintakō kaṉakappatam eṉtava meṉumpatameṉ meyttavap payaṉā yiyaintaceñ calacappatam eṉṉirukaṇ maṇiyāṉa patameṉkaṇ maṇikaḷuk kiṉiyanal viruntāmpatam
translation: These are the red lotus feet that are my knowledge and serve as the knowledge of my knowledge. These are the lotus feet that are my love and serve as the seed of my love. These are the red lotus feet that are my penance and serve as the true fruit of my penance. These are the feet that are the pupils of my two eyes and serve as a sweet, fine feast for my eyes.
commentary: Vallalar traces every part of his inner life back to these feet. They are the knowing behind his knowledge and the seed his love grows from. His penance is theirs, and so is its fruit.

tamil: என்செல்வ மாம்பதமென் மெய்ச்செல்வ வருவாயெ னுந்தாம ரைப்பொற்பதம்
என்பெரிய வாழ்வான பதமென்க ளிப்பா மிரும்பதமெ னிதியாம்பதம்
என்தந்தை தாயெனு மிணைப்பதமெ னுறவா மியற்பதமெ னட்பாம்பதம்
என்குருவெ னும்பதமெ னிட்டதெய் வப்பத மெனதுகுல தெய்வப்பதம்
translit: eṉcelva māmpatameṉ meyccelva varuvāye ṉuntāma raippoṟpatam eṉperiya vāḻvāṉa patameṉka ḷippā mirumpatame ṉitiyāmpatam eṉtantai tāyeṉu miṇaippatame ṉuṟavā miyaṟpatame ṉaṭpāmpatam eṉkuruve ṉumpatame ṉiṭṭatey vappata meṉatukula teyvappatam
translation: These are the golden lotus feet that are my wealth and the source of my true wealth. These are the great feet that are my magnificent life, my boundless joy, and my eternal treasure. These are the pair of feet that are my father and mother, my natural kin, and my true friends. These are the feet that are my Guru, my chosen deity, and my family deity.
commentary: Wealth, joy, security, family, friends, teacher: for Vallalar the Lord's feet take the place of all of them. He needs no money or earthly ties when father, mother and Guru are already found in God.

tamil: என்பொறிக ளுக்கெலா நல்விடய மாம்பதமெ னெழுமையும் விடாப்பொற்பதம்
எல்லார்க்கு நல்லபத மெல்லாஞ்செய் வல்லபத மிணையிலாத் துணையாம்பதம்
எழுமனமு டைந்துடைந் துருகிநெகிழ் பத்தர்கட் கின்னமுத மாகும்பதம்
translit: eṉpoṟika ḷukkelā nalviṭaya māmpatame ṉeḻumaiyum viṭāppoṟpatam eṉkuṟaiye lāntavirt tāṭkoṇṭa patameṉak keyppilvaippākumpatam ellārkku nallapata mellāñcey vallapata miṇaiyilāt tuṇaiyāmpatam eḻumaṉamu ṭaintuṭain turukinekiḻ pattarkaṭ kiṉṉamuta mākumpatam
translation: These feet are the perfect object for all my senses. They are the golden feet that never leave me across my seven births. They are the feet that removed all my flaws and claimed me. They serve as my hidden treasure in times of exhaustion. They are the feet that are good to everyone. They are the feet capable of doing all things. They are an unparalleled companion. They are the feet that become sweet ambrosia to devotees whose rising minds break, melt, and soften.
commentary: Every sense finds what it was made for in these feet, and they stay with Vallalar through all seven births. When the soul is spent, they are the strength kept in reserve. To a heart that breaks and melts in devotion, they taste like sweet ambrosia.

tamil: எண்ணுறிற் பாலினறு நெய்யொடு சருக்கரை யிசைந்தென வினிக்கும்பதம்
ஏற்றமுக் கனிபாகு கன்னல்கற் கண்டுதே னென்னமது ரிக்கும்பதம்
எங்கள்பத மெங்கள்பத மென்றுசம யத்தேவ ரிசைவழக் கிடுநற்பதம்
ஈறிலாப் பதமெலாந் தருதிருப் பதமழிவி லின்புதவு கின்றபதமே.
translit: eṇṇuṟiṟ pāliṉaṟu neyyoṭu carukkarai yicainteṉa viṉikkumpatam ēṟṟamuk kaṉipāku kaṉṉalkaṟ kaṇṭutē ṉeṉṉamatu rikkumpatam eṅkaḷpata meṅkaḷpata meṉṟucama yattēva ricaivaḻak kiṭunaṟpatam īṟilāp patamelān tarutirup patamaḻivi liṉputavu kiṉṟapatamē.
translation: When thought of, these feet taste sweet like a mixture of milk, fragrant ghee, and sugar. They bring a sweetness like the supreme three fruits, jaggery syrup, sugarcane, rock candy, and honey. They are the good feet over which the gods of various religions argue, claiming, "They are our feet, they are our feet." They are the sacred feet that grant all endless realms. They are the feet that bestow imperishable bliss.
commentary: Spiritual joy is experienced as a rich, physical sweetness combining milk, honey, and fruit. The gods of various religions bicker over this ultimate divine presence, each trying to claim it exclusively as their own. The true divine reality stands above these disputes to offer imperishable bliss.

note: Editor's note: after the opening invocation, this petition walks through the Siva temples of the Tamil land region by region, as the 1896 edition marks them. Couplets 2 to 65 are in the Chola country north of the Kaveri, 66 to 192 south of it. Couplets 193 and 194 are in Eelam (Sri Lanka), 195 to 207 in the Pandya country, 208 in the hill country (Malai Nadu), 209 to 215 in the Kongu country, 216 to 237 in the middle country (Nadu Nadu), 238 to 272 in the Thondai country, 273 in the Tulu country and 274 to 280 in the North. The petition itself follows.
translit: avvav viṭaivan takaṟṟi aruḷtaralāl evvev viṭaiyūṟum eytalilam - tevvartamaik kaṉṟumata māmukamuṅ kaṇmūṉṟuṅ koṇṭirunta toṉṟatunam muḷḷa muṟaintu.
translation: The One possessing three eyes and the great face of a rutting elephant that crushes enemies resides in our heart. By coming at every juncture to remove obstacles and bestow grace, that One ensures we face no impediments of any kind.
commentary: Vinayakar, the elephant-faced deity, is traditionally honored at the start of any undertaking because he clears away obstacles. Vallalar places him right inside the human heart. From there his grace steps in at every moment and clears the path of every difficulty.

translit: coṟpeṟumeyñ ñāṉac cuyañcōti yāntillaic ciṟcapaiyil vāḻtalaimait teyvamē - naṟcivaiyān
translation: O supreme Deity living in the hall of wisdom in Thillai as the self-luminous Jothi of true knowledge praised by words!
commentary: The petition opens by addressing the supreme Deity in Thillai, the sacred temple town of Chidambaram. In the hall of wisdom, God shines as a self-luminous light of pure, true knowledge.

translit: tāyi ṉulakaṉaittun tāṅkun tiruppuliyūrk kōyi lamarntakuṇak kuṉṟamē - māyamikum
translation: O mountain of virtues seated in the temple of Thiruppuliyur, bearing all the worlds like the good mother Sivai!
commentary: At Thiruppuliyur God is a towering mountain of good qualities. Vallalar likens this grace to a loving mother who holds up and cares for all the worlds.

translit: vāṭkaḷamuṟ ṟāṅkuviḻi mātarmaya laṟṟavarcūḻ vēṭkaḷamuṟ ṟōṅkum viḻupporuḷē - vāḻkkaimaṉai
translation: O supreme Reality reigning high in Vetkalam, surrounded by those freed from the delusion of women with sword-like eyes!
commentary: At the shrine of Vetkalam the supreme Reality stands surrounded by dedicated seekers. They have freed themselves entirely from worldly distraction and the illusions of physical desire.

translit: nalvāyi leṅku navamaṇikkuṉ ṟōṅkutiru nelvāyi ṉiṉṟoḷiru nīḷoḷiyē - celvāyt
translation: O vast Light shining in holy Nelvayil, where mountains of nine gems rise at every good entrance of the dwellings!
commentary: Next comes the holy town of Nelvayil. God is felt here as an endless, vast light over a place of great spiritual and material wealth.

translit: teḻippālai vēlait tiraiyolipō lārkkuṅ kaḻippālai yiṉpak kaḷippē - viḻippālaṉ
translation: O blissful ecstasy of Kazhippalai, resounding like the roar of the ocean waves. O Lord with the supreme eye,
commentary: At Kazhippalai the presence of God brings a joy so intense it sounds like the ocean's waves roaring without pause. Vallalar also calls Him the Lord with the supreme eye, meaning the inner eye of divine wisdom.

translit: kallūrp perumaṇattaik kaṭṭuraikkac cōtitaru nallūrp perumaṇamvāḻ naṉṉilaiyē - collun
translation: O beautiful state residing in Nallur Perumanam, radiating light to proclaim the great union of Kallur. Praised in words,
commentary: The light at the sacred town of Nallur Perumanam reveals the highest state of spiritual union. Its brightness proclaims the beauty of the soul merging perfectly with God.

translit: tayēntira ruḷḷat taṭampō lilaṅkum mayēntirap paḷḷiyiṉpa vāḻvē - kayēntiraṉaik
translation: O joyful life of Mayendirappalli, shining like the expansive hearts of the supremely compassionate. To rescue Gajendra the elephant,
commentary: The joy found at Mayendirappalli is compared to the wide hearts of truly compassionate people. God shines brightest in a heart that mercy for all living beings has expanded. Then the old story of Gajendra begins, the elephant devoted to God who cried out for rescue.

translit: kāyaluṟā taṉṟuvantu kāttōṉ pukaḻmullai vāyili ṉōṅku maṇiviḷakkē - mēya
translation: O towering jeweled lamp of Thirumullaivayil, praised by the protector Vishnu who came that day and saved him from suffering. Abiding,
commentary: The story ends with Gajendra saved from suffering. Vishnu came down to rescue him, yet even this great protector looks up in praise to the supreme light at Thirumullaivayil. Vallalar sees that light as a towering lamp studded with jewels, lighting the path for all beings.

translit: palikkāvūr tōṟum patañcēppac ceṉṟu kalikkāmūr mēvuṅ karumpē - valikkālil
translation: O sweet sugarcane dwelling in Kalikkamur, wandering for alms through every town until your sacred feet grow red. In the strong wind,
commentary: Here God takes the traditional form of a wandering beggar, going from town to town for alms until His sacred feet turn red. Hard and humble as that image is, the presence at Kalikkamur is still called sweet sugarcane. Grace keeps all its sweetness whatever lowly form it takes.

translit: pāykkāṭu kiṉṟavoru paccai mukilparavuñ cāykkāṭu mēvun taṭaṅkaṭalē - vāykkamaiyac
translation: O vast ocean abiding in Chaykkadu, where a spreading green cloud leaps.
commentary: God is a vast, boundless ocean of grace. Vallalar pictures this presence in the lush temple town of Chaykkadu, brimming with life and natural beauty.

translit: collava ṉīccaraṅku tōyavumpa rāmperumaip pallava ṉīccarattem pāvaṉamē - nallavarkaḷ
translation: O our pure Lord of Pallavaneesvaram of supreme greatness, merging in a way that can be aptly described.
commentary: The supreme, boundless God merges with the human soul intimately, and the merging is real. Vallalar addresses this pure presence at the Pallavaneesvaram shrine.

translit: kaṇkāṭṭu neṟṟik kaṭavuḷē yeṉṟutoḻa veṇkāṭṭiṉ mēvukiṉṟa meypporuḷē - taṇkāṭṭik
translation: Good people worship you, saying, "O God who reveals an eye on your forehead!" O true Reality abiding in Venkadu.
commentary: Good people worship God by honoring the third eye of spiritual wisdom on his forehead. At Venkadu, Vallalar calls him the true Reality, the truth that stands behind the familiar physical forms.

translit: kārkāṭṭit taiyalartaṅ kaṇkāṭṭic cōlaikaḷcūḻ cīrkāṭṭup paḷḷic civakkoḻuntē - pārkāṭ
translation: O tender shoot of Siva in glorious Kattupalli, surrounded by groves that display coolness, show dark clouds, and resemble the dark eyes of women.
commentary: A tender shoot is fresh, growing, beautiful life, and that is how Vallalar sees Siva at Kattupalli. The temple sits among cool, dark groves.

translit: ṭurukāvū rellā moḷinayakka vōṅkuṅ kurukāvūr veḷḷaṭaiyeṅ kōvē - arukāta
translation: O our King of the Velladai shrine in Kurukavur, rising up to reveal the world so that all the unyielding towns desire your light.
commentary: Divine light changes even the most stubborn, hard-hearted places. The Lord of the Kurukavur shrine is a King whose shining grace makes the whole world long for his presence.

translit: kārkāḻi ṉeñcak kavuṇiyarkkup pōtamaruḷ cīrkāḻi ñāṉat tiraviyamē - ōrkāḻip
translation: O treasure of wisdom in Sirkazhi. You granted enlightenment to the sage of the Kauniya clan whose heart dispels dark ignorance.
commentary: Sirkazhi is where a famous child-saint of the Kauniya family received sudden enlightenment from God. Vallalar recalls that story and praises the Lord as the treasure from which true wisdom comes.

translit: pālaṟkā vaṉṟu pacumpoṟṟā ḷaṅkoṭutta kōlakkā mēvuṅ koṭaiyāḷā - kōlakkā
translation: O generous giver residing in Kolakka. On that day you gave cymbals of pure gold to that child of Sirkazhi.
commentary: The child-saint's story goes on. When the young boy sang with devotion and clapped his bare hands, God appeared at Kolakka and gave him golden cymbals to ease his pain.

translit: uḷḷirukkum puḷḷirukku mōtum pukaḻvāynta puḷḷirukkum vēḷūrp puricaṭaiyāy -kaḷḷirukkum
translation: O Lord with twisted matted hair in Pullirukkuvelur. Your renowned shrine holds the Rig Veda and the divine bird within it.
commentary: The name Pullirukkuvelur carries its own sacred history. It points to the Rig Veda and to Jatayu, the legendary divine bird, both said to have worshipped the Lord at this famous shrine.

translit: kāviṉ maruvuṅ kaṉamun ticaimaṇakkum kōviṉ maruvukaṇṇār kōyilāy - māviṉ
translation: O Lord of Kannarkoil. Your temple is surrounded by dense groves where sweet nectar flows and fragrance spreads in all directions.
commentary: Kannarkoil sits among fragrant groves where nectar flows. Vallalar lets that sweetness of the place mirror the sweetness of grace.

translit: iṭaimuṭiyiṉ ṟīṅkaṉiyeṉ ṟelliṉ mucuttāvum kaṭaimuṭiyiṉ mēvuṅ karuttā - koṭaimuṭiyā
translation: O supreme mind residing in Kadaimudi. Here a monkey leaps at the mountain peak thinking the evening sun is a sweet mango.
commentary: Kadaimudi stands so high that a monkey on its peak leaps at the evening sun, taking it for a ripe mango. With that vivid picture Vallalar addresses God as the supreme intelligence presiding over the town.

translit: naṉṟiyū reṉṟinta ñālamelām vāḻttukiṉṟa niṉṟiyūr mēvu nilaimaiyaṉē - oṉṟik
translation: O unchanging Lord who dwells in Ninriyur, which this entire world praises as the city of goodness!
commentary: At Ninriyur the Lord is the steady, unchanging presence. The whole world, Vallalar notes, praises this shrine as a place of absolute goodness.

translit: karuppuṉkū ruḷḷak kayavar nayavāt tiruppuṉkūr mēvuñ civaṉē - uruppolintē
translation: O Siva who dwells in Thiruppunkur, unsought by base men whose minds are united in dark malice!
commentary: Siva dwells at Thiruppunkur, yet those whose minds are clouded by malice and base desire never seek Him. To them this holy presence stays hidden.

translit: īṭūri lātuyarnta ētuviṉā lōṅkutiru nīṭū rilaṅku niḻaṟṟaruvē - pīṭukoṇṭu
translation: O radiant, shade-giving tree shining in sacred Needur, rising high with unparalleled greatness!
commentary: At Needur God is a vast, sheltering tree. Its shade is cooling comfort and refuge for the weary soul.

translit: maṉṉiyū rellām vaṇaṅka vaḷaṅkoṇṭa aṉṉiyūr mēvu matipatiyē - maṉṉarcuka
translation: O Sovereign who resides in Anniyur, possessing such majestic wealth that all established towns bow before it!
commentary: Anniyur is so rich in grace that all other towns bow to it. The true wealth of any place, Vallalar suggests, comes entirely from the presence of God.

translit: vāḻvik kuṭikaḷaṭi maṇpūca lāleṉṉum vēḻvik kuṭiyamarnta vittakaṉē - cūḻvuṟṟōr
translation: O wise Lord seated in Velvikkudi, where people say that smearing the dust of Your feet grants the joyous life of kings!
commentary: People at Velvikkudi say that smearing the dust of the Lord's feet gives the joyous life of kings. Vallalar's point is that devotion is far greater than worldly power, since this simple act brings a joy the richest kings cannot reach.

translit: viṇṇetirkoṇ ṭintiraṉpōṉ mēvineṭu nāḷvāḻap paṇṇetirkoḷ pāṭip paramporuḷē - naṇṇum
translation: O Supreme Reality of Padi, receiving melodic songs and granting a long life akin to Indra who rules the heavens! Approaching
commentary: At Padi the Lord listens to devotional music and blesses those who sing. He grants them a long, prosperous life like that of Indra, king of the gods.

translit: vaṇañcē riṟaivaṉ makiḻntu vaṇaṅkum maṇañcēri nīṅkā makiḻvē - maṇañcērntu
translation: the beautifully adorned king who joyfully worships, O unceasing joy of Mananjeri! Uniting in fragrance,
commentary: Mananjeri is traditionally tied to divine marriage and fragrance. God lives there as endless joy, worshipped gladly even by earthly kings.

translit: vāraṭṭa koṅkai malaiyā ḷoṭuṅkoṟukkai vīraṭṭa mēvum viyaṉiṟaivē - ōraṭṭa
translation: O immense Lord residing in Korukkai Virattam alongside the mountain goddess whose breasts are bound by a bodice! Across the eight
commentary: At Korukkai Virattam the immense Lord is worshipped with His consort Parvati, the mountain goddess. The two stand together in majesty at this sacred site.

translit: tikkuṅ katināṭṭic cīrkoḷtirut toṇṭaruḷam okkuṅ karuppaṟiya lūraracē - mikkatiru
translation: directions you establish the path, O King of Karuppariyalur, dwelling in harmony with the hearts of excellent sacred devotees! Abundant
commentary: God sets the spiritual path across all eight directions of the world. As King of Karuppariyalur He makes His true home in the hearts of devoted seekers.

translit: māvaḷaruñ centā maraivaḷaruñ ceykurakkuk kāvaḷaru miṉpak kaṉacukamē - tāvumayal
translation: prosperity and red lotuses grow in the fields of Kurakkukka, O dense bliss of joy flourishing there! The leaping delusion
commentary: Kurakkukka is fertile country, its fields full of red lotuses. The Lord there is a thick, flourishing bliss that dispels human delusion.

translit: kāḻko ḷirumaṉattuk kāriruṇīt tōrmaruvum vāḻkoḷi puttūrmaṇiccuṭarē - tāḻvakaṟṟa
translation: O radiant gem-like flame of Koliputhur, embraced by those who have cast away the pitch darkness from their hardened minds.
commentary: A gem-like flame burns in Koliputhur, yet only those who have cleared the hard, stubborn darkness of ignorance from their minds come to know it. The shrine stands in a town. What it points to is a purified heart, where the divine is truly found.

translit: naṇṇip paṭikkaraiyar nāṭōṟum vāḻttukiṉṟa maṇṇip paṭikkaraivāḻ maṅkalamē - viṇṇiṉiṭai
translation: Approaching to remove their lowliness, devotees praise you every day. O auspicious one dwelling in Mannippadikkarai!
commentary: Devotees in Mannippadikkarai come every day to sing His praise and wash away their earthly flaws. Keeping the mind on the auspicious one, they rise out of lowliness little by little.

translit: vāmām puliyūr malarccōlai cūḻntilaṅkum ōmām puliyūrvāḻ uttamamē - nēmārnta
translation: O supreme one dwelling in Omampuliyur, shining amidst flower groves that reach up into the sky!
commentary: Omampuliyur sits among flower groves that seem to reach the sky, and Vallalar calls God the supreme one resting there. The beauty of the place mirrors the perfection of the divine.

translit: vāṉāṭṭu muḷḷūr maruvukiṉṟōr pōṟṟutiruk kāṉāṭṭu muḷḷūrk kalaikkaṭalē - mēṉāṭṭum
translation: O ocean of arts in holy Kanattumullur, praised by the devoted residents of the heavenly realm!
commentary: An ocean of arts is God as the source of all knowledge, wisdom and creativity. Even the residents of the heavenly worlds come down to Kanattumullur to worship. The wisdom found there is greater than any heavenly reward.

translit: tēraiyūrc ceṅkatirpōṟ cemmaṇika ṇiṉṟilaṅkum nāraiyūr mēvu naṭunilaiyē - pāril
translation: O impartial one residing in Naraiyur, where red gems shine like the rays of the red sun riding its chariot across the high heavens!
commentary: The impartial one treats every living being with equal fairness and compassion. Vallalar sees that justice glowing in Naraiyur like red gems, like the sun in its chariot. Grace shines on everyone alike, without distinction.

translit: uṭampūr pavattai yoḻittaruḷum mēṉmaik kaṭampūrvāḻ eṉṉiraṇṭu kaṇṇē - taṭampoḻilil
translation: O my two eyes dwelling in eminent Kadambur, graciously ending the cycle of births burdened by the physical body!
commentary: Vallalar calls the Lord of Kadambur his own two eyes. He praises Him for ending the cycle of births, the soul's heavy burden of taking on one body after another.

translit: kontaṇavuṅ kārkkuḻalār kōlamayiṟ pōlulavum pantaṇa nallūrp pacupatiyē - kantamalar
translation: O Lord Pasupati of Panthananallur, where women with dark hair adorned with flower clusters wander like beautiful peacocks in the wide groves!
commentary: Pasupati means the Lord of all living beings. He dwells in Panthananallur, a town of wide groves where women with flowers in their dark hair walk with the grace of peacocks.

translit: añcaṉūrceytatavat tālap peyarkoṇṭa kañcaṉūr vāḻumeṉṟaṉ kaṇmaṇiyē - añcukaṅkaḷ
translation: O pupil of my eye living in Kanjanur, which gained its name through the penance performed by Brahma seated on the fragrant lotus!
commentary: The pupil is the center of sight, and that is what the Lord of Kanjanur is to Vallalar's spiritual vision. The town takes its name from Brahma, the creator god of Hindu tradition, who performed intense spiritual discipline there to earn divine grace.

translit: nāṭikkā vuḷḷē namaccivā yampukalum kōṭikkā mēvuṅ kuḷirmatiyē - ōṭik
translation: O cool moon abiding in Kodikka, where parrots seek out the groves and chant Namashivaya!
commentary: The Lord of Kodikka soothes like a cool moon. Devotion runs so deep there that even the wild parrots in the groves have learned to chant "Namashivaya", the sacred five-syllable mantra.

translit: karumaṅka lakkuṭiyiṟ kāṇṭumeṉa vōtum tirumaṅka lakkuṭiyil tēṉē - taruma
translation: O honey of Thirumangalakudi, where devotees come running and declare, "We shall behold Him in Karumangalakudi!"
commentary: He is honey to those who seek Him in the twin shrines of Thirumangalakudi and Karumangalakudi. You can almost hear the pilgrims hurrying, eager to catch a glimpse of the Lord.

translit: maṉantāḷ malarai maruvuvippōr vāḻum paṉantāḷiṟ pālukanta pākē - tiṉantāḷiṟ
translation: O sweet syrup who delighted in the milk at Pananthal, where those who unite their minds with your fragrant lotus feet reside. Daily at your feet,
commentary: In Pananthal the Lord is sweet syrup, and the true devotees who live there keep their minds joined to His feet day after day.

translit: cūḻtiruvāyp pāṭiyaṅku cūḻkiṉumā meṉṟulakar vāḻtiruvāyp pāṭi-iṉpa vāritiyē - ēḻpuvikkuḷ
translation: worldly people gather and declare it a blessing even to dwell in its surroundings. O ocean of bliss in Thiruvaipadi where they live! Within the seven worlds,
commentary: Thiruvaipadi holds an ocean of bliss. People flock there because they count it a blessing just to live somewhere near it.

translit: vāyññalū rītē maruvaveṉa vāṉavarcēr cēyññalūr iṉpac ceḻuṅkaṉiyē - vāñcaiyuṟum
translation: celestials gather saying Seygnalur is the perfect place to reach. O rich fruit of bliss in that Seygnalur! The desiring
commentary: In Seygnalur God is the ripe fruit of spiritual joy. Even the celestials gather there, calling it the most perfect place to reach in all the worlds.

translit: cīvaṉ kuṭiyuṟavic cīrnakaroṉ ṟēyeṉuñcīrt tēvaṉ kuṭimakiḻnta teḷḷamutē - ōvil
translation: soul praises it as the one perfect city to inhabit. O clear nectar rejoicing in that excellent Devangudi! Ceaselessly,
commentary: In Devangudi the Lord is clear, pure nectar. The seeking soul looks to this one town as the ideal place to find lasting shelter.

translit: mayalūr maṉampōl vayaliṟ kayalūr viyalūr civāṉanta veṟpē - ayalāmpal
translation: carp dart through the fields like a mind possessed by delusion. O mountain of Siva's bliss in Viyalur! Nearby, water lilies
commentary: The Lord of Viyalur stands firm and still, a mountain of Siva's bliss. Down in the fields the carp dart about like a mind caught in worldly delusion, and Vallalar sets that restlessness against His steady peace.

translit: maṭṭaiyūr vaṇṭiṉaṅkaḷ vāyntu viruntukoḷum koṭṭaiyū ruṭkiḷaruṅ kōmaḷamē - iṭṭamuṭaṉ
translation: O beautiful Lord shining within Kottaiyur, where swarms of bees gather and feast on the oozing nectar! With fondness...
commentary: Kottaiyur's Lord is pictured as a flower brimming with nectar. The bees crowding in to feast are the devotees, eager for his sweet grace.

translit: eṉṉampa reṉṉampa reṉṟayaṉmāl vātukoḷa iṉṉampar mēviniṉṟa eṉṉuṟavē - muṉṉampu
translation: Brahma and Vishnu argued, each claiming, "He is my Lord! He is my Lord!" O my true kin who resides in Innambar! Long ago...
commentary: An old story tells of Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver quarreling over which of them was supreme. The reality above both of them lives at Innambar. Facing all that cosmic power, Vallalar still calls the Lord his own true kin.

translit: māṟkum puṟampiyalā vāymaiyaruḷ ceyyavuḷam ēṟkum puṟampiyamvāḻ eṉṉuyirē - māṟkaruviṉ
translation: Your heart graciously consented to bestow true and inseparable grace upon Vishnu. O my life who lives in Purampiyam!
commentary: God is the ultimate giver of grace at the Purampiyam shrine. Even great deities like Vishnu rely entirely on this supreme compassion. The poem brings this cosmic scale down to a deeply personal level by addressing the Divine simply as life itself.

translit: kaṇvicaiya maṅkaik kaṉipōṟ peṟattoṇṭar eṇvicaiya maṅkaiyilvāḻ eṉkuruvē - maṇṇulakil
translation: Devotees meditate on you to attain you like a visible, ripened fruit. O my Guru who lives in esteemed Visayamangai! In this earthly world...
commentary: Devotees reach for God the way you reach for a ripe, sweet fruit. At Visayamangai the Lord is a Guru (a spiritual teacher), neither hidden nor far away. Grace, in this picture, is something you can hold, ready to be taken.

translit: vaikāvūr namporuṭṭāṉ vaikiyateṉ ṟaṉpartoḻum vaikāvūr mēviyaveṉ vāḻmutalē - uyyumvakaik
translation: Devotees worship you and say, "He has stayed here just for our sake!" O source of my life who resides in Vaikavur! To find salvation...
commentary: At Vaikavur the devotees are amazed that the Divine has chosen to stay among them. God is no remote force in the heavens. He remains in this physical world out of pure compassion, to help people find freedom.

translit: kāttum paṭaittuṅ kalaittuniṟpōr nāṭōṟum ēttuṅ kuraṅkāṭṭiṉ eṉṉaṭpē - māttaḻaitta
translation: My friend in Kurangadu, praised daily by those who stand protecting, creating, and dissolving, fostering great growth.
commentary: The gods who create, protect and destroy are mighty, yet even they worship this Lord every day. Vallalar places the Supreme above them all. Still, he calls him his friend in Kurangadu.

translit: vaṇpaḻaṉat tiṉkuviveṇ vāyiṟṟēṉ vākkiyiṭa uṇpaḻaṉat teṉṟaṉ uyirkkuyirē - paṇpakaṉṟa
translation: Life of my life in Pazhanam, where honey pours into the sweet, pointed white mouths of blossoms in the rich fields, dispelling all baseness.
commentary: Vallalar names God the life of his own life. He sets that closeness in the fertile fields of Pazhanam, where blossoms overflow with honey. Grace washes away human flaws as naturally as that rich earth yields sweetness.

translit: veyyāṟṟi ṉiṉṟavarai meyyāṟṟi ṉēṟṟutiru aiyāṟṟiṉ mēviya-eṉ ṉātaravē - poyyāṟṟi
translation: My refuge dwelling in holy Thiruvaiyaru, lifting those who stand in the cruel river into the river of truth, erasing all falsehood.
commentary: The name Thiruvaiyaru refers to five holy rivers. Vallalar plays on the flowing water. The Lord pulls struggling souls out of the cruel river of worldly suffering and sets them safely in the steady river of truth.

translit: meyttāṉa niṉṟōr veḷittāṉa mēvutiru neyttāṉat tuḷḷamarnta nittiyamē - maitta
translation: O eternal one seated within holy Neyttanam, manifesting in the vast space to those who stand in the true state, clearing away the darkness.
commentary: The Lord of Neyttanam shows himself fully only to those whose lives stand on truth. Reach that honesty and he clears away your inner darkness. Then he appears as vast, endless space, no longer a limited physical form.

translit: karumpuliyūrk kāḷaiyoṭuṅ kaṇṇōṭṭaṅ koḷḷum perumpuliyūr vāḻkaruṇaip pēṟē - virumpinitam
translation: O treasure of compassion living in Perumpuliyur, casting a gracious glance upon the strong youth of Karumpuliyur, showering love daily.
commentary: For Vallalar the Divine is a living treasure of compassion, and that grace falls like a shower of love every day. The Lord of Perumpuliyur keeps a warm, protecting eye on his devotees and holds them always in his care.

translit: poṉṉuṅkauttuvamum pūṇṭōṉ pukaḻntaruḷai maṉṉu maḻapāṭi vacciramē - tuṉṉukiṉṟa
translation: O diamond of Mazhapadi, whose grace was secured by the praises of the Lord adorned in gold and the Kaustubha gem!
commentary: God is the diamond of Mazhapadi, a sacred temple town. Even Vishnu, known by his legendary Kaustubha gem, sings praises to receive this grace.

translit: nāykkuṅ kaṭaiyēṉ navaitīra naṟkaruṇai vāykkum paḻuvūr marakatamē - tēykkaḷaṅkil
translation: O emerald of Pazhuvur, who grants good grace to cure the flaws of this wretch, baser than an approaching dog!
commentary: The emerald of Pazhuvur heals. Vallalar, in deep humility, calls himself lower than a wandering dog and trusts wholly in divine compassion to cure his worldly flaws.

translit: vāṉūr matipōṉ maṇiyāṟ kumutamalar kāṉū ruyartaṅkak kaṭṭiyē - nāṉūṟu
translation: O lofty gold ingot of Kanur, where water lilies bloom by the light of gems that shine like the unblemished moon moving across the sky!
commentary: At Kanur the Divine is a lofty block of solid gold. The town shines so brightly that its gems glow like the clear night moon, and the night-blooming water lilies open in their light.

translit: kōlan tuṟaikoṇṭa kōvaiyaruḷ kōvaimakiḻ ālan tuṟaiyiṉ aṇimuttē - nīlaṅkoḷ
translation: O beautiful pearl of joyful Alandurai, the Sovereign of grace who assumes four hundred splendid forms!
commentary: At Alandurai God is a beautiful pearl, the Sovereign of grace who takes on hundreds of splendid forms to reach and lift up humanity.

translit: tēntuṟaiyi laṉṉamakiḻ cēkkai palanilavu māntuṟaivāḻ māṇikka māmalaiyē - ēntaṟivām
translation: O great ruby mountain residing in Manthurai, where joyful swans find many resting places along the sweet, dark shores!
commentary: Manthurai's Lord stands like a great ruby mountain, vast and unshakable. Around that glow lies deep peace, where joyful swans rest safely at the water's edge.

translit: nūṟṟuṟaiyil niṉṟavarkaḷ nōkkimakiḻ veytutirup pāṟṟuṟaiyil niṉṟa parañcuṭarē - nāṟṟicaiyun
translation: O supreme flame standing in Tiruppatrurai, where those established in the scriptures look upon you and rejoice. In all four directions,
commentary: At Tiruppatrurai the Lord stands as a supreme flame. Those who have studied the scriptures deeply find their real joy when they finally look upon that living light.

translit: tēṉaikkā vuḷmalarkaḷ tēṅkaṭaleṉ ṟākkuvikkum āṉaikkā mēviyamar aṟputamē - māṉaippōl
translation: flowers within the groves pour honey to create a sweet ocean. O wonder abiding in Anaikka! Like a deer,
commentary: Anaikka is so full of flowering groves that their nectar runs together into an ocean of sweetness. In the middle of all that plenty, the Lord is the wonder.

translit: maiññīla vāṭkaṇ malarāḷ maruvutirup paiññīli mēvum paramparamē - eññāṉṟum
translation: the lady of the flower with dark blue sword-like eyes embraces you. O supreme of the supreme abiding in sacred Tirupanjali! Forever,
commentary: Tirupanjali is home to the supreme of the supreme. Vallalar draws the traditional picture of the Lord embraced by the Goddess, whose dark, sharp eyes are likened both to a gentle deer and to a sword.

translit: ēccirā maṅkalattō ṭiṉpan tarumpācci lāccirā mañcēr aruḷnilaiyē - nīccaṟiyā
translation: bringing joy with unblemished auspiciousness, O state of grace present in Pachil Achiramam! For those ignorant of swimming,
commentary: Grace itself dwells at Pachil Achiramam. It brings a joy with no blemish in it, and a goodness to the world that lasts.

translit: tāṅkōy malaippiṟavi yārkalikkōr vārkalamām īṅkōy malaivāḻ ilañciyamē - ōṅkātu
translation: across the roaring ocean of mountainous births, you are a sturdy ship. O living reservoir in Eengoi Malai! Without rising,
commentary: The endless cycle of birth and death is a vast, roaring ocean. For souls who do not know how to swim across this terrifying sea, the divine at Eengoi Malai acts as a sturdy rescue ship. It is a living reservoir of grace that carries them safely to the shore.

translit: nāṭpōkki niṟku navaiyuṭaiyār nāṭaritām vāṭpōkki mēvukiṉṟa vaḷḷalē - kōṭpōkki
translation: O benevolent Lord dwelling in Vāṭpōkki, you are rarely found by flawed people who stand wasting their days. Dispelling false tenets,
commentary: People who let their days drift by without purpose rarely find the benevolent Lord of Vāṭpōkki. He dispels false tenets and clears the mind for real seeking.

translit: nilluṅ kaṭampa neṟipō leṉappūvai colluṅ kaṭampan tuṟainiṟaivē - mallaloṭu
translation: O perfect Lord of Kaṭampantuṟai, where the mynah bird speaks and urges people to stand firmly in the Kadamba path. With abundance,
commentary: Even the birds teach at Kaṭampantuṟai. The mynah calls out for people to stand firm in the Kadamba path, and all of nature seems to carry the same message.

translit: vāḻum parāyttuṟaivāṉ maṉṉavaru maṉṉavaruñ cūḻum parāyttuṟaivāḻ tōṉṟalē - kūḻumpal
translation: heavenly gods and earthly kings surround you, O noble Lord living in Parāyttuṟai. Abundant crops and many
commentary: Kings of the earth and gods of the heavens both gather to worship at Parāyttuṟai. The Lord they surround stands above the rulers of both worlds.

translit: naṟkuṭiyu mōṅki nalamperuku mēṉmaitiruk kaṟkuṭiyiṟ cantāṉa kaṟpakamē - ciṟcukattār
translation: good families flourish and multiply their prosperity in majestic and holy Kaṟkuṭi, where you stand as the wish-fulfilling Kalpaka tree. Those of divine bliss
commentary: The Kalpaka is the celestial tree of Indian tradition that grants any wish. At holy Kaṟkuṭi the Lord is that tree, and good families there flourish and grow in prosperity.

translit: piṟcanana millāp perumai tarumuṟaiyūrc caṟcaṉarcēr mūkkīc carattaṇiyē - maṟcey
translation: and virtuous people gather around you, O jewel of Mūkkīccaram in Uṟaiyūr, as you grant them the greatness of having no future births. Wrestling
commentary: Freedom from the round of death and rebirth is the highest gift. Virtuous seekers gather at Mūkkīccaram in Uṟaiyūr to receive exactly that, and find a lasting peace where no future birth waits for them.

translit: arāppaḷḷi mēvu mavaṉiṉṟu vāḻttum cirāppaḷḷi ñāṉat teḷivē - irāppaḷḷi
translation: You are the clear wisdom of Cirappalli, praised today by the one who rests upon the serpent bed.
commentary: In Hindu tradition Vishnu rests on a cosmic serpent. Vallalar pictures even him praising the Lord who is the clear wisdom of Cirappalli.

translit: niṉṟeḻaṉmey yaṉṟeṉavē nērntulaku vāḻttukiṉṟa naṉṟeṟumpi yūrilaṅku naṉṉeṟiyē - tuṉṟukayaṟ
translation: You are the good path shining in the fine town of Erumpiyur, praised by the world which realizes that waking from the sleep of night is not the ultimate truth.
commentary: The Lord shines as the good path in Erumpiyur. Every morning people wake from the night's sleep, and the world sees that this waking is not the final truth. The awakening the wise praise lies deeper.

translit: kaṇṇār neṭuṅkaḷattaik kaṭṭaḻitta meyttavarcūḻ taṇṇār neṭuṅkaḷameyt tārakamē - eṇṇār
translation: You are the true support of cool Nedungkalam, surrounded by true ascetics who have destroyed the binding spell of women with carp-like eyes.
commentary: Classical Tamil poetry likens a woman's beautiful eyes to carp. The true ascetics around cool Nedungkalam have broken that spell of physical desire and worldly illusion, and the Lord is their true support. He holds up those who look past fleeting beauty for lasting truth.

translit: tarukkāṭṭup paḷḷit takaikoṇṭōr cūḻun tirukkāṭṭup paḷḷiyilvāḻ tēvē - marukkāṭṭu
translation: O God residing in Tirukkattuppalli, you are surrounded by great ones who possess the power to subdue the arrogant dance of the unthinking.
commentary: People who lack understanding often live with loud, arrogant pride. At Tirukkattuppalli the Lord is surrounded by great souls who have the quiet power to calm it.

translit: nīlam poḻiṟkuḷ niṟaitaṭaṅkaṭ kērkāṭṭum ālam poḻiṟcivayō kappayaṉē - cīlaniṟai
translation: You are the fruit of Siva-yoga in Alampozhil, revealing beauty to the wide eyes within the fragrant groves of blue lilies.
commentary: Siva-yoga is deep spiritual practice, and the Lord of Alampozhil is its fruit. Vallalar pictures that fruit as beauty shown to wide eyes among fragrant groves of blue lilies, tying the inner focus of yoga to the blossoming of the natural world.

translit: vānturutti koṇṭuḷ ḷaṉaleḻuppu vōrpukaḻum pūnturutti mēvuciva puṇṇiyamē - kāntaruvat
translation: O holy merit of Siva abiding in Poonduruthi, praised by yogis who raise their inner fire using the bellows of breath!
commentary: Yogis work their breath like a bellows to wake the fire within, and they are the ones who praise Siva at Poonduruthi. Vallalar calls that presence a holy merit.

translit: taṇṭiyūr pōṟṟun takaikācik kaṭceytu kaṇṭiyūr vāḻuṅ kaḷaikaṇṇē - koṇṭiyalpiṉ
translation: O ultimate refuge residing in Kandiyur, which serves as the great Kasi praised by lute-playing Gandharvas!
commentary: Kandiyur is the refuge Vallalar praises here. He sets it beside Kasi (Varanasi), the great pilgrimage city, and says even the Gandharvas, the celestial musicians, sing of it.

translit: vēṟṟut tuṟaiyuḷ viravā tavarpukaḻum cōṟṟut tuṟaiyuṭ cukavaḷamē - āṟṟalilāt
translation: O blissful wealth within Sotrutthurai, praised by those of steadfast nature who never stray into alien paths!
commentary: Sotrutthurai holds a true wealth of bliss. The ones who praise it are seekers who stay on their path and never let their attention drift into conflicting ones.

translit: tītik kuṭiyeṉṟu ceppap paṭārmaruvum vētik kuṭiyiṉpa veḷḷamē - kōtiyalum
translation: O flood of bliss in Vedikkudi, reached by those who are never scorned as a weak and wicked lineage!
commentary: At Vedikkudi the Lord comes as a flood of joy. It reaches people of clean living, whose name no one can call wicked.

translit: vaṉkuṭit tiṭṭai maruvār maruvutirut teṉkuṭit tiṭṭaic civapatamē - naṉkuṭaiya
translation: O supreme state of Siva in the beautiful and sacred Tenkudithittai, reached by those who shun harsh and flawed settlements!
commentary: Tenkudithittai holds the high state of Siva. Seekers reach it by keeping away from harsh places and bad company and staying close to virtue.

translit: uḷḷamaṅkai mārmē luṟuttā tavarpukaḻum puḷḷamaṅkai vāḻparama pōkamē - kaḷḷamilañ
translation: O supreme bliss dwelling in Pullamangai, praised by those who do not fix their minds on women!
commentary: Pullamangai's Lord is the highest joy. Ascetics who have turned their minds from physical desire worship Him there and give their whole attention to the truth.

translit: cakkarap paḷḷitaṉiṟ ṟāmpayiṉṟa maintarkaḷcūḻ cakkarap paḷḷitaṉil taṇṇaḷiyē - mikka
translation: O cool grace of Cakkarappalli, surrounded by youths who have practiced the guileless five-syllable mantra in their school!
commentary: The five-syllable mantra is Na-Ma-Si-Va-Ya, the primary sacred chant of Siva. At Cakkarappalli young devotees practice it with pure hearts, and the Lord's cooling grace is what they receive.

translit: arukāvūr cūḻntē aḻakupeṟa vōṅkum karukāvūr iṉpak katiyē - murukārnta
translation: O joyful refuge of Karukavur, rising beautifully and surrounded by great imperishable towns!
commentary: Karukavur is a joyful refuge. Its shrine rises tall and beautiful, ringed by prosperous towns that endure.

translit: cōlait tuṟaiyiṟ cukañcivanūl vācikkum pālait tuṟaiyiṟ parimaḷamē - cīlattar
translation: O fragrance of Palaitturai, where devotees happily recite the scriptures of Siva amidst fragrant groves!
commentary: At Palaitturai the Lord is a sweet fragrance. Devotees sit among the flowering groves and recite the sacred texts together, quietly happy.

translit: collū raṭiyappar tūyamuṭi mēlvaitta nallū ramarntanaṭu nāyakamē - mallārnta
translation: O supreme Lord seated in Nallur, who placed your feet on the pure head of the devotee Appar praised by the virtuous!
commentary: Appar was one of the most revered Tamil saints of the seventh century. Tradition says that at Nallur, Siva gave him the highest blessing by placing His feet directly on the saint's head.

translit: māvū riraviyiṉpoṉ vaiyamaḷa vuñcikari āvūri luṟṟaveṅkaḷ āṇtakaiyē - ōvātu
translation: Our noble Lord residing in Avur, where the temple peak reaches up to the golden chariot of the sun drawn by great horses. Ceaselessly...
commentary: At Avur the Lord is our noble one. Vallalar pictures the temple tower so tall that it brushes the golden chariot of the sun as it passes overhead.

translit: cittimuṟṟa yōkañ ceḻumpoḻiliṟ pūvaiceyum cattimuṟṟa mēvuñ catācivamē - pattiyuṟṟōr
translation: O Sadashiva abiding in Sathimutram, where mynah birds perform perfect yoga in lush groves to attain spiritual powers. Those with devotion...
