commentary: Sadashiva is the eternal Lord, and Sathimutram is where He abides. The place is so holy that even the mynah birds in its groves are said to practice yoga.

translit: muṭṭīc curattiṉ muyalā vakaiyaruḷum paṭṭīc carattem parāparamē - tuṭṭamayal
translation: O our Supreme Lord of Patteeswaram, you grant grace so they do not suffer the burning fever of obstacles. Free from evil delusion...
commentary: The Supreme Lord of Patteeswaram protects sincere devotees. His grace keeps them from the burning fever of worldly struggle and spiritual obstacles.

translit: tīṅkuviḻai yārtamaivāṉ ceṉṟamarac ceyvikka ōṅkupaḻai yāṟaiyileṉ ṉuḷḷuvappē - pāṅkupeṟa
translation: O my inner joy residing in lofty Pazhaiyarai, you elevate those who desire no evil to abide in the heavenly realm. To gain goodness...
commentary: Vallalar feels the Lord of Pazhaiyarai as an intense joy inside him. That grace lifts anyone who wants no evil up into heaven.

translit: ārnta vaṭavilaiyāṉ aṉṉattāṉ pōṟṟinitam cārnta vaṭataḷivāḻ taṟparamē - cērnta
translation: O Supreme Lord living in Vadathali, the Lord resting on the banyan leaf and the Lord riding the swan praise you daily and seek your refuge. Reaching...
commentary: Vishnu rests on the cosmic banyan leaf and Brahma rides the swan. Both worship the supreme Lord of Vadathali every day and seek His shelter.

translit: malañcuḻi kiṉṟa maṉattark karitām valañcuḻi vāḻpoṉ malaiyē - nilañcuḻiyā
translation: O golden mountain dwelling in Valanjuzhi, rare to those whose minds swirl with impurities.
commentary: God dwells in the temple town of Valanjuzhi like a majestic golden mountain. A mind churning with worldly impurities finds this grace hard to reach, and harder still to understand.

translit: tōṇattil vantō ṉuṭaṉṟutittu vāḻkumpa kōṇattil teyvak kulakkoḻuntē - māṇuṟṟōr
translation: O divine tender shoot of Kumbakonam, praised by the one who arrived in a boat when the earth was engulfed by the deluge.
commentary: Kumbakonam's divine presence is a fresh, tender shoot of grace. Vallalar recalls an ancient story in which the creator god survived a cosmic flood in a vessel, then worshiped here to begin the world anew.

translit: kāḻkkōṭṭa nīṅkak karutuṅ kuṭamūkkiṟ kīḻkkōṭṭa mēvumaṉpar kēṇmaiyē - vāḻkkōṭṭat
translation: O intimate friend to the devotees dwelling in Keezhkottam of Kudamukku, who seek to banish their deeply rooted crookedness.
commentary: In the Keezhkottam temple of Kudamukku (an older name for Kumbakonam), God is an intimate friend to true devotees. He helps seekers remove their deepest flaws and crooked habits.

translit: tērōṇa maṭṭun tikaḻkuṭantai maṭṭumiṉṟik kārōṇa maṭṭuṅ kamaḻmalarē - cīrōṅkum
translation: O fragrant flower whose scent spreads not only to the grand chariot festivals and radiant Kudanthai, but all the way to Karonam.
commentary: God is a blossoming flower whose fragrance fills the whole region. The scent sweeps over the festival grounds and the radiant town of Kudanthai (another name for Kumbakonam), and carries all the way to the nearby temple of Karonam.

translit: yōkīc curarniṉ ṟuvantu vaṇaṅkutiru nākīc curamōṅku naṅkaṉivē - ōkaiyuḷam
translation: O our sweet fruit rising high in Thirunageswaram, gladly worshiped by the excellent masters of yoga.
commentary: A perfectly ripe, sweet fruit stands tall in Thirunageswaram. Even the greatest masters of yoga come here to offer it their joyous worship.

translit: tēkkum varakuṇaṉān teṉṉavaṉkaṇ cūḻpaḻiyaip pōkkum iṭaimarutiṟ pūraṇamē - nīkkamilā
translation: O Perfect One in Idaimaruthur who dispels the enveloping curse of blame from the virtuous Pandiyan king Varaguna!
commentary: Idaimaruthur holds the Perfect One. Vallalar recalls the old legend of the virtuous King Varaguna, freed at this very shrine from a terrible curse, and it shows that grace can wash away even the heaviest guilt.

translit: naṉkuraṅ kāṇu naṭaiyō raṭaikiṉṟa teṉkuraṅ kāṭutuṟaic cemmalē - puṉkurampai
translation: O Lord of southern Kurangaduthurai reached by those who walk the path seeking inseparable good strength!
commentary: Next comes the shrine of southern Kurangaduthurai. Vallalar calls the Lord there a noble one who gives lasting inner strength to those who sincerely walk the spiritual path.

translit: ēlak kuṭipukunta emmaṉōrk kuṇmaitaru nīlak kuṭiyilaṅku niṭkaḷamē - ñālattu
translation: O Formless One shining in Neelakkudi who grants truth to people like me residing in this lowly bodily hut!
commentary: Neelakkudi shines with the formless reality. Vallalar speaks with deep humility, amazed that this supreme truth is given freely to ordinary people living in fragile, temporary bodies.

translit: nīṭakkōr nāḷum niṉaintēt tiṭumvaikal māṭakkō yiṟkuṇ maturamē - pāṭaccīr
translation: O Sweetness within the elevated temple of Vaikal praised daily by those seeking a long life in this world!
commentary: Pure sweetness lives in the raised temple of Vaikal. Vallalar notes that people gather there every day to pray for a long and healthy life on earth.

translit: valla tamiḻppulavar maṉṉi vaṇaṅkutiru nallamakiḻ iṉpa navavaṭivē - illamayal
translation: O ever-new form of joyful bliss in Thirunallam worshipped constantly by capable Tamil poets who sing your excellence!
commentary: At Thirunallam the divine is a form of joy that keeps renewing itself. Vallalar honors the great Tamil poets who have stood before this shrine and sung its praises across the generations.

translit: āḻampaṅ keṉṉa vaṟintōr ceṟintēttum kōḻampam vāḻkaruṇaik koṇṭalē - vīḻumpoy
translation: O cloud of compassion dwelling in Kozhambam, where the wise gather and praise you, knowing your profound significance.
commentary: Picture a heavy raincloud resting over the temple town of Kozhambam. As rain brings relief to the earth, this cloud of compassion sustains the wise who gather to understand its depths.

translit: tīrā vaṭuvuṭaiyār cērtaṟ karunteyvac cīrā vaṭutuṟaiyeñ celvamē - pērāk
translation: O our wealth in Avaduthurai of divine glory. You are the God rare to be reached by those who bear the unhealing scars of falling into falsehood.
commentary: Avaduthurai holds our true wealth. Vallalar warns that living in falsehood leaves deep, unhealing spiritual wounds, and those wounds make this presence incredibly difficult to reach. Truthfulness is the essential step toward grace.

translit: karuttirutti yēttuṅ karuttark karuḷcey tirutturutti iṉpac ceḻippē - varuttumayal
translation: O abundance of bliss in Tirutturutti. You grant grace to the mindful devotees who praise you with unwavering thoughts.
commentary: Tirutturutti is an endless source of joy. Grace flows naturally to those who steady their minds and keep their thoughts wholly on God.

translit: nāḷu meḻuntūr navaiyaṟukku maṉparuḷḷam nīḷum aḻuntūr niṟaitaṭamē - vēḷimaiyōr
translation: O brimming reservoir in Azhundur, where the hearts of devotees expand. You sever the creeping flaws and the daily rising afflictions of delusion.
commentary: In Azhundur, God is a brimming reservoir of grace. Like fresh water sustaining life, this presence washes away the daily confusions and flaws that trouble the human mind.

translit: vāyūrat tēmā malarcorintu vāḻttukiṉṟa māyūrat taṉpar maṉōratamē - tēyā
translation: O fulfillment of the desires of the devotees in Mayuram, where the god of love and the celestials shower sweet large flowers and praise you with watering mouths.
commentary: In Mayuram, God fulfills every spiritual longing of the devotee. Even heavenly beings gather there in awe to offer sweet flowers and praise.

translit: vaḷanakareṉ ṟevvulakum vāḻttap paṭuñcīr viḷanakarvā ḻeṅkaṇ viruntē - iḷamaic
translation: O our feast residing in Viḷanakar, possessing such glory that all worlds praise it as a fertile city.
commentary: God is a feast here, laid out and waiting for the soul in prosperous Viḷanakar.

translit: ceṟiyalūr kūntal tiruvaṉaiyā rāṭum paṟiyalūr vāḻmeyp paramē - neṟikoṇṭē
translation: O true Supreme residing in Paṟiyalūr, where women resembling the goddess of wealth with dense, youthful dark hair play and dance.
commentary: Paṟiyalūr is full of youthful joy, dancing and beauty. Vallalar finds the true Supreme living right in the middle of that earthly life.

translit: aṉpaḷḷi yōṅku maṟivuṭaiyōr vāḻttuñcem poṉpaḷḷi vāḻñāṉa pōtamē - iṉpuḷḷit
translation: O awakening of wisdom residing in Cempoṉpaḷḷi, praised by the wise who take the path of overflowing love.
commentary: The wisdom Vallalar means is woken by overflowing love, and the head alone does not reach it. That living wisdom is God's own nature, found in the shrine of Cempoṉpaḷḷi.

translit: teḷḷiyār pōṟṟit tikaḻun tirunaṉṉip paḷḷiyārn tōṅkum paracivamē - eḷḷuṟunōy
translation: O Supreme Siva rising full in Tirunaṉṉippaḷḷi, shining as the clear-minded praise you while meditating on bliss.
commentary: It takes a clear mind settled on bliss. Those who meditate that way find Supreme Siva rising full within them, just as he fills the sacred town of Tirunaṉṉippaḷḷi.

translit: ēya valampurattai yeṇṇāma leṇṇukiṉṟōr mēya valampurattu mētakavē - tūyakoṭi
translation: O supreme excellence residing in Valampuram, sought by those who meditate on you without giving a thought to this miserable body afflicted by despised diseases.
commentary: True seekers stop giving their attention to the pains and diseases of the body. With their minds fixed wholly on God, they find supreme excellence waiting in Valampuram.

translit: aṅkāṭu kōpuramvā ṉāṟṟāṭu kiṉṟatalaic caṅkāṭu mēvuñ cayampuvē - poṅkumiruṭ
translation: O self-manifest Lord residing in Thalaichangadu, where the temple tower bathes in the celestial river.
commentary: The temple tower at Thalaichangadu rises so high it seems to bathe in the starry river of the heavens. God is called self-manifest because the sacred presence arose here on its own. No human hand installed it.

translit: kūṟutiru vākkūr koṭuppaṉapōṟ cūḻntumatil vīṟutiru vākkūr viḷakkamē - māṟakaṟṟi
translation: O shining lamp of glorious Thiru Aakkur, surrounded by walls that rise as if to hold back the surging darkness.
commentary: God shines as a lamp in Thiru Aakkur. The high walls around the town are pictured holding back the surging darkness of ignorance and despair.

translit: naṉkaṭaiyūr paṟpalavu naṉṟimaṟa vātēttum teṉkaṭaiyūr āṉantat tēṟalē - vaṉmaiyilāc
translation: O nectar of bliss in southern Kadaiyur, praised with unforgotten gratitude by many good towns that have set aside all enmity.
commentary: In southern Kadaiyur God is tasted as pure nectar of bliss. The towns around it have laid their quarrels aside and come together to give thanks, and they do not forget. Grace here leaves people at peace and grateful.

translit: coṟkaṭavi mēlōr tutittaloḻi yātōṅku naṟkaṭavūr vīraṭṭa nāyakaṉē - vaṟkaṭattum
translation: O heroic Lord of the grand Veerattam shrine in good Kadavur, praised endlessly by exalted ones with gentle words.
commentary: Kadavur's shrine is one of the heroic sites where divine power conquered destructive forces. The wise gather here without end, honoring that supreme strength in gentle, refined words.

translit: vāṭṭak kuṭicaṟṟum vāyppatē yillaiyeṉum vēṭṭak kuṭimēvu mēlavaṉē - nāṭṭamuṟṟa
translation: O supreme Lord residing in Vettakkudi, where it is said no family will ever suffer want even in times of severe famine.
commentary: Vettakkudi is a place of divine protection and plenty. Those who live under this grace, it is said, will never know hunger or poverty, even when severe famine strikes the wider world.

translit: vākkun teḷiccēri mātavattark kiṉpanalam ākkun teḷiccēri aṅkaṇaṉē - nīkkum
translation: O beautiful Lord of Teliccheri, you create blissful goodness for great ascetics of clear speech.
commentary: At Teliccheri the Lord brings deep joy to those who practice genuine devotion. That grace is the direct reward of ascetics whose speech is clear and true.

translit: karuma purattiṟ kalavā taruḷcey taruma purañcey tavamē - irumaiyiṉum
translation: You remove us from the city of karma and bestow your grace so we never mingle in it. You are the fruit of the penance performed by Tarumapuram.
commentary: The 'city of karma' is the endless round of actions and their consequences that binds the soul to suffering. God pulls the soul out of it and gives grace instead, so it never mingles there again. Tarumapuram itself is pictured as having done great penance just to receive this presence.

translit: eḷḷāṟṟiṉ mēvāta ēṟpuṭaiyōr cūḻntiṟaiñcu naḷḷāṟṟiṉ mēviya-eṉ naṟṟuṇaiyē - teḷḷāṟṟiṉ
translation: In both this world and the next, you are my good companion residing in Nallar. Worthy devotees, who never walk the path of derision, surround and worship you.
commentary: In this world and the next, God is a steady companion, present in the sacred town of Nallar. You know true devotees by their gentle conduct. They never take the path of mocking or looking down on others.

translit: nīṭṭāṟu koṇṭarampai niṉṟu kaviṉkāṭṭum kōṭṭāṟu mēvuṅ kuḷirtuṟaiyē - kūṭṭāk
translation: By the clear river, you are the cool ford residing in Kottaru, where tall plantain trees stand and display their beauty.
commentary: A river ford is an old image for safety and crossing over. At Kottaru, by the clear river, God is a cool ford in the rushing waters of life, a quiet refuge among tall plantains.

translit: karuvampar tammaik kalavāta mēṉmait tiruvampar ñāṉat tiraṭṭē - oruvantar
translation: O mass of wisdom in Thiru Ampar, you hold the supreme excellence of never joining or mingling with base people bound to the cycle of birth.
commentary: In Thiru Ampar God is a mass of pure wisdom. Those stubbornly tied to base desires and the endless round of rebirth cannot touch it.

translit: mākāḷaṅ koḷḷa mataṉait turattukiṉṟa mākāḷāt taṉpar maṉōlayamē - yōkāḷak
translation: You drove away the god of love to his utter destruction. O Lord of the Makalam shrine, you are the profound absorption of the minds of your loving devotees.
commentary: The Lord of Makalam drove off the god of love to his destruction. Vallalar recalls the old story to show that spiritual love conquers physical desire completely. In him the minds of devoted seekers come to complete stillness.

translit: kāyaccūr viṭṭuk katicēra vēṭṭavarcūḻ mīyaccūr taṇṇeṉṉum veṇṇeruppē - māyak
translation: You are surrounded by devotees who master yoga, desiring to leave the cruel afflictions of the body and attain salvation. O cool white fire of the Miyachur shrine.
commentary: Most people think of fire as hot and destructive. Vallalar pictures divine grace as a cool white fire that soothes. Seekers gather around this cooling light to escape the pain of physical life and find lasting freedom.

translit: kaḷaṅkōyil neñcak kayavar maruvā iḷaṅkōyiṉ ñāṉa iṉippē - vaḷaṅkōvai
translation: Base people whose hearts are temples of deceit and illusion cannot approach you. O sweetness of wisdom of the Ilangoyil shrine.
commentary: A deceitful mind is an absolute barrier to the divine. The sweetness of true wisdom stays out of reach for any heart filled with trickery and illusion.

translit: nāṭun tilata nayappulavar nāṭōṟum pāṭun tilataip patinitiyē - āṭumayil
translation: Loving poets who weave fertile garlands of words and stand as ornaments to the seeking world sing your praise every day. O treasure of the Thilathai shrine.
commentary: Gifted poets celebrate this treasure every day. They string words together like flower garlands, and those garlands guide and uplift the world.

translit: kāmpuraṅkoḷ tōḷiyarpoṟ kāviṟ payilkiṉṟa pāmpuraṅkoḷ uṇmaip paramporuḷē - āmpuvaṉam
translation: Dancing peacocks and women with shoulders like bamboo wander in the golden groves of the Pampuram shrine. You are the true supreme reality residing there.
commentary: God, the supreme and absolute reality, lives right in the middle of the living world. Vallalar places that truth among dancing peacocks and golden groves.

translit: tuṉṉum peruṅkuṭikaḷ cūḻntuvalañ ceytuvakai maṉṉuñ ciṟukuṭi-āṉ mārttamē - muṉṉaracum
translation: O Lord Anmarthar of Sirukudi, where great multitudes gather to circumambulate you with enduring joy! In the past, the kingly Appar
commentary: Anmarthar means the Lord of the Soul, praised here in the sacred town of Sirukudi. Vallalar recalls the joy of the crowds circling the shrine, then begins a memory of the revered saint Appar.

translit: kāḻi miḻalaiyaruṅ kaṇṭutoḻak kācaḷitta vīḻi miḻalai virāṭṭuruvē - ūḻitoṟum
translation: and Sambandar of Sirkazhi saw and worshipped you, and you granted them gold coins, O Cosmic Form of Veezhimizhalai! Through every eon,
commentary: A famous story of grace. During a terrible famine the two great saints Appar and Sambandar prayed, and God appeared at the temple of Veezhimizhalai and gave them gold coins so they could feed the starving people.

translit: maṉṉiyūr mālviṭaiyāy vāṉavā veṉṟutoḻa vaṉṉiyūr vāḻu maṇikaṇṭā - innimiṭam
translation: devotees worship you saying, "O Lord of Manniyur, rider of the great bull, O heavenly being!" O jewel-necked Lord residing in Vanniyur!
commentary: Devotees in town after town call on him as the rider of the sacred bull. The name jewel-necked Lord recalls the ancient story where he swallowed a deadly poison to save the universe.

translit: cintuṅ karuvaliyiṉ tiṇmaiyeṉṟu tērntavarkaḷ muntuṅ karuvilivāḻ mukkaṇṇā - mantaṇattaik
translation: Realizing in an instant the relentless strength of the cycle of birth, the wise rush before you. O three-eyed Lord residing in Karuvili!
commentary: The wise run to God because they see how easily the endless cycle of birth and death traps the soul. They take shelter with the three-eyed Lord of Karuvili.

translit: kāṇu maruntuṟaiyik kāmartala meṉṟevarum pēṇu peruntuṟaiyiṟ pemmāṉē - ēṇuṭaṉkā
translation: Everyone cherishes this beautiful place as the rare realm to witness the supreme secret. O Lord of Perunthurai!
commentary: Perunthurai is cherished as the place where the supreme divine secret is revealed. Here the great saint Manikkavasagar experienced God's grace directly.

translit: īṭṭum perunaṟaiyā ṟeṉṉa vayalōṭi nāṭṭum perunaṟaiyūr nampaṉē - kāṭṭum
translation: O Lord of Perunaraiyur, where gathered nectar flows through the fields like a great river.
commentary: Nectar runs through the fields of Perunaraiyur like a great river. That richness points to the sweetness of the holy presence there.

translit: pariciṟ karaippuṟṟōr pāṅkupeṟa vōṅkum ariciṟ karaipputtūrāṉē - taricaṉattek
translation: O Lord of Putthur on the banks of the Arisil river. You stand tall to reveal your blessings, allowing those who reach the shore of refuge to attain greatness.
commentary: At Putthur on the Arisil river, the Lord is a steady shore for seekers. Anyone looking for refuge finds a safe harbor there, and greatness.

translit: kāluñ civapurattaik kātalittōr taṅkaḷtuti ēluñ civapuratti lemmāṉē - māluṅkoḷ
translation: O our Lord in Sivapuram. You accept the praises of those who constantly long for the vision of Siva's realm.
commentary: Sivapuram means the city of Siva. God warmly receives the devotion of those who spend their lives longing to see it.

translit: veppuṅ kalaiyanallōr meṉmaturac coṉmālai ceppuṅ kalayanallūrc ciṉmayaṉē - ceppamuṭaṉ
translation: O embodiment of pure consciousness in Kalayanallur. The virtuous recite garlands of gentle and sweet words to dispel the burning fever of delusion.
commentary: In Kalayanallur God is pure consciousness itself. The virtuous sing him sweet words of praise, and that singing clears the mind of confusion and worldly fever.

translit: ōṅkun tiruttoṇṭar uḷkuḷira nallaruḷāl tāṅkuṅ karukkuṭivāḻ caṅkaraṉē - āṅkakaṉan
translation: O Shankara residing in Karukkudi. With perfect and good grace you sustain the exalted holy devotees and make their hearts rejoice.
commentary: Shankara, a traditional name for Siva, means the bringer of peace. In Karukkudi his grace sustains true devotees and fills their hearts with deep joy.

translit: tāñciyattaivēṅkait talaiyāṟ ṟaṭukkiṉṟa vāñciyattiṉ mēvu maṟaiyōṉē - āñciyilā
translation: O Lord of the Vedas dwelling in Vanchiyam, you ward off danger with the head of a tiger.
commentary: At Vanchiyam the Lord guards his devotees from danger. The tiger's head recalls an old story in which Siva subdued a fierce beast sent to attack him.

translit: tinnilattum vāṉāti yennilattu mōṅkuperu naṉṉilattu vāḻñāṉa nāṭakaṉē - maṉṉumalar
translation: O Dancer of wisdom dwelling in the great flourishing Nannilam, you rise without fading in this world, in the heavens, and in all other realms.
commentary: Nannilam is the shrine greeted here. God is the dancer of wisdom, and his presence fills the earth, the heavens and every other world without ever fading.

translit: vaṇṭīc curampāṭi vārmatuvuṇ ṭuḷkaḷikkuṅ koṇṭīc curattamarnta kōmāṉē - kaṇṭīca
translation: O King seated in Kondichuram, where bees sing musical notes, drink the flowing nectar, and rejoice in their hearts.
commentary: Kondichuram overflows with joy. Its bees sing as they drink nectar from the flowers, and they mirror the bliss of souls drinking in divine grace.

translit: naṇpaṉaiyū raṉpukaḻum nampaveṉa umpartoḻat taṇpaṉaiyūr mēvuñ caṭātaraṉē - paṇpuṭaṉē
translation: O Lord with matted hair dwelling in cool Panaiyur, the celestials worship you, crying out, 'O reliable Lord praised by the loving town.'
commentary: At cool, shaded Panaiyur the heavenly beings bow down. They praise the Lord as the dependable refuge for all who seek grace with love.

translit: eṟkuṭiyā ṉaṅkoṇ ṭirukka makiḻntaḷitta viṟkuṭiyiṉ vīraṭṭa mēyavaṉē - coṟkoṭiya
translation: O Lord dwelling in Virattam of Virkudi, you joyfully granted me a physical form to live here with noble qualities.
commentary: At Virkudi, Vallalar thanks the Lord for the gift of a human body. It is given so the soul can live a noble life and seek spiritual truth.

translit: vaṉpukalā neñciṉ maruvum orutakaimait teṉpukalūr vāḻmakā tēvaṉē - iṉpamaṟai
translation: O Great Lord who lives in beautiful Pukalur, you abide with a singular nature in hearts completely free of cruelty. The blissful Vedas'
commentary: God makes a home in hearts that hold no cruelty. Vallalar calls him the Great Lord of Pukalur, a sacred town in Tamil Nadu. The line spills into the next one, starting a thought about the ancient scriptures known as the Vedas.

translit: arttamā nīkkariya vātāra mākiniṉṟa varttamā nēccarattu vāyntavaṉē - mittaiyuṟṟa
translation: meaning, you stand as the inseparable foundation. O Lord who dwells in Vardhamaneswaram. The illusion-bound
commentary: God is the true meaning and foundation of the ancient scriptures. The text calls on the Lord enshrined at Vardhamaneswaram, naming the divine as the solid base beneath all sacred knowledge.

translit: kāmaṉatī caṅkeṭavē kaṇpārt taruḷceyta rāmaṉatī campeṟuni rāmayaṉē - tōmuṇ
translation: Kama saw his supremacy perish when you looked at him and bestowed your grace. O flawless Lord of Ramanatheeswaram. The faulty
commentary: Kama is the god of desire. Old stories tell how Siva opened his third eye and burned him to ashes. Vallalar counts that destruction of worldly lust as grace from the flawless Lord of Ramanatheeswaram.

translit: mayaṟṟūr paṟitta maṉattil viḷainta payaṟṟūr ticaiyam paraṉē - iyaṟṟuñcīr
translation: root of delusion is plucked out in the mind where you manifest. O supreme Lord of Payatrur. Abounding in excellent
commentary: Once the Lord enters the mind, the deep roots of confusion and delusion come up completely. Vallalar celebrates that clarity by calling on the supreme Lord of Payatrur.

translit: ācciramē vuñceṅkāṭ ṭaṅkuṭiyi ṉaṅkaṇapa tīccaramvā ḻuñcantra cēkaraṉē - ēccakala
translation: fame, you reside in the Ganapatheeswaram shrine of Tiruchengattangudi. O Chandrasekara, to dispel all reproach
commentary: Another famous temple now, the Ganapatheeswaram shrine in Tiruchengattangudi. The name Chandrasekara means the Lord who wears the crescent moon in his hair.

translit: viṇmaruvi ṉōṉai viṭanīkka nallaruḷcey vaṇmarukal māṇikka vaṇṇaṉē - tiṇmaikoṇṭa
translation: O ruby-colored Lord of flourishing Marugal, you granted your good grace to remove the poison from the man who had died and reached the heavens.
commentary: Marugal remembers a famous miracle. A man died of a snakebite, and the Lord's grace drew out the poison and brought him back to life. Vallalar praises this ruby-colored Lord, whose compassion can reverse even death.

translit: māttamaṅkai yuḷḷam maruvip piriyāta cāttamaṅkaik kaṅkaic caṭāmuṭiyōy - tūttakaiya
translation: O Lord of Sathamangai wearing the river Ganga in your matted hair, you abide forever without separating from the steadfast heart of the great Goddess.
commentary: At Sathamangai, Siva wears the rushing Ganga in his matted hair. He never leaves the steadfast heart of the Goddess, and the two stay in perfect, unbroken harmony.

translit: pākaikkā reṉṉum paṇimoḻiyār vāḻttōvā nākaikkā rōṇam nayantōṉē - ōkaiyaṟa
translation: O Lord who joyfully resides in Nagai Karonam, you are ceaselessly praised by women whose gentle words are sweeter than pure syrup.
commentary: Next comes the coastal shrine of Nagai Karonam. Devoted women praise the Lord there without pause, their words sweet as syrup, and such gentle, joyful devotion pleases God.

translit: vikkal varuṅkāl viṭāytīrt tulakiṭainī cikkaleṉuñ cikkal tiṟalōṉē - mikkamiṉār
translation: O mighty Lord of Sikkal, you quench our thirst when joy fades and the dying gasps come, resolving all the worldly tangles we face.
commentary: Sikkal means a tangle in Tamil, and Vallalar plays on the name. The Lord of this shrine untangles the messy attachments of worldly life. He also quenches the soul's thirst at death, when the final gasps arrive.

translit: vāḷūr taṭaṅkaṇ vayalkāṭṭi yōṅkuṅkīḻ vēḷūriṟ ceṅkaṇ viṭaiyōṉē - nīḷuvakaip
translation: O Lord mounted on the red-eyed bull in lofty Keezhvelur, you stand amidst fertile fields where radiant women with wide sword-like eyes dwell.
commentary: Keezhvelur is fertile country. The Lord rides his red-eyed bull there, among the fields and the radiant devotees, watching over the thriving life of the world.

translit: pāvū ricaiyiṟ payaṉcuvaiyiṟ pāṅkuṭaiya tēvūr vaḷartēva tēvaṉē - pūviṉiṭai
translation: O God of gods who flourishes in Thevur, possessing the beauty of songs, the melody, and the sweet taste of their meaning. Amidst flowers,
commentary: Thevur's God is the very essence of music and poetry. He is found in the melody, in the beauty of the songs, and in the sweetness of what they mean.

translit: ikkūṭaṉ mainta viṉikkūṭa leṉṟupaḷḷi mukkūṭaṉ mēviyamar muṉṉavaṉē - takkaneṭun
translation: O primal one who abides in Pallimukkudal, saying, "Let us unite now, O son of this Kudal." Fitting and tall,
commentary: The primal one calls out to the devotee and invites him to unite. Vallalar places that welcoming voice in the sacred town of Pallimukkudal.

translit: tērū raṇivītic cīrūr maṇimāṭa ārūri leṅkaḷ arumaruntē - nīrūrnta
translation: O our rare nectar in Tiruvarur, possessing glorious gem-studded mansions and beautiful streets where chariots roll. Water-laden,
commentary: In the grand temple city of Tiruvarur, God is a rare, healing nectar. The splendor of its streets and mansions reflects how precious the One who lives there is.

translit: kārūr poḻiluṅ kaṉiyīn tiḷaippakaṟṟum ārū raraṉeṟivē ḷāṇmaiyē - ērārnta
translation: O bountiful Lord of Araneri in Tiruvarur, where dark clouds gather over groves that yield fruit to relieve fatigue. Beautiful,
commentary: At the Araneri shrine in Tiruvarur, God is the generous provider. Groves that give fruit to tired travelers picture his grace lifting our exhaustion.

translit: maṇmaṇ ṭalikar maruvumā rūrpparavai uṇmaṇ ṭali em uṭaimaiyē - tiṇmaik
translation: O our treasure who dwells in the heart of Paravai in Tiruvarur, approached by the kings of the earth. Strong,
commentary: Even the kings of the earth seek this treasure. Vallalar recalls the old stories of Tiruvarur and praises God as the beloved presence dwelling deep in the heart of the saintly woman Paravai.

translit: kaḷamar makiḻak kaṭaiciyar pāṭum viḷamar koḷumem viruppē - vaḷamai
translation: You are our desire residing in Vilamar, where peasant women sing to the delight of the farmers.
commentary: Vilamar is a scene of rural harmony, where the working women sing and the farmers are glad. Vallalar calls the Lord our desire, dwelling in that peaceful place.

translit: erukkaravī rañcē reḻilvēṇi koṇṭu tirukkaravī rañcēr ciṟappē - urukka
translation: You are the eminent one of Thirukkaraveeram, bearing beautiful matted hair adorned with the calotropis flower, a snake, and the wetness of the river.
commentary: At Thirukkaraveeram the Lord bears the classic marks of Siva. His matted hair holds wild things, the common calotropis flower, a coiled snake and the wetness of the river Ganga. He wears them as beautiful ornaments.

translit: varuvēḷūr māvellā māvēṟuñ cōlaip peruvēḷūr iṉpap perukkē - karumai
translation: You are the flood of bliss in Peruvelur, where beetles swarm all the great trees in the groves.
commentary: Peruvelur is lush, its groves alive with buzzing beetles. There the divine is felt as a huge flood of bliss.

translit: milaiyālaṅ kāṭṭu miṭaṟṟāyeṉ ṟēttum talaiyālaṅ kāṭṭut takavē - nilaikoḷ
translation: You are the worthy one of Thalaiyalangadu, praised by devotees who say, "O Lord whose throat displays the dark poison."
commentary: Devotees at Thalaiyalangadu praise the Lord for his dark throat. In the old story he swallowed a deadly cosmic poison to save all living beings, and the dark mark stayed on his neck as an eternal sign of compassion.

translit: taṭavāyil veṇmaṇikaḷ caṅkaṅka ḷīṉum kuṭavāyil aṉpar kuṟippē - maṭavāṭkōr
translation: You are the focus of the devotees in Kudavayil, where conches yield white pearls at the wide water-gates.
commentary: The waters of Kudavayil are so rich that conches yield white pearls. Amid all that outward wealth, the devotees keep their attention wholly on God.

translit: kūṟaiyuvantaḷitta kōvēyeṉ ṟaṉpartoḻac cēṟai yuvantirunta ciṟparamē - vēṟupaṭāp
translation: Devotees worship you and call you the King who gladly granted the garments. O Supreme Consciousness, you joyfully abide in Cherai.
commentary: God dwells in Cherai as pure consciousness. Devotees praise him as a generous king who provides even their clothing, and who gives them spiritual refuge as well.

translit: pālūr nilaviṟ paṇilaṅkaḷ taṇkatircey nālūril aṉparpeṟu naṉṉayamē - mēlūrum
translation: You are the pure grace received by devotees in Nalur, a town where conches radiate cool beams in the milk-white moonlight.
commentary: White conches glowing in milky moonlight are how Vallalar pictures the grace devotees receive at Nalur. It is cool, pure and soothing.

translit: nōykkaraiyuṭ ceyyāta nōṉmaiyōr cūḻntakaṭu vāykkaraiyuṇ mēvukiṉṟa vaṇmaiyē - vāytta
translation: O generous Lord, you dwell in Kaduvaykkarai, surrounded by steadfast ascetics who never fall onto the shores of spreading disease.
commentary: At Kaduvaykkarai the Lord lives among disciplined seekers. Their steady practice keeps them clear of worldly affliction and holds them firm in his generosity.

translit: perumpūkan teṅkiṟ piṟaṅka vaḷaṅkoḷḷum irumpūḷai mēvi yiruntōy - virumpum
translation: You reside in Irumpulai, a shrine richly flourishing with tall areca palms and coconut trees.
commentary: Irumpulai is fertile ground, ringed by towering areca and coconut palms. The abundance of these temple towns mirrors the spiritual wealth waiting for anyone who seeks it.

translit: viratap perumpāḻi viṇṇavarka ḷēttum arataip perumpāḻi ārntōy - caratattāl
translation: You dwell in Aratai Perumpazhi, praised by celestial beings who uphold great and powerful vows.
commentary: Even celestial beings come to Aratai Perumpazhi to praise him. They keep strict vows just to experience the presence that dwells there.

translit: ētum avaṇivaṇeṉ ṟeṇṇā tavariṟaiñci ōtum avaḷivaṇal lūruṭaiyōy - kōtakaṉṟa
translation: Lord of beautiful Avalivanallur, you are praised by those who bow and chant without distinguishing between here and there.
commentary: Vallalar names a real shrine, Avalivanallur, and praises the Lord who dwells there. Yet the ones who worship best are those who make no division between "here" and "there," because they know God is everywhere.

translit: nīṭṭuñ curuti niyamattōrk kiṉṉaruḷai nīṭṭum pariti niyamattōy - kāṭṭiyanan
translation: Lord of Parithiniyamam, you extend your sweet grace to those who stand steadfast in the faultless and expansive Vedas.
commentary: At Parithiniyamam the Lord extends sweet grace to those who hold steady in spiritual discipline. They have given themselves to the wide wisdom of the scriptures, and grace meets them there.

translit: tēvaṉū reṉṟu ticaimukaṉmāl vāḻttukiṉṟa pūvaṉūr mēvum pukaḻuṭaiyōy - pūvalakām
translation: Renowned Lord residing in Poovanur, praised by Brahma and Vishnu as the city of the supreme God.
commentary: Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver are great gods in their own right. Even they praise Poovanur as the true dwelling of the highest God.

translit: īṅkumpā tāḷamuta levvulaku meññāṉṟun tāṅkumpā tāḷēc carattamarntōy - ōṅkuputti
translation: Lord of Pathaleeswaram, you forever sustain this earthly world, the underworld, and all other worlds.
commentary: Everything rests on this power. At Pathaleeswaram God is worshipped as the one who forever holds up the earth, the underworlds and every other world there is.

translit: māṉkaḷari lōṭṭi makiḻvō ṭiruntēttum vāṉkaḷaril vāḻu maṟaimuṭipē - mēṉmaitarum
translation: Crown of the Vedas residing in Vankalar, you are joyfully praised by people of exalted intellect who have cast away all faults.
commentary: Wisdom starts with clearing the mind of its faults. People who have reached that purity praise God at Vankalar with joy, as the Crown of the Vedas, the truth that stands above all written scripture.

translit: muṟṟēmam vāynta muṉivar tiṉamparavum ciṟṟēmam vāynta ceḻuṅkatirē - kaṟṟavarkaḷ
translation: O rich ray of light abiding in Thiruchitremam, praised daily by fully mature sages! The learned ones
commentary: A rich ray of light abides at Thiruchitremam. Sages who have reached full spiritual maturity worship it every day.

translit: eṅkumucāt tāṉa miruṅkaḻaka maṉṟamutal taṅkumucāt tāṉat taṉimutalē - poṅkupava
translation: gather everywhere in great assemblies and halls of inquiry. O peerless First Lord of Thiruvusathanam! The swelling
commentary: Thiruvusathanam's Lord is peerless, the First. The town is alive with seeking: learned people gather in great halls to inquire into the truth.

translit: vallaliṭum pāvanatta maṭṭoḷicey kiṉṟatiru mallaliṭum pāvaṉattu māṭcimaiyē - tollaip
translation: afflictions of sinful worldly existence are destroyed. O majesty of Thiruppavanam, radiating light and bringing sacred abundance! The ancient
commentary: At Thiruppavanam the Lord's presence is a radiant majesty. It destroys the deep suffering of worldly life and leaves sacred abundance in its place.

translit: paṭikkuḷ nōvāta paṇpuṭaiyōr vāḻttum kaṭikkuḷat taṉpar kaḷippē - kaṭikkuḷattiṉ
translation: world holds people of gentle nature who do not cause pain, and they praise you. O joy of the devotees in Thirukkadikulam! As bees swarm in the fragrant
commentary: The Lord of Thirukkadikulam is the joy of His devotees. Those who praise Him there are known by their gentle nature and their absolute refusal to cause pain to any living being.

translit: vaṇṭalaikkat tēṉalariṉ vārntōr taṭamākkum taṇṭalaikkuḷ nīṇeṟiccin tāmaṇiyē - koṇṭaleṉa
translation: blossoms, honey pours out to form a pool within the cool groves. O wish-fulfilling gem of Thiruthandalaineeneri! Like a cloud
commentary: The Lord of Thiruthandalaineeneri is the legendary gem that grants every wish. The place itself mirrors that rich grace, with nectar spilling from the flowers and pooling in the cool groves.

translit: maṉkōṭṭūr cōlai vaḷarkōṭṭūr taṇpaḻaṉat teṉkōṭṭūr tēva cikāmaṇiyē - teṉkūṭṭip
translation: O crest-jewel of the gods in the beautiful southern Kottaiyur, with its enduring groves, flourishing forests, and cool fields.
commentary: Kottaiyur is a southern town rich in groves and cool fields, and its Lord is the crest-jewel of the gods. Calling Him a jewel puts His radiant worth above everything else.

translit: pōyvaṇ ṭuṟaitaṭamum pūmpoḻiluñ cūḻntamarar āyveṇ ṭumaṟaimāci lāmaṇiyē - tōyvuṇṭa
translation: O flawless gem praised by the pure Vedas and sought by the immortals, residing in the shrine surrounded by beautiful flower groves and ponds where bees gather.
commentary: A flawless gem (mācilā maṇi), sought by the immortals and praised by the pure Vedas. Bees gather at the flower groves and ponds around the shrine, and that easy harmony reflects the perfect peace of His presence.

translit: kaḷḷampū tātinilai kaṇṭuṇarvu koṇṭavarcūḻ koḷḷampū tūrvāṉ kulamaṇiyē - veḷḷiṭaivāṉ
translation: O supreme gem of Kollampoothur, surrounded by realized sages who have understood the true nature of the elements and dispelled all deceit.
commentary: Realized sages surround the Lord at Kollampoothur. They have understood the true nature of the elements and cleared every trace of deceit from their minds. Real spiritual wisdom asks for that complete inner honesty.

translit: vāmpē reyiṟcūḻnta māṇpāṟ ṟirunāmam āmpē reyiloppi lāmaṇiyē - tāmpērā
translation: O incomparable gem of Pereyil, beautifully enclosed by great fortress walls that rise high into the open sky.
commentary: Pereyil is famous for its fortress walls rising into the open sky. Its Lord is praised as the incomparable gem (oppilā maṇi), a treasure nothing in the physical world can match.

translit: vīṭṭilaṉpa rāṉantam mēvac ceyuṅkoḷḷik kāṭṭi lamarnta-eṉkaṇ kāṭciyē - nīṭṭumoḷi
translation: O vision of my eyes seated in Kollikkadu, you make your devotees experience supreme bliss in the unwavering state of liberation.
commentary: Vallalar calls the Lord of Kollikkadu the vision of his own eyes. That light gives devotees the supreme joy of liberation (vīṭu), a lasting bliss no worldly pleasure can offer.

translit: āṅkū rilaivē lavaṉā tiyarcūḻat tēṅkūril vāḻtēva ciṅkamē - ōṅkumalai
translation: O Divine Lion dwelling in the sweet town of Tēṅkūr, surrounded by the spear-wielding Murugan and the other gods!
commentary: At Tēṅkūr the Lord is a lion, ruler over all. Even Murugan with his spear and the other gods gather around him to serve and honor the source of grace.

translit: vallikkā tāra maṇippuyaveṉ ṟaṉpartoḻa nellikkā vāḻmeyn niyamamē - elalkaṇ
translation: O true Principle dwelling in Tirunellikkā, worshiped by devotees who praise your beautiful jeweled shoulders that support the goddess of the high mountain!
commentary: At Tirunellikkā he is the absolute truth. Devotees praise the strong shoulders that bear the goddess of the high mountain, and in that image the supreme reality and its nurturing grace are never apart.

translit: cēṭṭiyat tāṉē terintucurar vantēttu nāṭṭiyat tāṉkuṭivāḻ nalliṉamē - nāṭṭumoru
translation: O noble One dwelling in Tirunāṭṭiyattāṉkuṭi! Understanding the greatness of the goddess with eyes dark as night, the celestials come and offer you praise.
commentary: The celestials come to Tirunāṭṭiyattāṉkuṭi because they have grasped the power of the goddess with night-dark eyes. Understanding her grace is how one rightly approaches the Lord.

translit: nūṟāyi laṉpartamai nōkki yaruḷceytiruk kāṟāyiṉ mēlōr kaṭaippiṭiyē - vīṟākum
translation: O ultimate ideal of the great sages in Tirukkāṟāyil! You look upon hundreds of thousands of steadfast devotees and bestow your grace upon them.
commentary: The sages of Tirukkāṟāyil hold him as their highest aim. That aim is generous. He looks on devotees by the countless thousands and gives grace to every one.

translit: iṉṟāppūr vantoṭ ṭiruntativvū reṉṉavuyar kaṉṟāppūr pañcāk karapporuḷē - tuṉṟācai
translation: O essence of the five sacred syllables in exalted Tirukkaṉṟāppūr! Your majestic glory makes people say that the town of Āppūr has come today and merged with this place.
commentary: The five sacred syllables (Na-ma-shi-va-ya) are the central prayer of the Saiva tradition, and the Lord of Tirukkaṉṟāppūr is what they mean. His glory is so great that it seems to pull the glory of other sacred towns into itself, as if Āppūr had come today and merged with this place.

translit: veyya valivalattai vīṭṭiyaṉpark kiṉṉaruḷcey tuyya valivalattuc coṉmuṭipē - naiyumaṉa
translation: O ultimate crown of words in pure Valivalam! You destroy cruel karmic forces and grant sweet grace to devotees.
commentary: At Valivalam the Lord is the crown of all words, the highest truth speech can reach. He breaks the cruel weight of past actions and gives sweet grace to those who seek him.

translit: maicciṉattai viṭṭōr maṉattiṟ cuvaikoṭuttuk kaicciṉatti ṉuṭkaraiyāk kaṟkaṇṭē - neṟcumakka
translation: O rock candy that does not dissolve in the palm's heat! You grant sweetness in the minds of those who have cast away the dark anger of their suffering minds.
commentary: Rock candy that will not melt in a warm palm. That is how pure and lasting the Lord's sweetness is, and Vallalar says only those who have let go of their mental darkness and anger get to taste it.

translit: āḷilaiyeṉ ṟārūra ṉārtutikkat tantaruḷum kōḷiliyiṉ aṉparkulaṅ koḷḷuvappē - nīḷulakam
translation: O joy embraced by the lineage of devotees in Kōḷili! When Ārūrar sang your praise saying he had no men to carry his paddy, you graciously provided them.
commentary: Ārūrar is the saint Sundarar. At Kōḷili he had harvested paddy and no men to carry it, so he sang to the Lord, who at once sent divine helpers to bear the load. God answers the practical, everyday needs of his devotees too.

translit: kāymūrkka rēṉuṅ karutiṟ katikoṭukkum vāymūrk kamainta maṟaikkoḻuntē - nēyamuṇat
translation: O tender shoot of the Vedas presiding in Vāymūr! If even the fiercely angry fools of this vast world think of you, you grant them liberation.
commentary: No one is shut out of this grace. Even the most foolish, fiercely angry people in the world are given spiritual freedom if they simply turn their thoughts toward him.

translit: tēṭeliyai mūvulakun tērntutoḻac ceytaruḷum īṭiṉmaṟaik kāṭṭileṉṟaṉ eyppilvaippē - nāṭumeṉai
translation: O my reserve treasure in incomparable Maṟaikkāṭṭu! You graciously elevated the mouse that sought to consume the temple lamp's ghee, making the three worlds revere it.
commentary: Vallalar calls God his treasure saved up for times of weariness. The old legend of Maṟaikkāṭṭu tells of a hungry mouse that went for the ghee in a dying temple lamp. Tugging at the wick, it made the flame burn brighter without meaning to. For that tiny, accidental service God had it reborn as a great ruler honored across the three worlds.

translit: niṉṉakatti yāṉpaḷḷi nērntēṉeṉ ṟāṭkoṇṭa teṉṉakatti yāṉpaḷḷic cempoṉṉē - toṉṉeṟiyōr
translation: O pure gold of the southern shrine of Tirunagappalli. You took me as your own, declaring, "I have chosen your inner heart as my resting place." The followers of the ancient path
commentary: The Lord tells Vallalar he has chosen Vallalar's own heart as his resting place. The praise is for the temple of Tirunagappalli, yet the deeper revelation is this inner closeness. The highest shrine is the human heart.

translit: nāṭik kuḻaka nalamaruḷeṉ ṟēttukiṉṟa kōṭik kuḻakararuṭ kōlamē - nīṭulakil
translation: seek you and praise you, crying, "O beautiful Lord, grant us goodness." O gracious form of the beautiful Lord of Tirukkodi. In this vast world,
commentary: The seekers of the ancient path pray to the Lord of Tirukkodi for goodness, and he shows himself to them as a form made wholly of radiant grace.

translit: nāṭṭum pukaḻīḻa nāṭṭiṟ pavaviruḷai vāṭṭun tirukkōṇa māmalaiyāy - vēṭṭulakiṉ
translation: within the renowned land of Eelam, you are the great mountain of Tirukonamalai that scorches the darkness of worldly birth. Desiring it in this world,
commentary: Now the song crosses to Sri Lanka, historically called Eelam, and the great mountain temple of Tirukonamalai. There the Lord is a fire that burns away the darkness of worldly ignorance.

translit: mūtīc carameṉṟu muṉṉōr vaṇaṅkutiruk kētīc carattiṟ kiḷarkiṉṟōy - ōtukiṉṟōr
translation: the ancients worshipped it as the primeval shrine of the Lord. You shine in that Tiruketheeswaram. Those who pray to you
commentary: Tiruketheeswaram is another revered temple in Sri Lanka, and the Lord shines there too. The wise ancestors worshipped it as a primeval home of the divine.

translit: pālavāy niṟkum paraiyōṭu vāḻmaturai ālavāyc cokkaḻakā ṉantamē - cīlartamaik
translation: are supported by the supreme Goddess who stands by their side. You dwell with her in Madurai. O pure bliss, O beautiful Chokkanathar of Aalavaay. The virtuous ones
commentary: In Madurai the Lord dwells as beautiful Chokkanathar with the supreme Goddess. She stands close beside those who pray and gives them her active support. Here he is pure, boundless bliss.

translit: kāppaṉū rillāk karuṇaiyā leṉṟupukum āppaṉūr mēvucatā ṉantamē - māppulavar
translation: O eternal bliss dwelling in Appanur, entered forever through unmatched protecting grace. Great poets...
commentary: At Appanur the divine is known as pure, eternal bliss. No one gets there by effort alone, since it rests entirely on God's unmatched protecting grace.

translit: ñāṉaparaṅ kuṉṟameṉa naṇṇimakiḻ kūrntētta vāṉaparaṅ kuṉṟaliṉpā ṉantamē - vāṉavarkōṉ
translation: approach with abounding joy and praise it as the supreme mountain of wisdom. O sweet bliss of the heavenly supreme mountain Parankundram. The king of the celestials...
commentary: Great poets and seekers praise the hill of Parankundram as a towering mountain of divine wisdom. There, wisdom is tasted directly as sweet joy.

translit: tēmē ṭakattaṉoṭu cītaraṉum vāḻttuñcī rāmē ṭakattaṟivā ṉantamē - pūmītil
translation: Brahma on the sweet lotus and Vishnu praise the glorious Edakam. O bliss of consciousness in excellent Edakam. On this earth...
commentary: At Edakam even Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver honor the supreme presence. There God shows himself as the pure bliss of awakened consciousness.

translit: naṟṟavaruṅ kaṟṟa navacitta rumvāḻtti uṟṟakoṭuṅ kuṉṟattem ūtiyamē - muṟṟukatir
translation: virtuous ascetics and learned new siddhas praise and reach Kodunkundram. O our great reward in Kodunkundram. The fully radiant...
commentary: Virtuous ascetics and the mystics called siddhas gather at Kodunkundram to offer praise. After all their hard discipline, the reward they find is the divine presence itself.

translit: ittūra maṉṟi yiṉittūra millaiyeṉap puttūr varumaṭiyār pūrippē - cittāyntu
translation: O fulfilling joy of the devotees who arrive in Puttur, saying there is no distance left to travel beyond this. Having examined the mind...
commentary: Arriving at Puttur, the devotees feel their long search is over. There is nowhere farther to go, they say, and they find fulfillment in the divine presence right where they stand.

translit: nāmīca rākum nalantarumeṉ ṟumpartoḻum rāmīcamvāḻcīva rattiṉamē - pūmītu
translation: O living gem residing in Rameswaram, worshipped by celestials who proclaim you grant the goodness of becoming the Lord. On this earth,
commentary: At the temple town of Rameswaram the divine presence is a living gem. Vallalar says the heavenly beings worship it to attain the highest spiritual state.

translit: nīṭāṉai cūḻum nilamaṉṉar vāḻttutiru vāṭāṉai mēvukaru ṇākaramē - cēṭāṉa
translation: O form of compassion dwelling in Thiruvadanai, praised by earthly kings surrounded by tall elephants. The exalted
commentary: At Thiruvadanai the divine is pure compassion. Even mighty kings with great armies of elephants bow down to it.

translit: vāṉappē rāṟṟai matiyai muṭicūṭuṅ kāṉappēr āṉantak kāḷaiyē - mōṉaruḷē
translation: O blissful youth of Thirukkanapper, wearing the great celestial river and the moon on your crown. O silent grace,
commentary: At Thirukkanapper the divine takes the form of a joyful youth. He wears the crescent moon and the celestial Ganges on his crown, the traditional marks of Lord Siva.

translit: pūvaṇamum pūmaṇamum pōlava marntatirup pūvaṇattil āṉantap pokkiṣamē - tīvaṇattil
translation: O treasure of bliss in Thiruppuvanam, abiding like the color and fragrance of a flower. In the hue of fire,
commentary: Thiruppuvanam's Lord is like the color and scent of a flower. Grace sits in existence the way those sit in a petal, woven all through it and never apart.

translit: kaṇcuḻiya leṉṟu karuṇaiyaḷit teṉṉuḷañcēr taṇcuḻiyal vāḻcīva cākṣiyē - paṇceḻippak
translation: O witness of the soul residing in cool Thiruchuzhi, who entered my heart, granting compassion and telling my eyes not to weep. As the melody flourishes,
commentary: At Thiruchuzhi the divine enters Vallalar's heart directly to comfort him. He calls God the inner witness of the soul (jīva sākṣi), a loving presence that wipes away his tears and tells him not to weep.

translit: kaṟṟālaṅ kuṇmaik katitarumeṉ ṟaṟṟavarcūḻ kuṟṟālat taṉpar kutukalippē - poṟṟāma
translation: Surrounded by renunciates who declare that studying there grants the true path, O joyous ecstasy of the devotees of Kurralam!
commentary: Kurralam is famous for its waterfalls and its long spiritual traditions. Ascetics who have given up worldly attachments gather there, holding that study in such a holy place opens the way to freedom. Vallalar calls the divine presence there the sheer, bubbling joy of the devotees.

translit: nalvēli cūḻntu nayaṉpeṟumoṇ ceñcāli nelvēli uṇmai nilayamē - valvēlai
translation: O true abode at Nelveli, where bright red paddy yields goodness surrounded by a fine fence of golden rays!
commentary: The name Nelveli literally means a sacred hedge of paddy. Vallalar calls the town the true dwelling place of God, fenced by golden fields of bright red grain.

translit: nañcaik kaḷattuvaitta nātaveṉat toṇṭartoḻa añcaik kaḷañcēr aruvuruvē - neñcaṭakki
translation: O formless and formed Lord residing in Anjaikkalam, worshiped by devotees who cry out, "O Lord who placed the fierce ocean's poison in your throat!"
commentary: God is addressed as both formless and formed (aru-uruvu), a state often shown in temples by a simple rounded stone. At Anjaikkalam the devotees cry out in gratitude for his endless compassion. They remember the ancient story of the Lord swallowing the deadly poison from the churning ocean to save all living beings.

translit: āṉṟu niṟaintōrk karuḷaḷikkum pukkoḷiyūrt tōṉṟumavi nācic cuyampuvē - cāṉṟavarkaḷ
translation: O self-manifest Lord of Avinasi appearing in Pukkoliyur, granting grace to the perfected ones who have subdued their minds!
commentary: The divine light at Avinasi is self-manifest (svayambhu), meaning it appeared of itself, with no human hand shaping it. There God freely gives grace to perfected seekers who have completely quieted their minds.

translit: tammurukaṉ pūṇuṭ ṭalampōla vāḻkiṉṟa emmurukaṉ pūṇṭi irunitiyē - cemmaiyuṭaṉ
translation: O great treasure of our Muruganpundi, dwelling as the inner sanctum adorned by the melting love of the noble ones!
commentary: At Muruganpundi God is a great, hidden treasure. The presence dwells deep in the inner sanctuary, resting in the melting, tender love of noble people.

translit: aṅkuṉṟā tōṅku maṇikoḷ koṭimāṭac ceṅkuṉṟūr vāḻuñcañ cīviyē - taṅkumaṉa
translation: O life-giving elixir dwelling in Sengunrur, where tall mansions adorned with bells and flags rise undiminished. The lingering mind's
commentary: God is a life-giving elixir living in Sengunrur. Vallalar paints a prosperous temple town of tall, decorated mansions and puts that healing presence right in the middle of human life.

translit: vañcamāk kūṭal varaiyā tavarcūḻum veñcamāk kūṭal viricuṭarē - tuñcaleṉum
translation: deceitful gatherings are rejected by those who surround you, O expanding light of Venjamakkudal. The affliction called death
commentary: At Venjamakkudal God is a radiant light that keeps spreading. True devotees gather around it and turn away from the mind's deceitful habits.

translit: iṉṉa lakaṟṟa ilaṅkupavā ṉikkūṭal eṉṉu naṇāviṉiṭai iṉṉicaiyē - tuṉṉiyaruḷ
translation: is dispelled at the shining confluence of the Bhavani. O sweet music in the place called Nana. Seeking your abundant grace,
commentary: Bhavani is a sacred town where rivers meet, known in older times as Nana. There God is heard as sweet music, and that music washes away the deep sorrow of mortality.

translit: vēṇṭik koṭumuṭiyā mēṉmaipeṟu mātavarcūḻ pāṇṭik koṭumuṭiyiṟ paṇmayamē - tīṇṭariya
translation: great ascetics attain ultimate eminence and surround you, O embodiment of melody in Pandi Kodumudi. The hard-to-touch
commentary: At Pandi Kodumudi God is pure, perfect melody. Great seekers gather there to ask for grace and reach the highest state of being.

translit: veṅkaruvūr vañca viṉaitīrt tavarcūḻnta naṅkaruvūrc ceyyuḷ navaracamē - taṅkaḷaṟṟiṉ
translation: cruel womb's deceitful karma is dispelled by those who surround you, O ninefold essence of poetry in our Karuvur. Their
commentary: In Karuvur God is praised as the ninefold emotional essence of poetry itself. Those who gather there have freed themselves from past karma (the accumulated consequences of past actions) and from the painful round of rebirth in a body.

translit: tīṅkār piṟateyvat tīṅkuḻiyilvīḻntavarait tāṅkā varattuṟaiyil tāṇuvē - pūṅkuḻalār
translation: O eternal pillar at Varatturai. You lift those who have fallen into the harmful pit of other flawed deities. Women with flower-adorned hair
commentary: Vallalar describes the worship of lesser, flawed deities as a dangerous pit. He points to the divine presence at the shrine of Varatturai as a firm pillar that rescues people from this trap and guides them to the truth.

translit: vīṅkāṉai māṭañcēr viṇṇeṉ ṟakalkaṭantait tūṅkāṉai māṭac cuṭarkkoḻuntē - nīṅkātu
translation: gather in mansions vast as the sky in Kadanthai. O leaping flame of the Thoonganai Maadam shrine. Without ever departing
commentary: Here the divine is an intense, leaping flame inside the vast temple of Kadanthai. The shrine is called Thoonganai Maadam, a sanctuary built in the gentle shape of a sleeping elephant.

translit: nīṭalai yāṟṟūr niḻaṉmaṇikkuṉ ṟōṅkutiruk kūṭalai yāṟṟūrk kuṇanitiyē - nāṭiyavāṉ
translation: from holy Koodalaiyatroor, where long river waves flow and a hill of radiant gems rises. O treasure of virtues. Seeking the moon in the sky
commentary: Koodalaiyatroor is a fertile town framed by flowing river waves, and God lives there for good. He is a towering hill of radiant gems and the treasure of every good virtue.

translit: ampuliyūr cōlai yaṇivayalka ḷōṅkerukkat tampuliyūr vēta camaracamē - nampuviṭai
translation: that grazes the groves and flourishing beautiful fields of Erukkathampuliyoor. O harmonious essence of the Vedas. The trusted bull
commentary: The Vedas, the ancient sacred scriptures, teach many things. God brings them into harmony and gathers their varied teachings into one essence. That presence lives among the lush groves and fields of Erukkathampuliyoor.

translit: āṅkun tiṉaiyūrn taruḷāyeṉ ṟaṉpartoḻu tōṅkun tiṉaiyūr umāpatiyē - tīṅkuṟumoṉ
translation: is what devotees pray for you to ride to bestow your grace upon them here. O Lord of Uma at towering Thinaiyoor. The harmful
commentary: Devotees ache to meet grace directly. In lofty Thinaiyoor they pray that the Lord of Uma, the divine mother, will ride to them on his sacred bull and bless them.

translit: ṉārpurattaiveṇṇakaittī yālaḻittā yeṉṟutoḻac cōpurattiṉvāḻñāṉa tīvakamē - vārkeṭilac
translation: They worship you, declaring that you destroyed the enemies' cities with the fire of your white smile. Oh lamp of wisdom dwelling in Sopuram!
commentary: The old stories say Siva burned three demonic cities to ashes with a single fiery smile, and it cost him no effort at all. That absolute power over ignorance is why he is worshipped in holy Sopuram as the "lamp of wisdom."

translit: ceṉṉatikai yōṅkittilatavati yārparavum maṉṉatikai vīraṭṭa mātavamē - paṉṉaritām
translation: Oh great ascetic of majestic Athigai Veerattam, praised by Thilagavathiyar beside the rising waters of the flowing Kedilam river!
commentary: The Kedilam river flows past the ancient temple of Athigai Veerattam. Thilagavathiyar, a legendary woman, prayed hard at this very shrine, and her prayers guided her brother, the great saint Appar, to a life of devotion.

translit: āvalū reṅkaḷuṭai ārūra ṉārūrā nāvalūr ñāṉiyaruṇ ñāpakamē - tēvakamām
translation: Oh Lord of Aaroor, the deep unspeakable desire of our Arooran! Oh gracious memory of the sage of Navalur!
commentary: Arooran and the "sage of Navalur" are both names for Sundarar, a beloved saint of the Tamil tradition. His love for God was overwhelming and personal. God is praised as the very object of that deep desire.

translit: maṉṟa mamarnta vaḷampōṟ ṟikaḻntamutu kuṉṟa mamarnta-aruṭ koḷkaiyē - aṉṟakattiṉ
translation: Oh principle of grace abiding in Muthukundram, shining like the richness of the divine hall!
commentary: Muthukundram is the traditional name for the sacred town of Vriddhachalam. The Lord there shines outward as the pure, radiant principle of grace itself.

translit: nalveṇṇe yuṇṭoḷitta nāraṇaṉvan tēttukiṉṟa nelveṇṇey mēvuciva niṭṭaiyē - colvaṇṇam
translation: Oh pure state of Siva residing in Nelvennei! You are worshiped by Narayanan, who once secretly ate fine butter inside the house and hid.
commentary: Narayanan is Vishnu, who came to earth as Krishna, the playful child famous for secretly stealing butter. Even a god that great bows to the supreme, quiet state of the divine at Nelvennei.

translit: nāvalar pōṟṟi nalampeṟavē yōṅkutiruk kōvalūr vīraṭṭaṅ koḷparicē - āvalarmā
translation: O nature embodied in holy Kōvalūr Vīraṭṭam, which rises so the learned may praise it and attain goodness. O great one desired by eager devotees.
commentary: Kōvalūr Vīraṭṭam is an ancient temple where scholars and eager devotees gather to worship. Keep such holy places in the mind and you draw closer to real goodness.

translit: tēvā iṟaivā civaṉē yeṉumuḻakkam ōvā aṟaiyaṇinal lūruyarvē - tāvāk
translation: O eminence of Aṟaiyaṇinallūr, where the resounding cries of "O God! O Lord! O Siva!" never cease.
commentary: At Aṟaiyaṇinallūr the cries of devotees calling on God never stop. Repeating the divine names like that, without a break, keeps the mind anchored in grace.

translit: kaṭaiyāṟṟi ṉaṉpartamaik kallāṟṟi ṉīkkum iṭaiyāṟṟiṉ vāḻnal iyalpē - iṭaiyātu
translation: O good nature abiding in Iṭaiyāṟṟu, which delivers lowly devotees from the stony path of suffering without interruption.
commentary: Iṭaiyāṟṟu is known for a Lord who rescues humble seekers from harsh lives. He clears the stones of suffering from their path, and he never stops guarding them.

translit: collūraṉ ṟaṉṉait toḻumpukoḷuñ cīrveṇṇey nallū raruṭṭuṟaiyiṉ naṟpayaṉē - mallārntu
translation: O good fruit of Aruṭṭuṟai in excellent Veṇṇeynallūr, which took the eloquent Ūraṉ into its service.
commentary: Ūraṉ is the saint Sundarar. At Veṇṇeynallūr, God appeared and claimed the young saint as his lifelong servant. The story reassures us that the divine reaches out and steps into human lives.

translit: mācun tuṟaiyūr makipaṉmutal mūvaruñcīr pēcun tuṟaiyūrp piṟaicūṭī - nēcamuṟa
translation: O wearer of the crescent moon at Tuṟaiyūr, whose glory is spoken by three starting with the king of that city where abundant flaws are driven away so love may flourish.
commentary: At Tuṟaiyūr human flaws are washed away to make room for pure love. Siva wears the crescent moon there, praised by the local king, and his grace reaches everyone.

translit: vēṟṟā vaṭukū ritayatti ṉārkkeṉṟun tōṟṟā vaṭukūrc cuyañcuṭarē - āṟṟamayal
translation: Self-luminous flame of Vaṭukūr, forever unseen by those with harsh and alienated hearts.
commentary: The Lord of Vaṭukūr is a flame that lights itself, and harsh or hostile hearts cannot see it. Soften the heart first. Deep compassion is what lets a person see that inner light.

translit: kāṇik kuḻivīḻ kaṭaiyarkkuk kāṇpariya māṇik kuḻivāḻ makattuvamē - māṇuṟṟa
translation: Great majesty dwelling in Māṇikkuḻi, rarely seen by the lowest people who fall into the pit of worldly property through intense delusion.
commentary: Greed for land and property is a pit. Whoever falls into it is blinded by delusion and misses the true majesty dwelling at Māṇikkuḻi.

translit: pūppā tirikoṉṟai puṉṉaimutaṟ cūḻntilaṅkum ērppātirippuliyūr ēntalē - cīrppoliyap
translation: Lord of beautiful Pātirippuliyūr, surrounded and shining with glorious flowering trumpet, laburnum, mastwood, and other trees.
commentary: Pātirippuliyūr is known for its lush groves and flowering trees. The picture shows spiritual life flourishing right alongside the beauty and vitality of the natural world.

translit: paṇṭīc curaṉip patiyē viḻaintateṉum muṇṭīc curattiṉ muḻumutalē - peṇtakaiyār
translation: Absolute Supreme Lord of Muṇṭīccuram, a place radiating with excellence, said to be desired by the Lord in ancient times.
commentary: God is the absolute, original source of all that exists. That supreme reality still dwells in ancient places like Muṇṭīccuram, revered by seekers for generations.

translit: ērppaṉaṅkāṭ ṭūreṉ ṟirunilattōr vāḻttukiṉṟa cīrppaṉaṅkāṭ ṭūrmakiḻni kṣēpamē - cūrppuṭaitta
translation: Joyous treasure of famed Paṉaṅkāṭṭūr, praised by the people of the great earth as the beautiful Paṉaṅkāṭṭūr of noble women. You strike down all fear.
commentary: Vallalar calls the Lord of Paṉaṅkāṭṭūr a hidden treasure of joy, waiting to be found. Once a person sees that sacred presence in their own life, every worldly fear is struck down.

translit: tāmāttūr vīḻat taṭintōṉ kaṇēcaṉoṭum āmāttūr vāḻmey aruṭpiḻampē - yāmēttum
translation: Along with Vinayakar who struck down the foe to fall, O true mass of Grace dwelling in Amattur! We praise you.
commentary: Amattur holds a solid mass of divine grace. Vallalar links that grace with Vinayakar, the elephant-headed deity who clears obstacles and defeats enemies.

translit: uṇṇā mulaiyāḷ umaiyōṭu mēvutiru aṇṇā malaivāḻ aruṭcuṭarē - kaṇṇārnta
translation: O flame of Grace dwelling in holy Annamalai, residing with Uma, the Goddess Unnamulaiyal.
commentary: Annamalai is a holy mountain famous for its ancient fire temple. Siva dwells there as a flame of grace with the goddess Uma, known locally as Unnamulaiyal. The site itself is honored as a living expression of spiritual light.

translit: nākampa rāntoṇṭa nāṭṭi luyarkāñci ēkampa mēvumpē riṉpamē - ākunteṉ
translation: O supreme bliss residing in Ekambaram of exalted Kanchi in the Tondai country, which is beautiful to behold and praised by the heavens.
commentary: Ekambaram is a major temple in the ancient city of Kanchi. Vallalar treats the shrine itself as the true home of heavenly joy.

translit: kāṟṟaḷivaṇ pūmaṇattaik kāṭṭum poḻiṟkacci mēṟṟaḷivāḻ āṉanta vīṭṭuṟavē - nāṟṟamalarp
translation: The blowing south breeze and the bees reveal the fragrance of beautiful flowers in the groves of Kanchi. O joyful kinship of liberation dwelling in the Metrali temple.
commentary: Metrali is another ancient shrine in Kanchi, set in groves where the breeze carries the scent of flowers and the bees hum. Amid that beauty the Lord stands as a joyful companion who grants spiritual freedom.

translit: pūntaṇ ṭaḷivirittup pukkicaikkuñ cīrōṇa kāntaṉ ṟaḷi-aruṭpra kācamē - cērntavarkkē
translation: O light of Grace in the glorious Onakanthan Tali temple, where bees enter the fragrant blooming flowers and cool spreading shoots to sing their tunes.
commentary: At the Onakanthan Tali temple bees sing inside the open flowers. The Lord shines in that peaceful place as the pure light of grace, and the bees' song is the joy of a soul tasting it.

translit: iṅkā patañcaṟṟu millā tavaṉēka taṅkā patañcēr tayānitiyē - maṅkātu
translation: O Treasure of Compassion who reaches the singular and imperishable state, completely free from the lowly conditions of this world. Unfadingly...
commentary: The Lord is a treasure of compassion, and nothing of this world's decay or smallness touches Him. His state is single, pure, and never perishes.

translit: mecci neṟikkārva mēviniṉṟōr cūḻntatiruk kacci neṟikkāraik kāṭṭiṟaiyē - muccakamum
translation: O Lord of sacred Kacci Neṟikkāraikkāṭu, surrounded by those who praise the path and stand full of devotion. As the three worlds...
commentary: Vallalar praises the Lord enshrined at Kacci Neṟikkāraikkāṭu. The town is full of devoted seekers who rejoice in walking the spiritual path.

translit: āyuṅ kuraṅkaṇiṉmuṭ ṭappeyarkoṇ ṭōṅkupukaḻ ēyun talamvā ḻiyaṉmoḻiyē - tōyumaṉa
translation: O sweet Word who dwells in the highly renowned and fitting shrine of Kuraṅkaṇilmuṭṭam revered by the three worlds. With a mind immersed...
commentary: At the renowned shrine of Kuraṅkaṇilmuṭṭam, God is the sweet Word. The Divine speaks here, and that speech comforts and guides.

translit: yōkaṟalilāttavattō ruṉṉa viḷaṅkutiru mākaṟalil aṉparapi māṉamē - ōkaiyilā
translation: O pride of the devotees in sacred Mākaṟal, where you shine as ascetics of unbroken yoga meditate upon you. As joyless ruin...
commentary: At Mākaṟal ascetics sit in deep, unbroken yoga (spiritual union and meditation), and the Lord shines clearly in their focused minds. He is the true pride and joy of His devotees.

translit: vīttūramāvōṭa meyttavarkaḷ cūḻntatiru ōttūril vētānta uṇmaiyē - pūttaviciṉ
translation: O Truth of Vedanta in sacred Ōttūr, surrounded by true ascetics, where joyless ruin runs far away. Of the blossomed seat...
commentary: At Ōttūr the Lord is the living truth of Vedanta (the ultimate conclusion of the sacred scriptures). True ascetics gather around Him, and His pure presence drives all ruin and sorrow far away from them.

translit: ārttāṉ paṉakat tavaṉin tiraṉpukaḻvaṉ pārttāṉ paṉaṅkāṭṭūr pākkiyamē - pārttulakil
translation: The supreme fortune of Panankattur, where Indra praises the snake-adorned Lord and Arjuna beholds him.
commentary: Panankattur is a place of immense spiritual fortune. Old lore tells that Indra, king of the gods, and Arjuna, the famous warrior, came here to worship the Lord who wears serpents as ornaments.

translit: illa meṉacceṉ ṟiravā tavarvāḻum vallamaki ḻaṉpar vacittuvamē - collarikkuk
translation: The spiritual mastery of the joyful devotees in Vallam, where people live without ever approaching others to beg in poverty.
commentary: The devotees of Vallam hold great spiritual mastery (vacittuvam). Their town is one of dignity and plenty, where no one is forced into poverty or driven to beg at another's door.

translit: kāṟpēṟu kacciyiṉmuk kāṟpē ṟivaṇeṉṉum māṟpēṟṟi ṉaṉpar maṉōpalamē - ēṟpuṭaivāy
translation: The mental strength of the devotees in Thirumalperu, who declare that the Lord granted Vishnu a quarter of his grace in Kanchi and three quarters of it here.
commentary: The devotees of Thirumalperu are proud of their shrine. Their story goes that Vishnu received a quarter of the Lord's grace at the famous temple of Kanchipuram and the other three quarters right here in their own town. That claim shows how deep their devotion runs and how strong their minds are.

translit: ūṟa laṭiyā ruṟattoḻutu mēvutiru ūṟa laḻiyā uvakaiyē - māṟupaṭu
translation: The imperishable joy of Thiruural, where devotees worship intimately and attain the divine presence.
commentary: Thiruural holds a joy that never ends. Its devotees worship the Lord closely and intimately, and so they come to know His presence fully.

translit: tītu milampayaṅkōṭ ṭīreṉ ṟaṭiyarpukaḻ ōtu milampayaṅkōṭ ṭūrnalamē - tītuṭaiya
translation: The goodness of Ilampayankottur, where devotees chant praises saying they are free of evil and the Lord has dispelled their fears.
commentary: The town's name, Ilampayankottur, is linked to the dispelling of fear (payam). Its devotees chant with complete confidence, knowing the Lord has removed all evil from their lives and taken their worldly fears away.

translit: poṟkōlam āmeyiṟkup pōrkkōlam koṇṭatiru viṟkōlam mēvupara mēṭṭimaiyē - coṟpōril
translation: O supreme majesty who took up the divine bow in battle attire against the golden fortress.
commentary: Vallalar addresses God as the supreme protector who destroyed the mythical flying cities of the demons. Tradition says one of those fortresses was made of gold, and God took a mountain as His bow to strike it down. The temple celebrated here is Thiruvirkolam, a name that literally means the divine bow.

translit: ōlaṅkāṭ ṭumpaḻaiya ṉūrnīli vātaṭakkum ālaṅkāṭ ṭiṟcūḻ aruḷmayamē - ñālamcēr
translation: In the battle of words you quelled the arguments of the ghost Neeli from Pazhaiyanur who caused a great uproar. O embodiment of grace surrounding Thiruvalangadu.
commentary: Thiruvalangadu is a sacred town in Tamil Nadu with a famous local legend. A vengeful spirit named Neeli, from the nearby village of Pazhaiyanur, raised a massive uproar there. Vallalar praises God as the grace that quieted her anger and brought the region peace.

translit: mācūr akaṟṟum matiyuṭaiyōr cūḻntatirup pācūril uṇmaip parattuvamē - tēcūraṉ
translation: O true supreme reality in Thiruppachur, surrounded by the wise who join the world to remove its spreading blemishes.
commentary: At Thiruppachur God is the supreme truth, surrounded by wise people who work to heal the world and remove its flaws. Spiritual wisdom shows itself here as an active force for good in human society.

translit: kaṇpārkka vēṇṭumeṉak kaṇṭūṉṟu kōṟkoṭutta veṇpākkat taṉparpeṟum vīṟāppē - paṇpārkku
translation: When the radiant Uran asked for eyes to see, you gave him a walking stick to lean on. O great pride attained by the devotees of Venpakkam.
commentary: Uran is the saint Sundarar. When he lost his eyesight and prayed for his vision to return, God at Venpakkam gave him a walking stick to support his steps. Grace sometimes comes as the strength to endure a trial while it lasts.

translit: naḷḷip patiyē nalantarumeṉ ṟaṉparpukuṅ kaḷḷiṟ patinaṅ kaṭappāṭē - eḷḷaluṟuṅ
translation: Saying the town of Nalli brings goodness to those of noble character, devotees enter Kallil. O our ultimate duty in Kallil.
commentary: Devotees gather in the sacred town of Kallil because they know it brings goodness to those of noble character. The Lord there is their ultimate duty and their refuge.

translit: kōḷatti nīkkuṅ kuṇattōrk karuḷceytiruk kāḷatti ñāṉak kaḷañciyamē - āḷattā
translation: O treasure of wisdom in holy Kalahasti, you bestow grace upon the virtuous who remove all evils. O Father who rules me!
commentary: Kalahasti is a famous temple town in southern India, and God is its vast treasure of wisdom. He rules like a Father, granting his grace to those who live with virtue and clear evil from their hearts.

translit: veṟṟiyū reṉṉa viṉaiyēṉ viṉaitavirtta oṟṟiyūr mēviya-eṉ uḷḷaṉpē - teṟṟikaḷil
translation: O my inner love residing in Otriyur, you dispelled the karma of this karma-laden one and made it a city of victory. In the courtyards...
commentary: Now Otriyur, a temple town that mattered deeply in Vallalar's early life. He calls God his own inner love. By wiping away the heavy burden of his past actions (karma), God turns this earthly town into a place of spiritual triumph.

translit: poṅkumaṇik kālkaḷ polañceytiru voṟṟinakar taṅkuñ civapōka cāramē - puṅkavarkaḷ
translation: O essence of divine bliss residing in the holy city of Otriyur, a place adorned with radiant pillars of gold and gems. The celestials...
commentary: The radiant pillars of Otriyur are beautiful, yet the real treasure lies inside. God rests there as the pure essence of divine joy.

translit: cērntuvalaṅ koḷḷun tiruvoṟṟi yūrkkōyiṟ cārntu makiḻamuta cāramē - tērntulakar
translation: O essence of nectar dwelling joyously in the temple of holy Otriyur, where the celestials gather and circumambulate. The people of the world who realize...
commentary: God is the sweet, life-giving nectar inside the temple. Even heavenly beings gather to walk around the shrine in reverence.

translit: pōṟṟun tiruvoṟṟip pūṅkōyiṟ kuṭperiyōr cāṟṟum pukaḻvēta cāramē - ūṟṟuṟumey
translation: O essence of the Vedas, whose fame the great ones proclaim within the praised and beautiful temple of holy Otriyur. The springing true...
commentary: God is the very core of the Vedas (the ancient sacred scriptures of India). Wise elders gather in the beautiful temple at Otriyur to proclaim it.

translit: aṉpumikun toṇṭarkuḻu āyumvali tāyattil iṉpamiku ñāṉa ilakkaṇamē - tuṉpamaṟa
translation: O perfect definition of blissful wisdom, meditated upon by the assembly of devotees filled with love in Valithayam. To end all sorrow,
commentary: Valithayam is a historic temple area known today as Padi in Chennai. There the divine is the very definition of blissful wisdom, a truth devotees discover through their love.

translit: ellaivāyaṟ kuḷmaṭṭum ēkilviṉai yēkumeṉum mullaivāyiṟ kuḷvaitta muttivittē - mallalpeṟu
translation: O seed of liberation planted in Thirumullaivayil, where it is said that karma departs if one merely steps within its boundary gates. Gaining abundance,
commentary: Local tradition holds that simply stepping across the threshold of the temple at Thirumullaivoyal washes away the burden of past actions, known as karma. The Lord here is the seed of liberation, offering spiritual freedom to anyone who enters.

translit: vēṟkāṭṭa rēttutiru vēṟkāṭṭiṉ mēviyamuṉ nūṟkāṭ ṭuyarvēta nuṭpamē - pāṟkāṭṭum
translation: O subtle essence of the exalted Vedas shown in ancient texts, residing in Thiruverkadu praised by its people. Revealing milky purity,
commentary: At Thiruverkadu the Lord is the deepest truth of the ancient scriptures. Beyond their outer words, he is the subtle essence every sacred book points toward.

translit: ārttipeṟṟa mātumayi lāyppūcit tārmayilaik kīrttipeṟṟa nalvēta kītamē - kārttiraṇṭu
translation: O glorious song of the true Vedas in Mylapore, where the goddess filled with longing took the form of a peacock and worshipped. Gathering dark clouds
commentary: Mylapore takes its name from the Tamil word for peacock (mayil). In the ancient story, the goddess Parvati took the form of a peacock to worship the Lord here, and that legend still defines the temple today.

translit: vāvukiṉṟa cōlai vaḷarvāṉmi yūrttalattil mēvukiṉṟa ñāṉa vitaraṇamē - tūvimayil
translation: leap over the groves in the flourishing shrine of Thiruvanmiyur, O generous giver of wisdom residing there. The fine-feathered peacock
commentary: Thiruvanmiyur is pictured with lush groves reaching up into the rain clouds. Amid that abundance, God is the generous giver who freely grants wisdom to those who seek it.

translit: āṭum poḻiṟkaccū rālakkō yiṟkuḷaṉpar nīṭuṅ kaṉatūya nēyamē - īṭillai
translation: O vast, pure love growing in the devotees within the banyan temple at Kachur surrounded by swaying groves. "There is no equal,"
commentary: At the Kachur temple, God is the deep, pure love alive in the hearts of the devotees.

translit: eṉṉun tiruttoṇṭa rēttu miṭaiccurattiṉ maṉṉuñ civāṉanta vaṇṇamē - naṉṉeṟiyōr
translation: say the holy devotees who praise you. O enduring form of divine bliss in Idaichuram. The followers of the good path
commentary: The roll of sacred places goes on. In Idaichuram, the faithful know the divine as pure, lasting joy.

translit: tuṉṉuneṟik kōrtuṇaiyān tūyakaḻuk kuṉṟiṉiṭai muṉṉumaṟi vāṉanta mūrttamē - tuṉṉupoḻil
translation: find you as the unparalleled companion on their journey. O embodiment of the bliss of knowledge manifesting in pure Kazhukkundram. The dense groves
commentary: In Kazhukkundram, God is the companion for those walking the spiritual path. He takes form there as the sheer joy of true understanding.

translit: ammaturat tēṉpoḻiyum acciṟupāk kattulakar tammatanīk kuññāṉa cammatamē - emmatamum
translation: pour sweet honey in Achirupakkam, where you stand as the true wisdom that removes the arrogance of worldly people. Whatever faith
commentary: True wisdom destroys human arrogance. In the sweet groves of Achirupakkam, God stands as that grounding wisdom, curing worldly pride.

translit: cārntāl viṉainīkkit tāṅkutiru vakkaraiyuḷ nērntār upaniṭata niccayamē - tērntavarkaḷ
translation: they follow, if they reach you, you remove their karma and sustain them in Thiru Vakkarai. O certainty of the Upanishads revealed to those who approach you. Those who have realized
commentary: In Thiru Vakkarai, the divine removes the accumulated burdens of the past (karma) and cares for all who approach, no matter their prior religion. Vallalar calls this open grace the ultimate truth pointed to by the ancient spiritual texts (Upanishads).

translit: tatta matumatiyāṟ cārum araciliyūr uttamameyñ ñāṉa oḻukkamē - pattiyuḷḷōr
translation: O supreme conduct of true wisdom in Arasili, reached through one's own clear intellect.
commentary: At Arasili the Lord is the highest conduct of true wisdom. Vallalar says you reach it through your own intellect, once it is clear and purified enough to understand the world.

translit: eṇṇum pukaḻkoḷ irumpaimā kāḷattu naṇṇuñ civayōka nāṭṭamē - maṇṇakattuḷ
translation: O goal of Siva yoga in famous Irumbai Maakaalam, esteemed by the devoted.
commentary: At Irumbai Maakaalam, God is the goal of Siva yoga, the practice of seeking union with the divine. Devoted seekers hold that practice in high regard and look to this shrine as the center of their spiritual focus.

translit: kōpalattiṟ kāṇpariya kōkaraṇaṅ kōyilkoṇṭa māpalattu māpalamā māpalamē - tāpamilāp
translation: O supreme strength of supreme strengths enshrined in Gokarnam, hard to behold on this earth through worldly power.
commentary: At Gokarnam, God is the strength above all strengths. Worldly authority and physical force are useless for understanding or reaching it.

translit: pākiyaṟcol maṅkaiyoṭum pāṅkār paruppatattil yōkiyarka ḷēttiṭavāḻ oppuravē - pōkimutal
translation: O generosity dwelling in beautiful Paruppatham with the Goddess whose words are sweet as syrup, praised by yogis free of distress.
commentary: On the hill shrine of Paruppatham, God is generosity itself. Beside him is the Goddess, whose words are sweet as syrup and give comfort, and sages who have freed themselves from all earthly distress worship him there.

translit: pāṭiyuṟṟa nīlap paruppatattil nallōrkaḷ tēṭivaitta teyvat tilakamē - nīṭupavam
translation: O divine jewel sought and kept by the good in Neela Paruppatham, praised in song by Indra and the gods.
commentary: Neela Paruppatham holds a precious jewel, and the jewel is the Lord. Good people go looking for it and keep it safe in their hearts, singing his praise alongside the heavenly gods.

translit: taṅkā tavaṉēka taṅkā patañcērnta naṅkā talāṉa nayappuṇarvē - ciṅkātu
translation: O limitless One. O absolute One. You are the sweet union of love for us who have reached your steadfast feet.
commentary: The Lord has no limit, yet he is felt as close as love. Take refuge at his steadfast feet and you find a sweet union of affection that does not break.

translit: taṇṇiṟaintu niṉṟavartāñ cārtirukkē tārattiṟ paṇṇiṟainta kītap paṉuvalē - eṇṇiṟainta
translation: You are the undiminishing musical song filled with melody in holy Kedarnath, where those full of cool grace gather.
commentary: At holy Kedarnath, where peaceful seekers gather, God is felt as pure music. The melody runs on and never fades.

translit: cāṉṟōr vaṇaṅkunoṭit tāṉmalaiyil vāḻkiṉṟa tēṉṟōy amutac ceḻuñcuvaiyē - vāṉtōynta
translation: Countless noble ones worship you on Nodithaanmalai. You are the rich taste of honey-soaked ambrosia living on that mountain.
commentary: On the peak of Nodithaanmalai, devotees praise him as honey-soaked ambrosia (the mythical nectar of immortality). Those who worship there taste a rich spiritual sweetness.
