translation: O radiant gem-like flame, you do not abide among flawed men who engage in vain arguments. Tell me the truth of what you taught Manikkavasagar. Was it the pinnacle of the Vedas, the pinnacle of the clear Agamas, or the pinnacle of primal sound?
commentary: The highest truth shows itself to pure devotion, never to endless debate, and the flame Vallalar addresses will not stay among those who argue for the sake of it. He asks it what it taught the great saint Manikkavasagar. Was it the summit of the Vedas (ancient scriptures), of the Agamas (ritual texts), or of the primal sound of creation itself?

translit: ārkoṇṭār cēykkaṟiyiṭ ṭārē ciṟuttoṇṭap pērkoṇṭār āyiṭilem pemmāṉē - ōrtoṇṭē nāykkuṅ kaṭaippaṭṭa nāṅkaḷeṉpēm eṅkaḷmuṭai vāykkiṅ kiḵtōr vaḻakku.
translation: O our Lord, it was the devotee bearing the name Siruthondar who offered his own child as a meat dish. What single act of service can we claim, we who are lower than dogs? For our foul mouths, making such claims is merely an empty argument here.
commentary: Tradition holds that the saint Siruthondar was so devoted to feeding Siva's devotees that he cooked his own son when a guest demanded it. Set beside service like that, Vallalar finds his own efforts hollow. He calls his words empty boasting from a foul mouth and counts himself lower than a dog.

translit: kōḷkoṇṭa nañcaṅ kuṭiyēṉō kūrkoṇṭa vāḷkoṇṭu vīci maṭiyēṉō - kīḷkoṇṭa aṅkōva ṇattaḻakā ampalavā niṉpukaḻai iṅkōti vāḻttāta yāṉ.
translation: O beautiful Lord of the Hall wearing a torn loincloth! Since I do not recite and praise your glory here, should I not drink deadly poison? Should I not perish under the swing of a sharp sword?
commentary: To a true seeker, a life that does not praise God is worthless. Looking at the Lord of the Hall in his simple torn cloth, Vallalar turns hard on himself. If he fails to sing that glory, he might as well swallow poison or fall to a sword.

translit: āyāk koṭiyēṉuk kaṉpuṭaiyāy nī-aruḷiṅ kīyāk kuṟaiyē ilaikaṇṭāy - māyāṟkum viḷḷāt tiruvaṭikkīḻ viṇṇappam yāṉceytu koḷḷāk kuṟaiyē kuṟai.
translation: You who love even this weary, cruel one, there is no fault in You for not granting grace here. The only fault is mine, for failing to make my petition beneath Your holy feet, which remain hidden even from Vishnu.
commentary: Vallalar takes complete responsibility for feeling distant from the divine. God's love is constant, and any lack of grace is simply because the seeker has not asked for it with true and steady devotion.

translit: peṟṟiṭutāy pōlvatuniṉ peṟṟiyeṉpēṉ piḷḷaiyatu maṟṟaḻutāl kēṭṭum varātaṅkē - caṟṟirukkap peṟṟāḷ poṟuppaḷ pirāṉī poṟukkiṉuniṉ poṟṟāḷ poṟā-em pulampu.
translation: I declare Your nature is like a birth mother's. When a child weeps, a mother might hear it and stay away a little while, bearing the delay. O Lord, even if You bear it, Your golden feet will not bear our lamentation.
commentary: God's nature is like a birth mother's, who may let a crying child wail a little to teach it a lesson. Even if the Lord decides to wait, the compassion of his grace cannot bear to hear a devotee suffer.

translit: poṉpōl poṟumaiyuḷār puntiviṭāy nī-eṉpār eṉpōl poṟumaiyuḷār yārkaṇṭāy - puṉpōka allām paṭiciṉaṅkoṇ ṭāṇavañcey iṉṉāmai ellām poṟukkiṉṟēṉ yāṉ.
translation: People say You never leave the minds of those possessing golden patience. See, who has patience like mine? I endure all the misery inflicted by the ego, which rages so that base worldly experiences never leave.
commentary: Tradition teaches that God stays in the minds of those with golden patience. Vallalar points out the bitter irony. He has been far too patient already, silently enduring every misery his own ego (āṇavam) inflicts on him.

translit: muṉmaṇattil cuntararai muṉvaluvil koṇṭatupōl eṉmaṇattil nīvan tiṭāviṭiṉum - niṉkaṇattil oṉṟum orukaṇamvan tuṟṟaḻaikkil ceytataṉṟi iṉṟum orumaṇañcey vēṉ.
translation: You might not come to my wedding and forcibly claim me, as You once claimed Sundarar at his wedding. Yet if a member of Your divine host arrives for a moment and calls me, I will cancel this arrangement and hold a different wedding today.
commentary: Tamil tradition remembers how Sundarar's earthly wedding was interrupted when God arrived and claimed him by force. Vallalar does not ask for that much. If even one of God's host calls him for a moment, he will drop every worldly tie at once and hold a different wedding today, a true spiritual union.

translit: ceyyār aḻalēniṉ cemmēṉi eṉṉiṉumeṉ ayyāniṉ kālpiṭittaṟ kañcēṉkāṇ - meyyā-iñ ñāṉṟukaṇṭu nāṉmakiḻa nantoṇṭaṉ eṉṟeṉaiyum ēṉṟukoṇ ṭālpōtum eṉakku.
translation: Even if they say Your red form is like fierce fire, my Lord, I do not fear to grasp Your feet. O Truth, it is enough for me if You accept me today as Your devotee, so that I may see You and rejoice.
commentary: God is often described as a fierce, blazing fire. Vallalar feels no fear of this burning intensity, longing only for the pure joy of being claimed completely by the divine.

translit: eṉpālō eṉpāl irātōṭu kiṉṟamaṉat tiṉpālō ammaṉattaic cērmāyai - taṉpālō yārpāl piḻaiyuḷatō yāṉaṟiyēṉ eṉṉammai ōrpāl koḷaniṉṟōy ōtu.
translation: You who stand with our Mother on one side of your body, please tell me. Does the fault lie with me? Does it lie with the mind that runs away instead of staying with me? Or does it lie with the illusion that attaches to that mind? I do not know whose fault this is.
commentary: The root of spiritual failure is often hard to trace. Vallalar asks God to tell him exactly where the blame lies: with his own soul, with his restless mind, or with the cosmic illusion (māyai) that constantly distracts his thoughts.

translit: nāṇavatti ṉēṉṟaṉaiyō nāyēṉai mūṭiniṉṟa āṇavattai yōnāṉ aṟiyēṉē - vīṇavattil tīṅkuṭaiyāy eṉṉa-ivaṇ ceypiḻaiyai nōkki-aruṭ pāṅkuṭaiyāy taṇṭip patu.
translation: O Lord of Grace, looking at the wrongs committed here, you punish me and say I am full of evil. Are you punishing me, who stand here ashamed? Or are you punishing the ego that covers this dog? I do not know.
commentary: When we suffer for our mistakes, it is hard to know which part of us is being corrected. Vallalar asks whether God's punishment falls on his true self, standing there ashamed, or on the ego (āṇavam) that covers him and actually did the wrong.

translit: eccam peṟumulakōr eṭṭimara māṉālum pacceṉ ṟirukkap pakarvārkāṇ - vecceṉṟa nañcaṉaiyēṉ kuṟṟamelām nāṭātu nāta-eṉai añcaṉaiyēl eṉpāy amarntu.
translation: People of the world will wish for even a poisonous tree to stay green and flourish. O Lord, do not examine all the faults in me, who am like hot poison. Draw near and tell me not to fear.
commentary: Ordinary people wish even a poisonous tree to stay green, simply because it is alive. Vallalar asks God for that same basic mercy. He calls himself hot poison and begs the Lord to overlook his faults, draw near, and comfort him instead of judging him.

translit: kaṟṟaṟiyēṉ niṉṉaṭiccīr kaṟṟār kaḻakattil uṟṟaṟiyēṉ uṇmai uṇarntaṟiyēṉ - ciṟṟaṟivēṉ vaṉceyvēl nērviḻiyār maiyaliṉēṉ mātēvā eṉceyvēṉ niṉṉaruḷiṉ ṟēl.
translation: I have not learned. I have not joined the assembly of those who study the glory of your feet. I have not realized the truth. I possess only petty knowledge. I am lost in infatuation for women whose eyes pierce like cruel spears. O Great God, what will I do without your grace?
commentary: Spiritual progress usually asks for study, the company of the wise, and self-control. Vallalar confesses he has none of these and is lost in worldly desire. With no merit of his own to lean on, grace is his only hope.

translit: meytāṉ uṭaiyōr virumpukiṉṟa niṉaruḷeṉ ceytāl varumō teriyēṉē - poytāvu neñciṉēṉ maṉṟuḷ niruttā niṉaikkēṭka añciṉēṉ aṉpiṉmai yāl.
translation: I do not know what I must do to attain your grace, which those who hold the truth deeply desire. Falsehood runs wild in my heart. O Dancer in the hall, I am afraid to ask you because I have no love.
commentary: A heart full of falsehood feels unworthy even to ask for help. Vallalar does not know what he must do to receive grace, and he is afraid to pray for it because he feels he has no true love for God. He calls on the Dancer in the hall, a traditional image of the divine in cosmic motion.

translit: mātēvā ōvā maruntēvā māmaṇi-ip pōtēvā eṉṟē pulampuṟṟēṉ - nītāvā yāṉāluṉ citta maṟiyēṉ uṭampoḻintu pōṉāleṉ ceyvēṉ pukal.
translation: Great God, come as the ceaseless nectar, come as the great gem, come right now. I cried out like this, yet you have not come. I do not know your will. Tell me what I will do if this body perishes.
commentary: The fear is simple and sharp: the body may die before the Lord comes. Vallalar begs him to arrive now, this instant, and admits he cannot read the divine will. Without that knowledge, he is afraid his life will end in failure.

translit: koṉceytāṟ kēṟṟiṭumeṉ kuṟṟamelām aiya-eṉai eṉceytāl tīrntiṭumō yāṉaṟiyēṉ - muṉceytōy niṉpāl eṉaikkoṭuttēṉ nīceyka aṉṟi-iṉi eṉpāl ceyaloṉ ṟilai.
translation: Sire, all my faults warrant severe punishment. I do not know what must be done to me for them to be wiped away. O Ancient One, I have surrendered myself to you. Do with me as you will. I have no action left of my own.
commentary: Facing the weight of his own flaws, Vallalar stops trying and places himself entirely in God's hands. Nothing he does can undo his mistakes. Total surrender is the only path left.

translit: eṇṇileḷi yēṉtavira ellā uyirkaḷuniṉ taṇṇilakun tāṇīḻal cārntiṭuṅkāṇ - maṇṇilvarun tīṅkeṉṟa ellāmeṉ cintaiyicain tuṟṟaṉamaṟ ṟāṅkoṉṟum illāmai yāl.
translation: Except for my poor self, observe how all souls reach the cool, radiant shade of your feet. Everything deemed evil in this world has gathered willingly in my mind, leaving none of it anywhere else.
commentary: Intense devotional humility. Every other living being has found shelter with God, Vallalar says, while he alone has soaked up all the evil in the world. Calling himself the worst of creatures, he has nothing to lean on except divine mercy.

translit: tāramviṟṟuñ cēyviṟṟun taṉṉaiviṟṟum poyyāta vāramvaittāṉ muṉṉiṅkōr maṉṉaṉeṉpar - nāramvaitta vēṇip pirāṉatutāṉ meyyāmēl aṉṟeṉainī ēṇiṟ piṟappitta til.
translation: They say a king here in the past maintained unfailing devotion even while selling his wife, selling his child, and selling himself. O Lord with the river in your matted hair, if that is true, then you did not cause me to be born with such firmness.
commentary: An old legend tells of a king who sold his family and himself rather than break his vow of devotion. Vallalar holds that story up to Siva, the Lord with a river flowing through his matted hair. Then he confesses plainly that he was not created with that kind of unbending strength.

translit: uḷḷoṉṟa niṉṉaṭikkaṉ puṟṟaṟiyēṉ eṉṉuḷattiṉ veḷḷeṉṟa vaṉmai viḷaṅkātō - naḷḷoṉṟa accaṅkoṇ ṭēṉainiṉak kaṉpaṉeṉpar vēḻattiṉ eccaṅkaṇ ṭāṟpōla vē.
translation: I have never known love for your feet with a unified heart. Is the bare hardness of my heart not evident? People call me your devotee even though I harbor deep fear. It is like seeing the droppings of an elephant.
commentary: Vallalar tears down the public picture of himself as a perfect saint. His heart, he admits, is hard and filled with fear, with no pure love to speak of. Those who take him for a great devotee are like people who see an elephant's droppings and think they are looking at the majestic animal itself.

translit: nīttāṭuñceñcaṭaiyāy nīḷvēṭaṅ kaṭṭivañcak kūttāṭu kiṉṟēṉaik koṇṭucilar - kūttāniṉ pattaṉeṉpar eṉṉō pakalvēṭat tārkkumiṅku vittamilānāyēṟkum vēṟu.
translation: O Lord with red matted hair where the river dances! I put on a long disguise and perform a deceitful dance. Seeing me, some people call me your devotee, O Dancer. What is the difference between daytime actors in costume and this destitute dog here?
commentary: Every seeker sometimes feels like a spiritual fraud. People praise Vallalar as a great devotee, yet he feels he is only wearing a costume and playing a part. So he asks God what separates a paid daytime actor from himself.

translit: aṉpuṭaiyār iṉcol amutēṟu niṉcevikkē iṉpuṭaiyāy eṉpoyyum ēṟkuṅkol - tuṉpuṭaiyēṉ poyyuṭaiyēṉ āyiṉuniṉ poṉṉaruḷai vēṇṭumoru meyyuṭaiyēṉ eṉkō viraintu.
translation: O joyful Lord! The sweet nectar of words from your loving devotees fills your ears. Will my lies find acceptance there too? Even though I am full of sorrow and full of falsehood, I desire your golden grace. Shall I quickly say that this alone is the one truth I possess?
commentary: God's ears are used to the sweet, sincere prayers of true devotees. Vallalar fears his own words, full of falsehood and sorrow, are unfit to reach them. Still he offers one truth he cannot deny: his desperate desire for God's grace.

translit: eṉṉā ruyirkkuyirām emperumāṉ niṉpatattai uṉṉār uyirkkuṟuti uṇṭōtāṉ - poṉṉākat tārkkum catumukarkkum tāṉattavarkkumaṟṟai yārkkum pukaluṉ aruḷ.
translation: My Lord, the life of my precious life! Is there any salvation for the souls of those who do not think of your feet? Your grace is the only refuge for golden-bodied Vishnu, four-faced Brahma, the celestials, and all others.
commentary: Divine grace is the one true refuge for every soul. Even Brahma and Vishnu, the creator and preserver gods of Hindu tradition, depend on it entirely. Whoever does not turn to the divine has no salvation.

translit: veḷḷaip piṟai-aṇinta vēṇip pirāṉēnāṉ piḷḷaip pirāyattil peṟṟāḷai - eḷḷap poṟuttāḷat tāyil poṟuppuṭaiyōy nītāṉ veṟuttāl iṉi-eṉcey vēṉ.
translation: O Lord with matted hair wearing the white crescent moon! During my childhood, the mother who bore me patiently endured my mischief. You have even greater patience than that mother. If you yourself reject me, what will I do now?
commentary: A mother puts up with her child's endless mischief. God bears even more of our flaws, with a patience far beyond hers. If this Lord, more motherly than any mother, were to reject him, Vallalar asks where he could possibly turn.

translit: āyiramaṉṟēnūṟum aṉṟē-ī raintaṉṟē āyirampēr entai-eḻut taintēkāṇ - nī-iravum ellu niṉaittiyeṉa ēttukiṉum entāyvīṇ cellumaṉam eṉceykēṉ ceppu.
translation: It is not a thousand, nor a hundred, nor even ten. The sacred letters of my Father with a thousand names are exactly five. Even when I command my mind to meditate on them day and night, O Father, this mind wanders in vain. Tell me what I should do.
commentary: The sacred mantra of Siva has exactly five syllables (Na-Ma-Si-Va-Ya). It is short and simple. Even so, Vallalar's mind wanders every time he tries to meditate on it, and he asks God for help in taming his restless thoughts.

translit: vañcan taruṅkāma vāḻkkaiyiṭaic cikkiya-eṉ neñcan tirutti nilaittilaiyē - eñcaṅ karaṉē maḻukkoḷ karaṉē araṉē varaṉē citamparaṉē vantu.
translation: O Sankara, O Lord holding the battle-axe, O Hara, O supreme Lord, O Lord of Chidambaram. You have not come to correct and steady my heart that is caught in this deceitful life of lust.
commentary: Caught in the traps of worldly desire, Vallalar calls out for rescue. He uses the traditional names: Sankara (the source of grace), Hara (the destroyer of ignorance), and the Lord of Chidambaram (the sacred space of consciousness). For all his reverence, he is frustrated that God has not yet come to steady his restless heart.

translit: tāḻvikkum vañcac cakamāl oḻitteṉṉai vāḻvikkum nalla marunteṉkō - vīḻvikkum īṅkāṉa māyai ikantōrk karuḷvōyniṉ pāṅkāṉa cempoṟ patam.
translation: You grant grace to those who transcend the ruinous illusion of this place. Shall I call your beautiful golden feet the good medicine that gives me life by destroying the delusion of this deceitful and degrading world?
commentary: Divine grace works like medicine for the soul. Vallalar looks to the Lord's golden feet, a traditional symbol of spiritual refuge, as the cure for the degrading illusions of worldly life, and asks to rely entirely on that remedy to lift him out of delusion.

translit: ēcolikku māṉiṭaṉāy ēṉpiṟantēṉ toṇṭarkaṭan tūcolippāṉ kallākat tōṉṟilaṉē - tūcolippāṉ kallākat tōṉṟuvaṉēl kāḷakaṇṭā nāyēṉuk kellā nalamumuḷa tē.
translation: Why was I born as a human being subject to words of blame? I was not born as a stone upon which devotees wash their clothes. O Lord with the dark throat, if I had appeared as a washing stone, I, who am lower than a dog, would possess all goodness.
commentary: A flawed human life can feel like a heavy burden. Vallalar wishes he had been born a plain stone on which devotees wash their clothes. Serving spiritual people even as a lifeless object, he feels, would hold more goodness than a human life that keeps drawing blame. The Lord with the dark throat recalls the traditional story of the divine drinking poison to save the world.

translit: kuṟṟam palaceyiṉuṅ kōpañ ceyātavaruḷ ciṟṟam palamuṟaiyuñ ciṟparaṉē - veṟṟampal poyviṭṭāl aṉṟip purantaruḷēṉ eṉṟeṉainī kaiviṭṭāl eṉceykēṉ kāṇ.
translation: O supreme being of consciousness who dwells in Chitrambalam, granting grace without anger even when one commits many faults. If you abandon me, saying "I will not protect and bless you unless you give up your empty lies", what shall I do? Consider this.
commentary: God forgives without limit. Vallalar addresses the Lord in Chitrambalam (the hall of consciousness) as one who grants grace without anger despite our many faults, and he pleads for that unconditional mercy. If God demanded absolute perfection before giving protection, a flawed soul would be left helpless.

translit: tīkkuṇattār yāvarumeṉ cīṭareṉil eṉṉuṭaiya tīkkuṇattiṉ ellai-evar tērkiṟpār - ūkkamiku nallōrk kaḷikku naticcaṭaiyōy eṟkaruḷil ellōrkkum aiyuṟavā mē.
translation: If all people of evil nature are my disciples, who can fathom the limits of my own evil character? O Lord with the river in your matted hair, you grant grace to zealous and good people. If you bestow your grace on me, everyone will fall into doubt.
commentary: Vallalar feels the full weight of his flaws. If every evil person is his disciple, he says, no one could measure his own faults. Addressing the Lord with the river in his matted hair (a traditional image of the divine holding the sacred Ganges), he warns half in play that grace given to someone so unworthy might make everyone question God's judgment.

translit: iṉpaṭaiyāṉ ṟaṉpuṭaiyāṉ eṉṟēḻai yēṉtalaimēl aṉpuṭaiyāy nīyamaippit tāyitaṟku - vaṉpaṭaiyā tevvaṇṇam niṉṉeñ cicaintatō annāḷil ivvaṇṇam eṉṟaṟiki lēṉ.
translation: O loving Lord, you claimed me as your own and established your blissful feet upon my poor head. I do not know how your heart agreed to do this on that day without harboring any harshness.
commentary: When the Lord sets his feet on your head, he has claimed you as his own. Vallalar marvels at this love that asks nothing first, and wonders how the divine heart could take on someone so flawed without a trace of hesitation or judgment.

translit: ēyppiṟappoṉ ṟillātōy eṉpiṟappiṉ ēḻmaṭaṅkōr pēyppiṟappē nalla piṟappantō - vāyppulakam vañcameṉat tēka maṟaittaṭimaṇ vaiyāmal añciniṉṉō ṭāṭum atu.
translation: O Lord without birth! Alas, being born as a ghost is seven times better than my birth. Recognizing the opportunities of this world as mere deceit, a ghost hides its form, keeps its feet off the earth, and dances in awe with you.
commentary: Vallalar humbles himself so far that he calls a ghost's birth seven times better than his own, bound as he is to worldly illusion. A ghost keeps its feet off the ground and stays clear of the earth's deceit. It spends its time dancing in awe with the Lord.

translit: kōṭum piṟaiccaṭaiyōy kōḷuṅ kuṟumpuñcāk kāṭum piṇimūppuṅ kāṇārkāṇ - nīṭuniṉaik kaṇṭār aṭippoṭiyaik kaṇṭār tiruvaṭiyaik kaṇṭār vaṭivukaṇṭār kaḷ.
translation: O Lord with the curved crescent moon in your matted hair! Those who have eternally seen you, those who have seen the dust of your feet, those who have seen your holy feet, and those who have seen your sacred form will never experience planetary afflictions, harm, death, disease, or old age.
commentary: Seeing God, or even the dust gathered at his feet, brings complete freedom from suffering. Whoever receives that sight is free for good from illness, old age and death itself.

translit: māleṅkē vētaṉuyar vāḻveṅkē intiraṉceṅ kōleṅkē vāṉōr kuṭiyeṅkē - kōlañcēr aṇṭameṅkē avvav varumporuḷeṅ kēniṉatu kaṇṭamaṅkē nīlamuṟāk kāl.
translation: Where would Vishnu be? Where would Brahma's exalted life be? Where would Indra's righteous scepter be? Where would the dwelling of the celestials be? Where would the beautiful universe be? Where would all those rare entities be if your throat had not turned blue?
commentary: An old story tells of a deadly poison that threatened to destroy the universe until God swallowed it, and his throat turned blue to save creation. Vallalar asks where the other gods, the heavens and the world itself would be without that act of compassion. Everything exists only because God's grace holds it up.

translit: evvēḷai yōvaruṅkūṟ ṟempāleṉ ṟeṇṇukiṉṟa avvēḷai tōṟum aḻuṅkuṟṟēṉ - cevvēḷai mikkaḷittōy niṉkaḻaṟkāl vīrattai eṇṇutoṟum ekkaḷittu vāḻkiṉṟēṉ yāṉ.
translation: I suffered every time I wondered when the God of Death would come for us. O Lord who graciously bestowed Murugan upon us! Whenever I think of the valor of your anklet-adorned feet, I live in overflowing joy.
commentary: Fear of death brings deep suffering to a human life. Remembering the protecting power of the Lord's feet drives that terror away at once, and overflowing joy and safety take its place.

translit: tuṟcaṅkat tōrkaṇamun tōyātu niṉṉaṭiyar caṟcaṅkat teṉṟaṉainī tāṉkūṭṭi - naṟcaṅkak kāppāṉ pukaḻuṉ kaḻaṟpukaḻaik kēṭpittuk kāppāy iḵteṉ karuttu.
translation: Do not let me mingle even for a moment with wicked company. Unite me with the true company of your devotees. Make me hear the praise of your holy feet, praised by the protector of the good assembly, and protect me. This is my intention.
commentary: Vallalar asks to be kept entirely away from harmful company and placed among those who truly love God. He knows the people around us shape our minds. Among true devotees he can hear the Lord praised constantly and stay safe.

translit: eṉṉamutē mukkaṇ iṟaiyē niṟaiñāṉa iṉṉamutē niṉṉaṭiyai ēttukiṉṟōr - poṉṉaṭikkē kātaluṟṟut toṇṭuceyak kātalkoṇṭēṉ eṟkaruṇī kātaluṟṟuc ceytal kaṭaṉ.
translation: My ambrosia, O three-eyed Lord, O sweet ambrosia of perfect wisdom. I have fallen in love with the golden feet of those who praise your feet and I desire to serve them. It is your duty to grant me your grace with love.
commentary: Devotion reaches past God to God's followers. Vallalar's deepest desire is simply to serve the people who praise the divine. Then, with real intimacy, he tells the three-eyed Lord (Siva) that since he loves His devotees so much, granting him grace is now God's duty.

translit: ārā amutē aruṭkaṭalē nāyēṉṟaṉ pērāta vañcap piḻainōkki - yārēṉu niṉpōlvār illātōy nīyē puṟampaḻittāl eṉpōlvār eṉcollār īṅku.
translation: O insatiable ambrosia, O ocean of grace, O Lord who has no equal. If you look at the stubborn and deceitful faults of this dog-like wretch and reject me yourself, what will people like me say here?
commentary: Vallalar admits openly to stubborn faults and deceitful tendencies. Yet he puts it to God plainly. If the source of unlimited grace rejects a flawed soul, that soul has nowhere else to turn, and if the supreme Lord casts out a helpless person, ordinary people will lose all hope in divine mercy.

translit: meyyāka niṉṉaiviṭa vēṟōr tuṇaiyillēṉ aiyā atunī aṟintatukāṇ - poyyāṉa tītuceyvēṉ taṉpiḻaiyaic cittaṅ kuṟittiṭilyāṉ yātuceyvēṉ antō iṉi.
translation: Truly I have no companion other than you. O Lord, you know this well. I commit false and evil deeds. If you keep my faults in your mind, alas, what will I do now?
commentary: Vallalar drops every defense and leans entirely on his helplessness. He confesses his wrongdoing freely and reminds the Lord that he has no other refuge. If the divine mind keeps a strict record of his mistakes, he says, he is lost.

translit: tiṇṇam aṟiyāc ciṟiyēṉ uḷattirukkum eṇṇam aṟintāy iraṅkukilāy - aṇṇaluṉpāl nittam iraṅkā-eṉ neñcamarnta tālōniṉ cittam iraṅkāc ceyal.
translation: I am a lowly one who knows no certainty. You know the thoughts in my heart, yet you show no pity. O Lord, does your mind show no pity because you reside in my heart, which daily shows no feeling for you?
commentary: Vallalar turns the blame for God's silence back on his own hard heart. Perhaps, he wonders, God has stopped showing pity simply because God lives inside him. His heart stays indifferent and fails to melt in daily devotion, and the presence dwelling there may have caught the same lack of feeling.

translit: koṉṉañcēṉ taṉpiḻaiyaik kūrntuṟṟu nāṉiṉaikkil eṉneñcē eṉṉai erikkuṅkāṇ - maṉṉuñcīr entāyniṉ cittattiṟ kētāmō nāṉaṟiyēṉ cintā kulaṉeṉcey vēṉ.
translation: When I closely ponder my own faults, my very heart burns me. O Father of enduring glory, I do not know Your divine will. I am consumed by sorrow. What shall I do?
commentary: Looking honestly at our own mistakes can be agonizing. Vallalar's heart burns with regret when he examines his faults. Unsure what God intends for him, he feels entirely lost.

translit: niṉṉaṉpar tampāl niṟuttutiyō aṉṟi-eṉaip poṉṉaṉpar tampāl puṇarttutiyō - poṉṉaṉpar vaivamē eṉṉum vaṟiyēṉ aṟiyēṉeṉ teyvamē niṉṟaṉ ceyal.
translation: Will You establish me among Your devotees? Or will You join me with those who love only gold? I am a poor wretch who knows the lovers of gold will only abuse me. I do not know Your workings, O my God.
commentary: The company we keep shapes our lives. Vallalar fears being left among people who care only for wealth, since those who chase money will only mistreat a seeker. He wonders anxiously whether God will protect him by placing him among true devotees.

translit: eṉciṟumai nōkkā teṉakkaruḷal vēṇṭumeṉṟē niṉperumai nōkki-iṅku niṟkiṉṟēṉ - eṉperuma yātōniṉ cittam aṟiyēṉ aṭiyēṟkep pōtō aruḷvāy pukal.
translation: I stand here looking at Your greatness, praying that You grant me grace without looking at my baseness. O my Lord, I do not know Your will. Tell me when You will bestow Your grace upon this servant.
commentary: We often feel too flawed to deserve divine love. Vallalar asks God to overlook his smallness and act from His own boundless greatness. He stands in surrender, waiting anxiously for the moment grace arrives.

translit: entāyeṉ kuṟṟamelām eṇṇuṅkāl uḷnaṭuṅki nontā kulattiṉ nuḻaikiṉṟēṉ - cintāta kāḷa makiḻniṉ kaḷakkaruṇai eṇṇutoṟum mīḷamakiḻ kiṉṟēṉ viraintu.
translation: O my Father, when I count all my faults, I tremble within and plunge into agonizing sorrow. Yet whenever I think of the grace of Your throat that joyfully held the dark poison, I quickly rejoice again.
commentary: Remembering divine compassion cures the despair of self-doubt. Vallalar thinks again of the poison the Lord held safely in his throat to save the world. When he recalls that willingness to take in darkness for the sake of others, his fear over his own faults turns at once to joy.

translit: eḷḷalē eṉṉiṉumōr ēttutalāyk koṇṭaruḷem vaḷḷalē eṉṟaṉainī vāḻvittāl - taḷḷalē vēṇṭumeṉa yārē viḷampuvār niṉṉaṭiyar kāṇṭumeṉac cūḻvār kaḷittu.
translation: O our generous Lord, even if my words are mockery, accept them as praise and bestow Your grace. If You uplift me to a life of grace, who would say I must be cast away? Your devotees will joyfully surround me, eager to see me.
commentary: Divine acceptance can change everything. Vallalar asks God to take even his flawed words as praise. Once grace lifts a person up, he knows, the whole company of devotees will welcome them with open arms.

translit: vēṇikka mēvaitta veṟpē vilaiyillā māṇikka mēkaruṇai mākaṭalē - māṇikku muṉpoṟ kiḻiyaḷitta muttē-eṉ āruyirkku niṉpoṟ kaḻalē nilai.
translation: O Mountain who bears the river on your matted hair! O priceless ruby! O great ocean of grace! O Pearl who once gave a purse of gold to the young bachelor! For my precious life, your golden feet alone are the firm refuge.
commentary: Two old stories sit inside these names: the Lord who carries the Ganges in his matted hair, and the Lord who once gave a purse of gold to a young devotee in need. Behind the images the idea is plain. Life keeps shifting, and the divine presence is the only steady ground.

translit: muttēvar pōṟṟu mutaṟṟēva niṉṉaiyaṉṟi ettēvar caṟṟē eṭutturainī - pittēṉcey kuṟṟamelām iṅkōr kuṇamākak koṇṭeṉṉai aṟṟamilā tāḷkiṉ ṟavar.
translation: O Primal God praised by the three gods, tell me plainly. What god other than you accepts all the faults committed by this madman as a virtue and rules me flawlessly?
commentary: The poem asks who else could possibly show such boundless forgiveness. God looks at the many mistakes of a confused person and accepts them as virtues instead, offering flawless guidance.

translit: kaṅkaic caṭaiyāymuk kaṇṇuṭaiyāy kaṭceviyām aṅkac cuṭaiyāy aruḷuṭaiyāy - maṅkaik korukū ṟaḷittāy uṉaittoḻumin nāyēṉ irukū ṟaḷittēṉ iṭarkku.
translation: You hold the Ganges in your matted hair. You have three eyes. You wear serpents on your body. You are full of grace. You gave one half of yourself to the Goddess. Yet I, this dog who worships you, have given both halves of myself to sorrow.
commentary: The stories say the Lord gave exactly one half of his body to the Goddess. Vallalar sets his own condition beside that perfect balance. He worships a God so full of grace, and still he has handed both halves of himself over to sorrow.

translit: pēcat teriyēṉ piḻaiyaṟiyēṉ pētuṟiṉum kūcat teriyēṉ kuṇamaṟiyēṉ - nēcattil koḷḷuvār uṉṉaṭimaik kūṭṭattār allātār eḷḷuvār kaṇṭāy eṉai.
translation: I do not know how to speak properly. I do not recognize my own faults. Even when I blunder in ignorance, I feel no shame. I know no good qualities. The gathering of your devotees accepts me with love. You know well that all others mock me.
commentary: Vallalar's confession is total. He has no right words, he blunders in ignorance without shame, and he can name no good trait in himself. The world usually mocks a person like that. The community of true devotees takes him in with complete love.

translit: ūṇē uṭaiyē-eṉ ṟuṭkaruti veṭkamilēṉ vīṇēnaṉ ṉāḷai viṭukiṉṟēṉ - kāṇēṉiṉ cempāta mē-eṉṟun tīrāp poruḷeṉṟu nampāta nāyaṭiyēṉ nāṉ.
translation: My mind dwells entirely on food and clothing. I have no shame. I waste my good days in vain. I do not see the truth. I am a lowly dog who refuses to believe that your red feet alone are the everlasting, inexhaustible wealth.
commentary: It is easy to spend a whole life worrying about food and clothing. Vallalar mourns the days he has wasted that way. That everyday worry blinds him to the truth and keeps him from trusting that the divine presence is the only lasting wealth.

translit: civamē civañāṉac celvamē aṉpar navamē tavamē nalamē navamām vaṭivuṟṟa tēvēniṉ mākkaruṇai yaṉṟō paṭivuṟṟa eṉṉuṭ payaṉ.
translation: O Sivam! O wealth of divine knowledge! O renewal for your devotees! O penance! O goodness! O God taking ever new forms! Is it not your great compassion that is the fruit deeply settled within me?
commentary: Vallalar calls the supreme reality Sivam, the source of all spiritual wealth. Whatever goodness has taken root in him, he refuses to claim as his own achievement. It comes straight from God's immense compassion, dwelling in his heart.

translit: kōḷākkik koḷḷuṅ koṭiyē ṉaiyuniṉakkōr āḷākkik koḷḷaṟ kamaivāyēl - nīḷākkuñ ceṅkēca vēṇic civaṉē-eṉ āṇavattiṟ keṅkē iṭaṅkāṇ iyampu.
translation: O Siva with long matted red hair! If you agree to take even me, a cruel man given to slander, and make me your servant, tell me where my ego will find any room.
commentary: Once God accepts a person, pride has nowhere to stand. If the Lord forgives Vallalar's flaws and takes him in as a servant, grace will fill the place where ego lived. Selfishness will have no room left to survive.

translit: tiṇṇañcaṟ ṟīntiṭaniṉ cittam iraṅkāta vaṇṇañcaṟ ṟēteriya vantatukāṇ - eṇṇeñcil ittaṉaiyu meṉviṉaikaḷ nīṅkil irukka-aṇṭam ettaṉaiyum pōtāmai eṉṟu.
translation: It has become somewhat clear why your heart does not take pity to grant me even a little certainty. You consider in your heart that if all these karmas were to leave me, every universe combined would not provide enough space for them to stay.
commentary: Karma, the weight of past actions, can feel overwhelming. Vallalar answers it with a deliberate exaggeration about his own flaws. God must be hesitating, he says, because if all those faults were released at once, the entire universe would not be large enough to hold them.

translit: iṇṭaic caṭaiyōy eṉakkaruḷa eṇṇutiyēl toṇṭaip peṟumeṉ tuyarellām - caṇṭaikkiṅ kuyñcēmeṉa-ōṭum ōṭṭattiṟ keṉṉuṭaiya neñcē piṟakiṭuṅkāṇ niṉṟu.
translation: O Lord wearing a wreath on your matted hair! If you decide to bestow grace upon me, all my entrenched sorrows will run away thinking they have survived the battle. In their flight, my very mind will retreat and fall behind.
commentary: When grace enters, worldly suffering cannot stay. Vallalar pictures his deep-rooted sorrows fleeing in terror, desperate just to survive the Lord's arrival. They run so fast that his own fearful mind is left behind.

translit: kaṇṇā ṇiḻutaikaḷpāṟ kāṭṭik koṭukkileṉai aṇṇā aruḷuk kaḻakaṉṟē - uṇṇāṭu niṉṉaṭiyār kūṭṭattil nīrivaṉaic cērttiṭumiṉ eṉṉaṭiyāṉ eṉpāy eṭuttu.
translation: O Lord! It brings no beauty to your grace if you point me out and hand me over to blind fools. Lift me up, declare me your servant, and instruct the gathering of your inward-seeking devotees to include me in their fold.
commentary: Good company is itself a gift of grace. Vallalar asks not to be handed over to worldly people who are blind to the truth. He wants the Lord to claim him personally as a servant and place him among true devotees whose hearts are turned inward toward the light.

translit: kaṇṇappaṉ ēttunutaṟ kaṇṇappa meyññāṉa viṇṇappa niṉṟaṉakkōr viṇṇappam - maṇṇiṟcil vāṉavaraip pōṟṟum matattōr palaruṇṭu nāṉavaraic cērāmal nāṭṭu.
translation: O Lord with the eye on the forehead praised by Kannappan. O true spiritual sky. I have one petition for you. On this earth, there are many followers of religions who praise minor celestial gods. Establish me so that I do not associate with them.
commentary: Vallalar asks to be kept away from people who follow sectarian religions and worship minor gods. He addresses the Divine as the one praised by Kannappan (a famous saint known for his fierce, innocent devotion). Kannappan won the Lord by love alone.

translit: poṉṉiṉ ṟoḷirum puricaṭaiyōy niṉṉaiyaṉṟip piṉṉoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ piḻainōkki - eṉṉai aṭittālu nīyē aṇaittālu nīyē piṭittēṉuṉ poṟpātap pēṟu.
translation: O Lord with matted hair shining like gold. I know nothing but you. Looking at my faults, whether you strike me or embrace me, it is only you. I have grasped the ultimate blessing of your golden feet.
commentary: Vallalar surrenders completely and holds the divine feet as his only refuge. Punishment for his faults or a loving embrace, both come from the same Lord. He accepts it all as grace and trusts the Divine completely.

translit: tuṟkuṇattil vēṟu toṭarvēṉ eṉiṉumaṟṟai naṟkuṇattil uṉcīr nayappēṉkāṇ - ciṟkuṇattōy kūṟṟutaitta niṉpoṟ kuraikaḻaṟpūn tāḷaṟika vēṟṟuraittē ṉillai virittu.
translation: Even if I pursue other things out of base qualities, see that in my good nature I desire your glory. O Lord of supreme consciousness. Let your anklet-adorned, beautiful golden feet that kicked Death know this truth. I do not speak falsely or exaggerate.
commentary: Vallalar admits his lower nature sometimes pulls him toward worldly distractions. Underneath, his core self still longs for the Divine. He swears to this by the feet that kicked Death, recalling the ancient story of the Lord saving a devotee from the god of death. He wants God to know he is sincere.

translit: ippāril eṉpiḻaikaḷ ellām poṟuttaruḷeṉ appāniṉ tāṭkē aṭaikkalaṅkāṇ - ippāril nāṉiṉatu tāṇīḻal naṇṇumaṭṭum niṉṉaṭiyar pāṉiṉatu cīrkēṭkap paṇ.
translation: Forgive all my faults on this earth and bestow your grace. My Father, see that I seek refuge only at your feet. On this earth, until I reach the sheltering shade of your feet, make me listen to your glories from your devotees.
commentary: Vallalar asks for forgiveness and protection for as long as he lives on this earth. Until he finally reaches the shade of the Lord's feet, he has one wish: to stay among true devotees and hear them speak of God's glory. Hearing the Divine praised by others keeps the mind anchored in grace.

sections.title: The Garland for the Great God

translit: karuṇainiṟain takampuṟamum tuḷumpivaḻin tuyirkkellām kaḷaikaṇ ākit teruḷ niṟainta iṉpanilai vaḷarkkiṉṟa kaṇṇuṭaiyōy citaiyā ñāṉap poruḷniṟainta maṟaiyamutam poḻikiṉṟa malarvāyōy poyya ṉēṉṟaṉ maruḷniṟainta maṉakkaruṅkaṟ pāṟaiyumuṭ kacinturukkum vaṭivat tōyē.
translation: O Lord with eyes full of grace that overflows inside and out, becoming the refuge for all lives and nurturing the state of clear bliss. O Lord with a flower-like mouth pouring forth the deathless nectar of the scriptures filled with indestructible wisdom. O Lord whose form softens and melts the dark, rocky granite of my illusion-filled mind from within, false as I am.
commentary: God's grace is a tangible force that flows outward to protect all living beings. Vallalar says this divine compassion is so powerful that it can melt even the hardest, most stubborn human mind from the inside out.

translit: ulakanilai muḻutāki āṅkāṅ kuḷḷa uyirāki uyirkkuyirām oḷitāṉ ākik kalakanilai aṟiyāta kāṭci yākik katiyāki meyññāṉak kaṇṇa tāki ilakucitā kācamatāyp paramā kāca iyalpāki iṇaiyoṉṟum illā tāki alakilaṟi vāṉanta mākic cacci tāṉanta mayamāki amarnta tēvē.
translation: O God who sits established as the entire state of the world, as the souls within it, and as the light that is the life of all souls. You are the vision that knows no discord, the refuge, and the eye of true wisdom. You are the shining space of consciousness, the nature of the supreme space, and the one without equal. You are limitless blissful awareness and the embodiment of existence, consciousness, and bliss.
commentary: Vallalar puts God nowhere far away. God is the world itself, the souls living in it, and the inner light that gives those souls life.

translit: ulakamelān taṉiniṟainta uṇmai yāki yōkiyartam anupavattiṉ uvappāy eṉṟum kalakamuṟā upacānta nilaiya tākik kaḷaṅkamaṟṟa aruṇñāṉak kāṭci yāki vilakaluṟā nipiṭa-ā ṉanta māki mītāṉat toḷirkiṉṟa viḷakka māki ilakuparā paramāycciṟ paramāy aṉpar itayamalar mītirunta iṉpat tēvē.
translation: O God of bliss seated upon the heart-lotus of devotees. You became the unique truth filling all worlds, remaining forever the joy of the yogis' experience. You became the state of supreme peace untouched by conflict, the vision of flawless grace and wisdom. You became the inseparable dense bliss, the lamp shining in the supreme realm. You became the radiant supreme beyond the supreme and the supreme consciousness.
commentary: The divine is vast, and just as near. Vallalar says the same truth that fills all worlds and shines in the highest places also sits joyfully, like a radiant lamp, at the center of a loving heart.

translit: vittāki muḷaiyāki viḷaiva tāki viḷaivikkum poruḷāki mēlu mākik kottākip payaṉākik koḷvō ṉākik kuṟaivāki niṟaivākik kuṟaivi lāta cattākic cittāki iṉpa mākic catānilaiyāy evvuyirkkuñ cāṭci yāki muttāki māṇikka mākit teyva muḻuvayirat taṉimaṇiyāy muḷaitta tēvē.
translation: O God who sprouted as the seed, the shoot, the harvest, the cause of the harvest, and all that is beyond. You are the cluster, the fruit, the one who receives the fruit, the lack, and the fullness. You are the flawless existence, consciousness, and bliss. You are the eternal state, the witness to all lives. You are the pearl, the ruby, and the unique divine diamond.
commentary: God is present in every stage of life and action: the seed in the earth, the growing, the harvest, and even the one who enjoys the fruit. Behind every event and every living being, Vallalar says, God stands as the silent witness.

translit: vētānta nilaiyākic cittān tattiṉ meyyākic camaracattiṉ vivēka māki nātānta veḷiyāki muttān tattiṉ naṭuvāki navanilaikku naṇṇā tāki mūtāṇṭa kōṭiyellām tāṅki niṉṟa mutalāki maṉātīta mutti yāki vātāṇṭa camayaneṟik kamaiyā teṉṟum mavuṉaviyō mattiṉiṭai vayaṅkun tēvē.
translation: O God shining in the silent supreme space. You became the state of Vedanta, the truth of Siddhanta, and the discernment of the harmonious path. You became the space beyond sound, the center of ultimate liberation, remaining untouched by the nine states. You became the primal source supporting billions of ancient universes, the liberation beyond the mind. You remain forever uncontained by argumentative religious paths.
commentary: Arguing religions and sects can never contain the divine truth. Vallalar says God is the ultimate reality behind all spiritual philosophies, but this truth is only found in a space of deep inner silence, completely untouched by the noise of religious disputes.

translit: tōṉṟutuvi tāttuvita māyvi ciṭṭāt tuvitamāyk kēvalāt tuvita mākic cāṉṟacuttāt tuvitamāyc cuttan tōynta camaracāt tuvitamumāyt taṉṉai yaṉṟi ūṉṟunilai vēṟoṉṟu milatāy eṉṟum uḷḷatāy niraticaya uṇarvāy ellām īṉṟaruḷun tāyākit tantai yāki eḻiṟkuruvāyt teyvatamāy ilaṅkut tēvē.
translation: O shining Deity. You manifest as dual-nonduality, qualified nonduality, absolute nonduality, excellent pure nonduality, and the pure harmonious nonduality. You have no foundation other than yourself. You are eternally existent. You are unsurpassed consciousness. You become the mother and father who gracefully bring forth all things, the beautiful guru, and the supreme divinity.
commentary: Philosophers have long argued over how God and the soul relate, building whole schools on it, duality, nonduality, and their many variations. Vallalar sweeps these debates aside, stating simply that the Divine is the living truth within all of them. And that truth is close to us. God is our mother, our father, and our guiding teacher.

translit: paramākic cūkkumamāyt tūla mākip paramārtta nilaiyākip patattiṉ mēlām ciramākit tiruvaruḷām veḷiyāy āṉma ciṟcatti yāypparaiyiṉ cemmai yākit tiramākit taṟpōta nivirtti yākic civamākic civānupavac celva māki aramāki āṉanta pōta māki āṉantā tītamatāy amarnta tēvē.
translation: O seated Deity. You become the transcendent, the subtle, and the gross. You become the state of supreme truth. You become the crown above all states. You become the expanse of divine grace, the conscious energy of the soul, and the perfection of the supreme power. You become firmness. You become the cessation of self-awareness. You become the Supreme. You become the wealth of supreme experience. You become virtue. You become the consciousness of bliss, and you abide beyond bliss.
commentary: Everything we can experience takes the Divine's form, from the physical world we touch to the highest spiritual states we can reach. When a seeker's ego fades away, what remains is God. Yet even after becoming the highest joy and truth, the Divine rests beyond them, greater than any state the mind can grasp.

translit: intiyamāyk karaṇāti aṉaittu māki iyalpuruṭa ṉāykkāla paramu mākip pantamaṟṟa viyōmamāyp paramāy appāl paramparamāy vicuvamuṇṭa pāṉmai yāki vanta-upa cāntamatāy mavuṉa māki makāmavuṉa nilaiyāki vayaṅkā niṉṟa antamiltom patamāyttaṟ patamāy oṉṟum acipatamāy atītamāy amarnta tēvē.
translation: O seated Deity. You become the senses and all the inner faculties. You become the natural soul, time, and the transcendent. You become the unbound expanse, the supreme, and the supreme beyond the supreme. You become the nature that consumed the universe. You become the resulting supreme peace, silence, and the state of great silence. You become the endlessly shining word 'Thou', the word 'That', and the unifying word 'Art', and you abide in transcendence.
commentary: God makes up our senses, our minds, and time itself. The verse draws on the ancient teaching "Thou Art That", which declares the individual soul and the supreme reality to be one. Vallalar says the Divine is the true meaning of those words and the deep silence that follows them. It is also the reality lying far beyond them.

translit: niṉmayamāy eṉmayamāy oṉṟuṅ kāṭṭā nirāmayamāy niruvikaṟpa nilaiyāy mēlām taṉmayamāyt taṟparamāy vimala mākit taṭattamāyc corūpamāyc cakaca mākic ciṉmayamāyc ciṟparamāy acala mākic ciṟcolita māyakaṇṭa civamāy eṅkum maṉmayamāy vācakā tīta māki maṉātīta māyamarnta mavuṉat tēvē.
translation: O silent Deity. You exist as Your nature, as my nature, and as the unblemished state that reveals no distinctions. You exist as the undifferentiated state, the supreme true nature, the supreme Self, and the flawless one. You manifest as the conditioned state and the intrinsic nature. You become the natural state, the form of consciousness, the supreme consciousness, and the unmoving. You exist as the radiance of consciousness and the undivided Supreme. You are the nature that pervades everywhere. You become that which transcends speech and transcends the mind.
commentary: God's nature and the soul's true nature are the same, with no gap between them. That pure, undivided consciousness fills every corner of existence. Speech cannot reach it, and neither can thought.

translit: aḷaviṟanta neṭuṅkālam cittar yōkar aṟiñarmalar ayaṉmutalōr aṉanta vētam kaḷaviṟantum karaṇāti iṟantum ceyyum kaṭuntavattum kāṇparitām kaṭavu ḷāki uḷaviṟanta empōlvār uḷḷat tuḷḷē ūṟukiṉṟa teḷḷamuta ūṟa lākip piḷaviṟantu piṇṭāṇṭa muḻutun tāṉāyp piṟaṅkukiṉṟa peruṅkaruṇaip periya tēvē.
translation: O great Deity of immense compassion. You become the God who is difficult to behold even through the severe penance performed for an immeasurably long time by siddhas, yogis, wise men, the lotus-born Brahma, other celestials, and the endless Vedas, even as they transcend deception and surpass the inner faculties. Yet, you become the wellspring of clear ambrosia rising within the hearts of those like us who are free from deceit. Transcending division, you shine, becoming yourself the entirety of the body and the universe.
commentary: The greatest sages, the ancient scriptures known as the Vedas, and even the creator god Brahma cannot reach the Divine through severe spiritual discipline. Most people picture God as a distant prize won through painful effort. Vallalar says the opposite. In the hearts of ordinary people who live with pure, honest, open intentions, the Divine simply rises like sweet nectar.

translit: vāyāki vāyiṟanta mavuṉa māki matamāki mataṅkaṭanta vāymai yākik kāyākip paḻamākit taruvāy maṟṟaik karuvikara ṇātikaḷiṉ kalappāyp peṟṟa tāyākit tantaiyāyp piḷḷai yākit tāṉāki nāṉākic cakala māki ōyāta cattiyelām uṭaiya tāki oṉṟākip palavāki ōṅkun tēvē.
translation: O soaring God! You become speech and the silence beyond speech. You become religion and the truth beyond religion. You become the unripe fruit, the ripe fruit, and the tree. You become the blend of all bodily instruments and inner faculties. You become the mother who bore me, the father, and the child. You become Yourself, you become myself, and you become all things. Possessing all ceaseless powers, you become one and you become many.
commentary: God is present in every worldly form and relationship, yet stays beyond them all. The divine is the source of all religions, but is also the pure truth that transcends them. As mother, father, the individual soul, or the power that drives them all, the same reality is both the one and the many.

translit: aṇṭaṅkaḷ palavāki avaṟṟiṉ mēlum aḷavāki aḷavāta atīta mākip piṇṭaṅkaḷ aṉantavakai yākip piṇṭam piṟaṅkukiṉṟa poruḷākip pētan tōṟṟum paṇṭaṅkaḷ palavāki ivaṟṟaik kākkum patiyāki āṉantam paḻuttuc cāntam koṇṭeṅkum niḻalparappit taḻaintu ñāṉak koḻuṅkaṭavuḷ taruvākik kulavun tēvē.
translation: O rejoicing God! You become the many universes and the measure beyond them. You become the immeasurable transcendent reality. You become the endless varieties of physical bodies and the shining substance within those bodies. You become the many objects of diverse appearance. Becoming the Lord who protects them all, you ripen into bliss. Embracing peace, you spread your shade everywhere and flourish as the lush divine tree of wisdom.
commentary: The divine takes in the whole physical universe and the infinite space beyond it. It is the outer body of every living being and the radiant spark of life inside. Like a great tree, it shelters all things and spreads the deep shade of peace and wisdom.

translit: poṉṉāki maṇiyākip pōka mākip puṟamāki akamākip puṉita māki maṉṉāki malaiyākik kaṭalu māki matiyāki raviyāki maṟṟu māki muṉṉākip piṉṉāki naṭuvu māki muḻutāki nātamuṟa muḻaṅki eṅkum miṉṉākip paravi-iṉpa veḷḷan tēkka viyaṉkaruṇai poḻimukilāy viḷaṅkun tēvē.
translation: O radiant God! You become gold, gems, and enjoyment. You become the exterior, the interior, and the ultimate purity. You become the earth, the mountain, and the sea. You become the moon, the sun, and all other things. You become the beginning, the end, and the middle. You become the whole. Resounding with the primal sound, you spread everywhere like lightning and shine as the vast cloud pouring down grace to fill the flood of bliss.
commentary: Mountains, oceans, the wealth we chase, the pleasure we feel: Vallalar sees all of it as God made manifest. God spans all space and time as beginning, middle, and end. Above all this, the divine is a vast cloud pouring down a steady rain of grace until the world fills with joy.

translit: aritāki ariyatiṉum ariya tāki anātiyāy ātiyāy aruḷa tākip peritākip periyatiṉum periya tākip pētamāy apētamāyp piṟaṅkā niṉṟa karitāki veḷitākik kalaika ḷākik kalaikaṭanta poruḷākik karaṇā tītat teritāṉa veḷinaṭuvil aruḷām vaṇmaic ceḻuṅkiraṇac cuṭarākit tikaḻun tēvē.
translation: O shining God! You become the rare and the rarer than the rare. You become the beginningless, the beginning, and grace itself. You become the great and the greater than the great. You stand shining as the differentiated and the undifferentiated. You become the dark, the bright, and the arts. You become the reality beyond all arts. In the center of the conscious space beyond the inner faculties, you shine as the radiant flame of lush rays revealing the pure bounty of grace.
commentary: God holds every opposite, the dark and the bright, the diverse and the unified. This reality sits far beyond the intellect and all human arts. Step past the mind's inner faculties and you find God shining at the center of conscious space as a radiant flame of grace.

translit: uruvāki uruviṉiluḷ uruva māki uruvattil uruvāki uruvuḷ oṉṟāy aruvāki aruviṉiluḷ aruva māki aruvattil aruvāki aruvuḷ oṉṟāyk kuruvākic cattuvaciṟ kuṇatta tākik kuṇarakitap poruḷākik kulavā niṉṟa maruvāki malarāki valli yāki makattuvamāy aṇuttuvamāy vayaṅkun tēvē.
translation: O luminous God! You become form, the inner form within form, the form within form, and the unity within form. You become the formless, the inner formless within the formless, the formless within the formless, and the unity within the formless. You become the Guru. You take on the attributes of purity and consciousness, and you become the reality beyond all attributes. You become the fragrance, the flower, and the creeping vine. You manifest as the greatest magnitude and the smallest atom.
commentary: Form and formless both belong to God, the physical structure of the world and the invisible reality hidden inside it. The divine holds the highest qualities of pure consciousness while staying free of every limiting attribute. Whole and undivided, it is present as fully in the vast cosmos as in the smallest atom.

translit: cakalamāyk kēvalamāyc cutta mākic carācaramāy allavāyt tāṉē tāṉāy akalamāyk kuṟukkamāy neṭumai yāki avaiyaṉaittum aṇukāta acala māki ikaluṟāt tuṇaiyākit taṉiya tāki eṇkuṇamāy eṇkuṇattem iṟaiyāy eṉṟum ukalilāt taṇṇaruḷkoṇ ṭuyirai yellām ūṭṭivaḷart tiṭuṅkaruṇai ōvāt tēvē.
translation: You become the manifest, the dormant, and the pure states. You become the moving, the unmoving, and that which is neither, existing as Your very Self. You become breadth, shortness, and length, yet remain the immovable reality untouched by any of these. You become the unconflicting companion and the solitary one. You become the eight attributes and our Lord of eight attributes. O God of ceaseless compassion, You hold unfailing cool grace, feeding and nurturing all souls forever.
commentary: God takes every dimension, shape, and state of awareness, and none of them binds Him. After that whole list, Vallalar lands on one constant act: feeding and nurturing every living being with compassion that never runs out.

translit: vācakamāy vācciyamāy naṭuvāy anta vācakavāc ciyaṅkaṭanta mavuṉa mākit tēcakamāy iruḷakamāy iraṇṭuṅ kāṭṭāc cittakamāy vittakamāyc ciṟitum panta pācamuṟāp patiyākip pacuvu mākip pācanilai yāki-oṉṟum pakarā tāki nācamilā veḷiyāki oḷitā ṉāki nātānta muṭivilnaṭam naviṟṟum tēvē.
translation: You become the word, the meaning, and the center between them. You become the silence that transcends both word and meaning. You become the realm of light, the realm of darkness, and the realm of pure consciousness that reveals neither. You become the supreme wonder. You become the Lord who never incurs the slightest bondage. You become the bound soul and the state of bondage itself, yet You remain the one who speaks nothing. You become the indestructible space and the light itself. O God, You perform Your dance at the ultimate summit of sound.
commentary: God is the source of word and meaning, and also the silence beyond both. He plays every part in life's drama: the soul that feels trapped, the chains that bind it, and the Lord who stays perfectly free. Beyond all of it, He dances at the summit of existence.

translit: cakamākic cīvaṉāy īca ṉākic catumukaṉāyt tirumālāy araṉṟā ṉāki makamāyai mutalāykkū ṭatta ṉāki vāṉpirama māki-allā vaḻakku māki ikamākip patamākic camaya kōṭi ettaṉaiyu māki-avai eṭṭā vāṉkaṟ pakamākip paramākip parama mākip parāparamāyp paramparamāyp patiyum tēvē.
translation: You become the universe, the individual soul, and the ruling Lord. You become four-faced Brahma, Vishnu, and Siva. You become the great illusion and all its effects, and You become the unmoving witness. You become the supreme reality and the state that transcends it. You become this world, the heavenly realms, and the countless millions of religions, yet You remain the heavenly wish-fulfilling tree that they cannot reach. You become the supreme, the most supreme, the supreme beyond the supreme, and the boundless transcendent reality. O God, You reside as the ultimate Lord.
commentary: God appears as the universe, the individual soul, and the gods who create and protect, Brahma, Vishnu, and Siva. Yet Vallalar plainly states that while the divine is the origin of the world's millions of religions, God remains completely out of their reach. The true divine reality is vaster than any god, heaven, or system they describe.

translit: vitiyāki ariyākik kirīca ṉāki viḷaṅkumakēc curaṉāki vimala māṉa nitiyākuñ catācivaṉāy vintu vāki nikaḻnāta māypparaiyāy nimalā ṉantap patiyākum paracivamāyp paramāy mēlāyp pakkamiraṇ ṭāyiraṇṭum pakarā tākik katiyāki aḷaviṟanta katika ḷellām kaṭantuniṉṟu niṟaintaperuṅ karuṇait tēvē.
translation: You become Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra. You become the radiant Maheshvara and the pure treasure Sadasiva. You become the primal light, the prevailing primal sound, and the supreme energy. You become Parasiva, the abode of pure bliss. You become the supreme, the highest, the two opposing sides, and that which remains completely unspoken between them. You become the ultimate refuge, standing full and transcending all the boundless realms of attainment. O God of infinite compassion!
commentary: Vallalar runs through the highest deities and cosmic principles of the traditional scriptures, such as Sadasiva, primal sound (nādam), and primal light (vintu), and says God takes all these forms. Still, God transcends every one of these fixed stages of spiritual attainment. What stands far beyond them is pure, infinite compassion.

translit: māṉāki mōkiṉiyāy vintu māki maṟṟavaiyāl kāṇāta vāṉa māki nāṉāki nāṉalla ṉāki nāṉē nāṉākum patamāki nāṉṟāṉ kaṇṭa tāṉākit tāṉalla ṉākit tāṉē tāṉākum patamākic cakaca ñāṉa vāṉāki vāṉnaṭuvil vayaṅku kiṉṟa mavuṉanilai yākiyeṅkum vaḷarun tēvē.
translation: You become the primal illusion, the enchanting delusion, and the primal light. You become the vast space unseen by any of these. You become 'I', You become 'not I', and You become the state where 'I' remains truly 'I'. You become the 'That' which I have seen, You become 'not That', and You become the state where 'That' remains truly 'That'. You become the sky of natural wisdom and the state of silence shining in the center of that sky. O God, You flourish everywhere.
commentary: Behind our sense of self ("I") and behind the truth we try to grasp ("That") stands the same reality. God becomes both of them, the illusions that hide them, and the vast silent wisdom where such divisions of the mind finally dissolve.

translit: mantiramāyp patamāki vaṉṉa māki vaḷarkalaiyāyt tattuvamāyp puvaṉa mākic cantiraṉāy intiraṉāy iravi yākit tāṉavarāy vāṉavarāyt tayaṅkā niṉṟa tantiramāy ivaiyoṉṟum alla vākit tāṉākit taṉatākit tāṉāṉ kāṭṭā antaramāy appālāy ataṟkap pālāy appāluk kappālāy amarnta tēvē.
translation: O God seated in grace! You became mantras, words, letters, expanding aspects, foundational principles, and worlds. You became the moon, Indra, the sun, asuras, celestials, and the shining systems. Yet You became none of these. Becoming Yourself, becoming Your own, You are the unmanifest space, the beyond, the beyond to that, and the beyond to the beyond.
commentary: From sacred mantras to celestial rulers like Indra, God takes the form of everything. Yet He is limited to none of these forms. Vallalar keeps pushing outward, beyond, and beyond that, and beyond even that, past every physical and spiritual structure we can name.

translit: malaimēlum kaṭaṉmēlum malariṉ mēlum vāḻkiṉṟa mūvuruviṉ vayaṅkum kōvē nilaimēlum neṟimēlum niṟuttu kiṉṟa neṭuntavattōr niṟaimēlum nikaḻttum vētak kalaimēlum empōlvār uḷattiṉ mēlum kaṇmēlum tōḷmēlum karuttiṉ mēlum talaimēlum uyirmēlum uṇarviṉ mēlum takumaṉpiṉ mēlumvaḷar tāṇmeyt tēvē.
translation: O shining King in the three forms dwelling upon the mountain, upon the ocean, and upon the flower! O true God whose feet flourish upon the steadfast state, upon the righteous path, upon the perfection of those engaged in great penance, upon the proclaimed Vedic arts, upon the hearts of people like us, upon the eyes, upon the shoulders, upon the mind, upon the head, upon the life force, upon the consciousness, and upon worthy love!
commentary: The three forms are the traditional Hindu gods: Siva on the mountain, Vishnu on the ocean, and Brahma on the lotus flower. The divine includes them, but the same feet also rest on our eyes, shoulders, head, and mind. Wherever there is genuine, worthy love, that is where God is found.

translit: poṟkuṉṟē akampuṟamum polintu niṉṟa pūraṇamē āraṇattuṭ poruḷē eṉṟum kaṟkiṉṟōrk kiṉiyacuvaik karumpē tāṉa kaṟpakamē kaṟpakattīṅ kaṉiyē vāymaic coṟkuṉṟā nāvakattuḷ māṟā iṉpam tōṟṟukiṉṟa tiruvaruṭcīrc cōti yēviṇ niṟkiṉṟa cuṭarē-ac cuṭaruḷ ōṅkum nīḷoḷiyē avvoḷikkuḷ niṟainta tēvē.
translation: O golden hill! O perfection shining inside and out! O meaning within the scriptures! O sugarcane of sweet taste to those who constantly learn! O generous wish-fulfilling tree! O sweet fruit of that tree! O Jothi of divine grace's excellence, manifesting unchanging bliss within the tongues that never fail in truthful words! O flame standing in the sky! O expansive light rising within that flame! O God who fills that light!
commentary: God is the meaning hidden inside all sacred scripture, revealed as an expansive light called the Jothi. That light brings unchanging bliss to those whose tongues never fail in truthful words.

translit: tēcuvirit tiruḷakaṟṟi eṉṟum ōṅkit tikaḻkiṉṟa ceḻuṅkatirē ceṟinta vāḻkkai mācuvirit tiṭumaṉattil payilāt teyva maṇiviḷakkē āṉanta vāḻvē eṅkum kācuvirit tiṭumoḷipōl kalantu niṉṟa kāraṇamē cāntameṉak karutā niṉṟa tūcuvirit tuṭukkiṉṟōr tammai nīṅkāc cukamayamē aruṭkaruṇai tulaṅkum tēvē.
translation: O rich sun who spreads brilliance, removes darkness, and forever rises in splendor! O divine jeweled lamp who does not dwell in minds spreading the impurities of dense worldly life! O blissful life! O Primal Cause mingling everywhere like the radiating light of a gem! O embodiment of joy who never forsakes those who wear peace as their spreading garment! O God shining with graceful compassion!
commentary: A mind clouded by the dense impurities of worldly life will not hold this divine lamp. For those who wear inner peace like a garment, God is a joyful companion who never leaves.

translit: kōvē-eṇ kuṇakkuṉṟē kuṉṟā ñāṉak koḻuntēṉē ceḻumpākē kuḷirnta mōṉak kāvēmey aṟiviṉpa mayamē eṉṟaṉ kaṇṇēmuk kaṇkoṇṭa karumpē vāṉat tēvē-at tēvukkun teḷiya oṇṇāt teyvamē vāṭāmal tikaḻciṟ pōtap pūvē-ap pūviluṟu maṇamē eṅkum pūraṇamāy niṟaintaruḷum puṉitat tēvē.
translation: O King! O hill of eight attributes! O flawless thick honey of wisdom! O rich syrup! O cool grove of silence! O embodiment of true knowledge and bliss! O my eye! O sugarcane with three eyes! O God of the heavens! O Deity whom even those celestial gods cannot clearly comprehend! O unfading radiant flower of supreme consciousness! O fragrance abiding in that flower! O pure God perfectly filling everywhere with grace!
commentary: God holds every perfect attribute and gives deep wisdom, yet even the highest celestial gods cannot fully comprehend Him. He is a pure, unfading state of supreme consciousness, filling the whole universe with grace.

translit: vāṉē-av vāṉulavum kāṟṟē kāṟṟiṉ varuneruppē neruppuṟunīr vaṭivē nīril tāṉēyum puviyē-ap puviyil taṅkum tāparamē caṅkamamē cāṟṟu kiṉṟa ūṉēnal uyirē-uḷ oḷiyē uḷḷat tuṇarvē-av vuṇarvukalan tūṟu kiṉṟa tēṉēmuk kaṉiyēceṅ karumpē pākiṉ tīñcuvaiyē cuvaiyaṉaittum tiraṇṭa tēvē.
translation: O sky! O wind moving in that sky! O fire emerging from the wind! O form of water emerging from fire! O earth resting in water! O moving and unmoving things abiding on that earth! O spoken flesh! O good life! O inner light! O awareness of the heart! O honey springing forth mingled with that awareness! O threefold fruit! O red sugarcane! O sweet taste of syrup! O God who is the gathering of all tastes!
commentary: Sky, wind, fire, water, earth. The Divine unfolds as the five elements, each emerging from the one before. God is the life in moving and unmoving things, the flesh of the body, and the light of awareness in the heart. Vallalar ends in sweetness: honey, fruit, sugarcane, syrup, every joy of life gathered into a single taste.

translit: viṇṇēviṇ uruvēviṇ mutalē viṇṇuḷ veḷiyē-av veḷiviḷaṅku veḷiyē eṉṟaṉ kaṇṇēkaṇ maṇiyēkaṇ oḷiyē kaṇṇuṭ kalantuniṉṟa katirē-ak katiriṉ vittē taṇṇētaṇ matiyē-am matiyil pūtta taṇṇamutē taṇṇamuta cāra mēcol paṇṇēpaṇ ṇicaiyēpaṇ mayamē paṇṇiṉ payaṉēmeyt tavarvāḻttip paravum tēvē.
translation: O space! O form of space! O source of space! O expanse within space! O expanse shining within that expanse! O my eye! O pupil of the eye! O light of the eye! O ray standing mingled within the eye! O seed of that ray! O coolness! O cool moon! O cool ambrosia blooming in that moon! O essence of cool ambrosia! O spoken melody! O music of the melody! O embodiment of melody! O fruit of the melody! O God praised and celebrated by true ascetics!
commentary: God is the vast expanse of space and the hidden space within it. He is our very sight, the light in the eye and the seed of that light. Vallalar feels this presence as the soothing coolness of a moonlit night and as the pure essence of music.

translit: māṇēyat tavaruḷattē malarnta centā maraimalariṉ vayaṅkukiṉṟa maṇiyē ñāṉap pūṇēmeyp poruḷē-aṟ putamē mōṉap puttamutē āṉantam polinta poṟpē āṇēpeṇ uruvamē aliyē oṉṟum allāta pēroḷiyē aṉaittun tāṅkun tūṇēciṟ cukamē-ac cukamēl poṅkuñ corūpāṉan takkaṭalē cōtit tēvē.
translation: O great one! O gem shining in the red lotus flower blossoming in the hearts of those ascetics! O jewel of wisdom! O true reality! O wonder! O fresh ambrosia of silence! O golden beauty brimming with bliss! O male! O female form! O genderless one! O great light that is none of these! O pillar supporting everything! O bliss of consciousness! O ocean of natural bliss surging above that bliss! O God of Light!
commentary: People often project human traits onto God. Vallalar says the Divine appears as male, female, and genderless, yet is a great light that is actually none of these. It is the pillar holding up existence, an ocean of natural bliss found in the deep silence of the heart.

translit: pūtamē avaitōṉṟip pukunto ṭuṅkum pukaliṭamē iṭampurinta poruḷē pōṟṟum vētamē vētattiṉ viḷaivē vēta viyaṉmuṭivē ammuṭiviṉ viḷaṅkum kōvē nātamē nātānta naṭamē anta naṭattiṉaiyuḷ naṭattukiṉṟa nalamē ñāṉa pōtamē pōtamelām kaṭantu niṉṟa pūraṇamē yōkiyaruḷ polinta tēvē.
translation: O elements! O refuge where they appear, enter, and resolve! O reality that made space! O praised Vedas! O fruit of the Vedas! O vast conclusion of the Vedas! O king shining at that conclusion! O sound! O dance at the end of sound! O goodness directing that dance within! O teaching of wisdom! O perfection standing beyond all teachings! O God shining within yogis!
commentary: The physical elements are born in God and dissolve back into Him, their quiet refuge. He is the true meaning of all sacred scriptures and the cosmic dance at the very edge of sound. This perfection stands far beyond every formal teaching and doctrine.

translit: ñālamē ñālamelām viḷaṅka vaitta nāyakamē kaṟpamutal navilā niṉṟa kālamē kālamelām kaṭanta ñāṉak katiyēmeyk katiyaḷikkuṅ kaṭavu ḷēciṟ kōlamē kuṇamē-uṭ kuṟiyē kōlaṅ kuṇaṅkuṟikaḷ kaṭantuniṉṟa kuruvē aṉpar cīlamē mālaṟiyā maṉattiṟ kaṇṭa cemporuḷē umparpatañ ceḻikkum tēvē.
translation: O world! O Lord who made all worlds shine! O time spoken of from the first eon! O path of wisdom transcending all time! O God granting the true path! O form of consciousness! O quality! O inner sign! O Guru standing beyond form, qualities, and signs! O conduct of loving devotees! O perfect reality seen in a mind free of delusion! O God who makes the celestial realm flourish!
commentary: The Divine holds the world and the flow of time, and is also the path of wisdom that passes beyond both. As Guru, God stands outside every form, quality, and sign. A confused mind cannot grasp this perfect reality. It shows itself naturally to a heart full of love.

translit: tattuvamē tattuvā tīta mēciṟ cayampuvē eṅkuniṟai cāṭci yēmeyc cattuvamē cattuvattiṉ payaṉām iṉpam tantaruḷum peruvāḻvām cāmi yē-em cittanilai teḷivikkum oḷiyē caṟṟum teviṭṭāta teḷḷamutē tēṉē eṉṟum cuttaneṟi tiṟampātār aṟivil tōynta cukapporuḷē meyññāṉam tulaṅkum tēvē.
translation: O reality! O one beyond all realities! O self-manifested consciousness! O witness filling everywhere! O true goodness! O Lord who is the great life granting the bliss that is the fruit of goodness! O light that clarifies the state of our mind! O clear nectar and honey that never cloys in the least! O substance of bliss immersed in the awareness of those who never swerve from the pure path! O God shining as true wisdom!
commentary: God is the basic reality of the universe and also the truth beyond every physical and mental category (tattvas). This self-manifesting light sweeps confusion from the mind. Its sweetness never cloys, and it reveals true wisdom to those who walk the pure path of compassion.

translit: yōkamē yōkattiṉ payaṉē yōkat torumutalē yōkattiṉ ōṅkun tūya pōkamē pōkattiṉ polivē pōkam purintaruḷum puṇṇiyamē puṉita ñāṉa yākamē yākattiṉ viḷaivē yākat tiṟaiyē-av viṟaipuriyum iṉpē aṉpar mōkamē mōkamelām aḻittu vīṟu mōṉamē mōṉattiṉ muḷaitta tēvē.
translation: O Yoga! O fruit of Yoga! O unparalleled source of Yoga! O pure enjoyment rising from Yoga! O splendor of enjoyment! O merit that graciously bestows enjoyment! O pure sacrifice of wisdom! O yield of sacrifice! O Lord of sacrifice! O bliss granted by that Lord! O longing of devotees! O majestic silence that destroys all worldly delusion! O God sprouting from silence!
commentary: Whether a person sits in deep meditation (yoga) or offers wisdom as a sacrifice, God is the practice, its source and its reward all at once. Look at the last lines. A majestic inner silence destroys worldly delusion, and the true God is the light that sprouts from that very silence.

translit: kāṭciyē kāṇpatuvē ñēya mē-uḷ kaṇṇuṭaiyār kaṇṇiṟainta kaḷippē ōṅkum māṭciyē uṇmai-aṟi viṉpa meṉṉa vayaṅkukiṉṟa vāḻvēmā mavuṉak kāṇi āṭciyē āṭciceyum aracē cutta aṟivēmey aṉpēteḷ ḷamutē nalla cūṭciyēcūṭciyelām kaṭantu niṉṟa turiyamē turiyamuṭic cōtit tēvē.
translation: O vision! O the seen! O object of knowledge! O joy filling the eyes of those possessing the inner eye! O rising majesty! O life shining as truth, knowledge, and bliss! O dominion over the great estate of silence! O king who rules! O pure intelligence! O true love! O clear nectar! O supreme subtlety! O transcendent state standing beyond all subtleties! O God of light at the crown of that transcendent state!
commentary: God is the seeing, the seen, and the knowledge that comes of it. For those whose inner eye is open, the divine shines as truth, pure intelligence and true love. Vallalar then climbs through ever finer subtlety to the transcendent state of consciousness (turiya). Even that peak has a crown, and God is the light upon it.

translit: maṟaimuṭikkup poṟuttamuṟu maṇiyē ñāṉa vāritiyē aṉparkaṭam maṉattē niṉṟa kuṟaimuṭikkum kuṇakkuṉṟē kuṉṟā mōṉak kōmaḷamē tūyacivak koḻuntē veḷḷaip piṟaimuṭikkum perumāṉē tuḷava mālaip pemmāṉē ceṅkamalap pirāṉē inta iṟaimuṭikku mūvarkaṭku mēlāy niṉṟa iṟaiyē-iv vuruvumiṉṟi irunta tēvē.
translation: O fitting gem at the crown of the scriptures! O ocean of wisdom! O mountain of virtues who removes the wants in the minds of devotees! O unfading tender beauty of silence! O pure tender shoot of the Supreme! O great Lord wearing the white crescent moon! O Lord wearing the basil garland! O Lord of the red lotus! O God standing above these three crowned lords! O God existing without even this form!
commentary: Vallalar names the three crowned lords of the Hindu trinity, Siva, Vishnu and Brahma, by their symbols (the crescent moon, the basil garland, and the red lotus) only to point beyond them. The God he praises stands above all three. This God is an ocean of wisdom with no such form at all.

translit: kōtakaṉṟa yōkarmaṉak kukaiyil vāḻum kuruvēcaṇ mukaṅkoṇṭa kōvē vañca vātakaṉṟa ñāṉiyartam matiyil ūṟum vāṉamutē āṉanta maḻaiyē māyai vētakaṉṟa muttarkaḷai viḻuṅku ñāṉa vēḻamē meyyiṉpa viruntē neñcil tītakaṉṟa meyyaṭiyar tamakku vāytta celvamē ellaiyilāc cīrmait tēvē.
translation: O Guru living in the heart-cave of yogis freed from flaws! O Lord with six faces! O heavenly nectar welling in the minds of the wise freed from deceitful arguments! O rain of bliss! O elephant of wisdom that swallows the liberated ones freed from the affliction of illusion! O feast of true bliss! O wealth attained by true devotees whose hearts are freed from evil! O God of boundless excellence!
commentary: God lives as the Guru in the heart-cave of flawless yogis and as the wealth of devotees whose hearts are free of evil. Vallalar borrows familiar images, the six-faced Murugan and an elephant of wisdom, for a power so vast it swallows the very identity of the liberated seeker. That boundless inner reality is the real wealth, tasted as a feast of bliss.

translit: aruḷaruvi vaḻintuvaḻin toḻuka ōṅkum āṉantat taṉimalaiyē amala vētap poruḷaḷavu niṟaintavaṟṟiṉ mēlum ōṅkip polikiṉṟa paramporuḷē puraṇa māki iruḷaṟuciṟ pirakāca mayamāñ cutta ēkāntap peruveḷikkuḷ irunta vāḻvē teruḷaḷavum uḷamuḻutuṅ kalantu koṇṭu tittikkuñ ceḻuntēṉē tēva tēvē.
translation: O matchless mountain of bliss rising high as the waterfall of grace continuously overflows. O supreme reality filling the bounds of the pure Vedas and shining high above them. O life residing in the pure, solitary vast space, wholly formed of the light of supreme consciousness that destroys darkness. O rich honey tasting sweet, blending completely with my heart and my understanding. O God of gods.
commentary: Vast and intimate at once. God fills the pure space of consciousness and rises far above the bounds of scriptures like the Vedas. Yet that same supreme reality turns sweet as honey and blends into the heart and mind.

translit: aḷavaiyelāṅ kaṭantumaṉaṅ kaṭantu maṟṟai aṟivaiyelāṅ kaṭantukaṭan tamala yōkar uḷavaiyelāṅ kaṭantupataṅ kaṭantu mēlai oṉṟukaṭan tiraṇṭukaṭan tuṇarac cūḻnta kaḷavaiyelāṅ kaṭantaṇṭa piṇṭa mellām kaṭantuniṟai vāṉacukak kaṭalē aṉpar vaḷavaiyelām iruḷakaṟṟum oḷiyē mōṉa vāḻvē-eṉ uyirkkuyirāy vatiyum tēvē.
translation: You transcend all measures, the mind, and all other forms of knowledge. You transcend the inner workings of pure yogis, the spiritual states, the supreme one and two, and all the deceptions that obscure human understanding. You transcend the entire macrocosm and microcosm, O full ocean of heavenly bliss. O light dispelling the darkness in the homes of your devotees. O life of silence. O God abiding as the life of my life.
commentary: Nothing can measure God, not the intellect, not even the highest states of pure yogis. No physical or spiritual category holds the divine, whether it belongs to the outer universe or the inner world of the individual. And this God who transcends everything stays as close as the life within our life.

translit: vaṉpukalan taṟiyāta maṉattōr taṅkaḷ maṉaṅkalantu matikalantu vayaṅkā niṉṟa eṉpukalan tūṉkalantu pulaṉka ḷōṭum intiriya mavaikalantuḷ iyaṅku kiṉṟa aṉpukalan taṟivukalan tuyiraim pūtam āṉmāvuṅ kalantukalan taṇṇit tūṟi iṉpukalan taruḷkalantu tuḷumpip poṅki eḻuṅkaruṇaip perukkāṟē iṉpat tēvē.
translation: You blend with the minds and intellects of those whose hearts know no cruelty. You blend with the bones, the flesh, the senses, and the internal organs. You blend with love, knowledge, the life force, the five elements, and the soul, welling up with sweetness. You blend with joy and grace. O overflowing and surging great river of compassion. O God of bliss.
commentary: Where a heart holds no cruelty, God merges into the whole person. Bones, flesh, senses and soul fill with the divine like a river of sweetness rising. Compassion in the human heart draws in the compassion of God until the two can no longer be pulled apart.

translit: taṇṇamuta matikuḷirnta kiraṇam vīcat taṭampoḻiṟpū maṇamvīcat teṉṟal vīca eṇṇamutap paḷikkunilā muṟṟat tē-iṉ icaivīcat taṇpaṉinīr eṭuttu vīcap peṇṇamutam aṉaiyavarviṇ ṇamutam ūṭṭap peṟukiṉṟa cukamaṉaittum piṟpaṭ ṭōṭak kaṇṇamutat tuṭampuyirmaṟ ṟaṉaittum iṉpaṅ kalantukoḷat taruṅkaruṇaik kaṭavuḷ tēvē.
translation: The cool moon casts its chilling rays. The broad groves spread the fragrance of flowers, and the south wind blows. Sweet music plays on the crystal moonlit terrace while cool rosewater is sprinkled. Nectar-like women offer heavenly nectar. Yet all such worldly pleasures retreat and run away before you. O compassionate God, you grant a joy that permeates the eyes, the body, the soul, and everything else with nectar.
commentary: Cool moonlight, fragrant breezes from the groves, sweet music, romance. The finest pleasures of the world lose their pull once a person tastes divine grace. God's joy soaks the eyes, body and soul with sweetness, and every ordinary pleasure falls behind and runs off.

translit: cuḻiyāta aruṭkaruṇaip perukkē eṉṟun tūṇṭāta maṇiviḷakkiṉ cōti yēvāṉ oḻiyātu katirparappuñ cuṭarē aṉpark kōvāta iṉparuḷum oṉṟē viṇṇōr viḻiyālum moḻiyālum maṉatti ṉālum viḻaitarumeyt tavattālum viḷampum enta vaḻiyālum kaṇṭukoḷaṟ karitāyc cutta mavuṉaveḷi yūṭiruntu vayaṅkum tēvē.
translation: O steady flood of gracious compassion. O light of the jeweled lamp that never needs trimming. O flame that ceaselessly spreads its rays across the sky. O Supreme One granting ceaseless bliss to devotees. You remain impossible to perceive through the eyes, words, or minds of the celestials. You cannot be reached through arduous true penance or any described path. O God shining from within the pure space of silence.
commentary: Even the heavenly gods cannot reach the supreme divine through traditional penance, intellectual effort, or any established spiritual path. God is an endless, steady flame of compassion that requires no tending. This boundless light is found only in the pure space of inner silence, beyond every described path.

translit: colloḻiyap poruḷoḻiyak karaṇa mellām cōrntoḻiya uṇarvoḻiyat tuḷaṅkā niṉṟa alloḻiyap pakaloḻiya naṭuvē niṉṟa āṉanta anupavamē atīta vāḻvē nelloḻiyap patarkoḷvār pōla iṉpa niṟaivoḻiyak kuṟaikoṇmata neṟiyōr neñcak kalloḻiya meyyaṭiyar itaya mellāṅ kalantukalan tiṉikkiṉṟa karuṇait tēvē.
translation: When words cease, when meaning ceases, when all inner instruments grow weary and fade, when sensation ceases, when the unwavering night and day cease, you remain in the center as the blissful experience and the transcendent life. Followers of religious paths discard the fullness of bliss and embrace flaws, like those who throw away the rice grain and gather the chaff. You stay away from their stony hearts, endlessly mingling and tasting sweet in all the hearts of true devotees. O God of compassion.
commentary: God is found in the stillness beyond words, thoughts, and ordinary sensations. Vallalar says plainly that the followers of religious paths miss this truth entirely. He says they throw away the nourishing rice of true bliss to gather the empty chaff of flaws and doctrines, which turns their hearts to stone. The divine presence avoids these stony hearts, choosing instead to mingle and taste sweet in the open hearts of true devotees.

translit: alaikaṭalum puvivaraiyum aṉalkāl nīrum antaramum maṟṟai-aki lāṇṭam yāvum nilaikulaiyā vaṇṇamaruḷ veḷiyi ṉūṭu nirainiraiyā niṟutti-uyir nikaḻum vaṇṇam talaikulaiyāt tattuvañcey tirōtai yeṉṉum taṉiyāṇai naṭatti-aruḷ talattil eṉṟum malaivaṟavīṟ ṟiruntaruḷum aracē mutti vaḻittuṇaiyē viḻittuṇaiyuḷ maṇiyām tēvē.
translation: You arrange the rolling oceans, the earth, fire, wind, water, the sky, and all other universes row upon row within the space of grace, ensuring they never lose their stability. For the sake of living souls, you enact your supreme command of obscuration to establish the unshakeable principles of existence. O King who graciously presides forever without confusion in the realm of grace. O companion on the path to liberation. O God who is the pupil in the eyes that guide me.
commentary: Grace holds the whole universe in place, setting the oceans, the elements and countless worlds row upon row and keeping them steady. For the sake of living souls, God governs every cosmic force, even the power that hides the truth for a while so souls can act and learn in the physical world. The same King who runs all this walks beside each soul as its companion toward freedom.

translit: varampaḻutta neṟiyēmeyn neṟiyil iṉpa vaḷampaḻutta peruvāḻvē vāṉōr taṅkaḷ cirampaḻutta patapporuḷē aṟivā ṉantac civampaḻutta anupavamē citākā cattil parampaḻutta naṭattaracē karuṇai eṉṉum paḻampaḻutta vāṉtaruvē parama ñāṉat tirampaḻutta yōkiyartam yōkat tuḷḷē tiṉampaḻuttuk kaṉinta-aruṭ celvat tēvē.
translation: O path of ripened boons. O great life brimming with the ripened wealth of bliss on the path of truth. O supreme meaning that ripens upon the heads of celestial beings.
