translit: kūṟāta vāḻkkaic ciṟumaiyai nōkkik kuṟittiṭumeṉ tēṟāta viṇṇappam caṟṟēṉum niṉṟaṉ tirucceviyil ēṟāta vaṇṇameṉ oṟṟit tiyākar iṭappuṟattiṉ māṟā tamarnta mayilē vaṭivuṭai māṇikkamē.
translation: Looking at the unspeakable baseness of my life, I make a confused appeal. It does not enter your holy ears even a little, O peacock seated constantly on the left side of my Lord Thyagar of Otriyur! O Vadivudai Manikkam!
commentary: Despair can make the divine feel distant and deaf to prayer. Weighed down by his shortcomings, Vallalar feels his confused cries are not reaching her ears. He pictures her seated peacefully beside Lord Siva, seemingly unaware of his struggle.

translit: ōyā iṭarkoṇ ṭulaivēṉuk kaṉpark kutavutalpōl īyā viṭiṉumōr eḷḷaḷa vēṉum iraṅkukaṇṭāy cāyā aruḷtarum tāyē eḻiloṟṟit taṟparaiyē māyā nalamaruḷ vāḻvē vaṭivuṭai māṇikkamē.
translation: I suffer with ceaseless afflictions. Even if you do not grant me the help you give your true devotees, please show me at least a sesame seed's measure of pity. O Mother who gives unfading grace! O Supreme Goddess of beautiful Otriyur! O Life that grants imperishable goodness! O Vadivudai Manikkam!
commentary: True devotion earns boundless grace, and Vallalar feels he deserves none of it. So he asks for the smallest fraction of pity, a sesame seed's worth, to ease his endless suffering.

translit: perumpētai yēṉciṟu vāḻkkait tuyareṉum pēralaiyil turumpē eṉa-alai kiṉṟēṉ puṇainiṉ tuṇaippatamē karumpē karuṇaik kaṭalē aruṇmuk kaṉinaṟavē varumpēr aruḷoṟṟi vāḻvē vaṭivuṭai māṇikkamē.
translation: I am a great fool. I am tossed about like a piece of straw in the massive wave of sorrow in this petty life. Your pair of feet is my only raft. O sugarcane! O ocean of compassion! O honey of the three gracious fruits! O Life of Otriyur with abounding great grace! O Vadivudai Manikkam!
commentary: Ordinary worldly life can feel like a vast ocean of sorrow. Vallalar sees himself as a helpless bit of straw tossed on its waves. The Goddess is the only raft he has to cling to.

translit: kātara vāluṭ kalaṅkiniṉ ṟēṉniṉ kaṭaikkaṇaruḷ ātara vālmakiḻ kiṉṟēṉ iṉi-uṉ aṭaikkalamē cītaraṉ ēttum tiruvoṟṟi nātartam tēvi-eḻil mātara cē-oṟṟi vāḻvē vaṭivuṭai māṇikkamē.
translation: I stood inwardly shaken by fear. I now rejoice in the supportive grace of your side-glance. Henceforth I take refuge in you. O Consort of the Lord of Otriyur praised by Vishnu! O beautiful Queen among women! O Life of Otriyur! O Vadivudai Manikkam!
commentary: Fear had shaken him inside. One protective glance from the corner of the Goddess's eye turns it to joy, and comforted by that small sign of grace, Vallalar surrenders completely and takes permanent refuge in her care.

translit: poṉṉuṭai yāraṉṟip pōṟṟunaṟ kalvip poruḷuṭaiyār eṉṉuṭai yāreṉa ēcukiṉ ṟāriḵ teṉṉai-aṉṉē miṉṉuṭai yāymiṉṉil tuṉṉiṭai yāyoṟṟi mēvumukkaṇ maṉṉuṭai yāyeṉ ṉuṭaiyāy vaṭivuṭai māṇikkamē.
translation: People mock me, asking what I possess since I have no gold and lack the wealth of praiseworthy good education. What is this, Mother? O you who possess the radiance of lightning! O you with a waist as slender as lightning! You possess the three-eyed King who resides in Otriyur. O you who possess me! O Vadivudai Manikkam!
commentary: The world judges a person's worth by money and formal education. When people mock Vallalar for having neither, he turns to the Goddess. His true wealth is simply that he belongs to her.

translit: poyviṭṭi ṭātavaṉ neñcakat tēṉaip pulampumvaṇṇam kaiviṭṭi ṭātiṉṉum kāppāy atuniṉ kaṭaṉkarumpē meyviṭṭi ṭāruḷ viḷai-iṉpa mē-oṟṟi vittakamē maiviṭṭi ṭāviḻi māṉē vaṭivuṭai māṇikkamē.
translation: I have a hard heart that never abandons falsehood. Please do not forsake me to lamentation. Continue to protect me. That is your duty, O sugarcane! O bliss that blossoms in the hearts of those who never abandon truth! O marvel of Otriyur! O deer with eyes lined with kohl! O Vadivudai Manikkam!
commentary: A mother protects her child whatever the child's failures. Vallalar admits plainly that his heart still clings to falsehood, and he asks for her protection anyway, resting his whole case on that maternal bond.

translit: nēyāṉu kūla maṉamuṭai yāyiṉi nīyumeṉṟaṉ tāyākil yāṉuṉ taṉaiyaṉum ākileṉ taṉuḷattil ōyā tuṟuntuyar ellām tavirttaruḷ oṟṟiyilcev vāyār amuta vaṭivē vaṭivuṭai māṇikkamē.
translation: O Vadivudai Manikkam, form of nectar with red lips in Otriyur! You possess a heart full of loving grace. If you are indeed my mother and I am your son, please banish all the ceaseless sorrow that fills my heart.
commentary: A child has a natural right to run to its mother for comfort. Vallalar comes to the Goddess Vadivudai Manikkam purely as her son. If the bond is real, let her prove it by clearing away his unending sorrow.

translit: vāḻiniṉ cēvaṭi pōṟṟiniṉ pūmpata vāricaṅkaḷ vāḻiniṉ tāṇmalar pōṟṟiniṉ taṇṇaḷi vāḻiniṉcīr vāḻi-eṉ uḷḷattil nīyuniṉ oṟṟi makiḻnarumnī vāḻi-eṉ āruyir vāḻvē vaṭivuṭai māṇikkamē.
translation: Long live your red feet. Praise to your lotus-like flower feet. Long live your blossoming feet. Praise to your cool grace. Long live your glory. May you and your beloved Lord of Otriyur live long in my heart. Long may you live, O life of my precious soul, O Vadivudai Manikkam!
commentary: Vallalar closes his appeal with a steady rhythm of praise and blessing for her feet, her grace and her glory. His last prayer is that his own heart become a permanent home for her and her beloved Lord.

note: Editor's note: the source's theme lines: a poem of praise (pāṭāṇ tiṇai, பாடாண் திணை), in the mode where a human woman longs for a god (kaṭavuṇmāṭṭu māṉiṭap peṇṭir nayanta pakkam, கடவுண்மாட்டு மானிடப் பெண்டிர் நயந்த பக்கம்), told as question and answer (viṉā uttaram, வினா உத்தரம்).
translit: aṉparpāl nīṅkā-eṉ ammaiyē tāmaraimēṟ poṉporuvu mēṉi ayaṉpūviṉ-maṉperiya vākkiṟaivi niṉtāḷ malarccaraṇam pōntēṉaik kākkak kaṭaṉuṉakkē kāṇ.
translation: My mother who never departs from devotees! Goddess of the great word, dwelling on the flower of Brahma whose body is like gold! It is your duty to protect me, who has sought refuge at your lotus feet.
commentary: A prayer to the goddess of speech and learning opens the work. She is the mother who never leaves those who love her, and Vallalar asks her to protect him and guide his words.

tamil: ஒருமா முகனை யொருமாவை யூர்வா கனமா யுறநோக்கித்
திருமான் முதலோர் சிறுமையெலாந் தீர்த்தெம் மிருகண் மணியாகிக்
கருமா லகற்றுங் கணபதியாங் கடவு ளடியுங் களித்தவர்பின்
வருமா கருணைக் கடற்குமர வள்ள லடியும் வணங்குவாம்.
translit: orumā mukaṉai yorumāvai yūrvā kaṉamā yuṟanōkkit tirumāṉ mutalōr ciṟumaiyelān tīrttem mirukaṇ maṇiyākik karumā lakaṟṟuṅ kaṇapatiyāṅ kaṭavu ḷaṭiyuṅ kaḷittavarpiṉ varumā karuṇaik kaṭaṟkumara vaḷḷa laṭiyum vaṇaṅkuvām.
translation: We bow to the feet of the elephant-faced God Vinayakar, who rides an animal vehicle, who removed the distress of Vishnu and other gods, who becomes the pupil of our two eyes and dispels dark delusion. Following Him, we also bow to the feet of the benevolent Lord Kumara, the great ocean of compassion, who joyfully comes after Him.
commentary: Vinayakar, the elephant-faced god, is said to clear away the darkness of spiritual delusion, so he is honored first. Then Vallalar bows to Kumara, the Lord of compassion. Seeking their blessings before a major work begins is the old custom.

tamil: திருவார் கமலத் தடம்பணைசூழ் செல்வப் பெருஞ்சீ ரொற்றியில்வாழ்
மருவார் கொன்றைச் சடைமுடிகொள் வள்ள லிவர்க்குப் பலிகொடுநா
னொருவா தடைந்தே னினிநமக்கிங் குதவ வருந்தோ றுன்முலைமே
லிருவா ரிடுநீ யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: tiruvār kamalat taṭampaṇaicūḻ celvap peruñcī roṟṟiyilvāḻ maruvār koṉṟaic caṭaimuṭikoḷ vaḷḷa livarkkup palikoṭunā ṉoruvā taṭaintē ṉiṉinamakkiṅ kutava varuntō ṟuṉmulaimē liruvā riṭunī yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This benevolent Lord wears a crown of matted hair adorned with fragrant konrai flowers. He lives in wealthy, glorious Otriyur, surrounded by vast fields of beautiful lotuses. Giving Him alms, I became unseparated from Him. He says to me, "From now on, whenever I come here to help you, place two bands upon your breasts." What is this, my friend?
commentary: The woman tells her friend about the Lord of Otriyur, who comes to her door as a wandering beggar. She gives him alms, and he answers with teasing, intimate instructions. Under the play lie hidden meanings about the soul's loving union with God.

tamil: தண்ணார் மலரை மதிநதியைத் தாங்குஞ் சடையா ரிவர்தமைநா
னண்ணா லொற்றி யிருந்தவரே யைய ரேநீர் யாரென்றே
னண்ணா ரிடத்து மம்பலத்து நடவா தவர்நா மென்றுசொலி
யெண்ணா தருகே வருகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: taṇṇār malarai matinatiyait tāṅkuñ caṭaiyā rivartamainā ṉaṇṇā loṟṟi yiruntavarē yaiya rēnīr yāreṉṟē ṉaṇṇā riṭattu mampalattu naṭavā tavarnā meṉṟucoli yeṇṇā tarukē varukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: He has matted hair bearing a cool flower, the moon, and the river. I asked Him, "O exalted one residing in Otriyur! O Lord, who are you?" He replied, "We do not walk among enemies, but we are the dancer in the Hall." Saying this, He approaches me without hesitation. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks the wandering Lord who he really is. His answer is a riddle: he is the dancer in the divine hall of truth, who never walks among foes. Then he steps right up to her. This God is near and deeply personal, and he keeps no distance.

tamil: பிட்டி னதிமண் சுமந்தவொற்றிப் பிச்சைத் தேவ ரிவர்தமைநான்
றட்டின் மலர்க்கை யிடத்தெதுவோ தனத்தைப் பிடியு மென்றுரைத்தேன்
மட்டி னொருமூன் றுடனேழு மத்தர் தலையீ தென்றுசொலி
யெட்டி முலையைப் பிடிக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: piṭṭi ṉatimaṇ cumantavoṟṟip piccait tēva rivartamaināṉ ṟaṭṭiṉ malarkkai yiṭattetuvō taṉattaip piṭiyu meṉṟuraittēṉ maṭṭi ṉorumūṉ ṟuṭaṉēḻu mattar talaiyī teṉṟucoli yeṭṭi mulaiyaip piṭikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: He is the mendicant Lord of Otriyur who carried river sand for the sake of sweet pudding. I asked Him, "What do you hold in your tray-like lotus hand? Please take this wealth." He replied, "This is the head of a madman," and reaching out, He grabbed my breast. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She offers the beggar wealth, using a word that also means a woman's breast. He takes the second meaning and reaches out to touch her. Through this romantic banter the soul surrenders completely, without fear.

tamil: மடையிற் கயல்பா யொற்றிநகர் வள்ள லாகு மிவர்தமைநா
னடையிற் கனிவாற் பணியென்றே யருளீ ருரியீ ருடையென்றேன்
கடையிற் படுமோர் பணியென்றே கருதி யுரைத்தே மென்றுரைத்தென்
னிடையிற் கலையை யுரிகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: maṭaiyiṟ kayalpā yoṟṟinakar vaḷḷa lāku mivartamainā ṉaṭaiyiṟ kaṉivāṟ paṇiyeṉṟē yaruḷī ruriyī ruṭaiyeṉṟēṉ kaṭaiyiṟ paṭumōr paṇiyeṉṟē karuti yuraittē meṉṟuraitteṉ ṉiṭaiyiṟ kalaiyai yurikiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I told this benefactor of Otri city, where carp leap in the water channels, "Graciously bestow a task when I tenderly approach you, you have the right." He said, "We thought you were speaking of a lowly garment," and he strips the dress from my waist. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks the Lord for some task in his service and grants that he has the right to command her. He pretends to mishear, taking "task" as a garment and his "right" as leave to pull it from her waist. The double meanings show how intimate and teasing the bond between the soul and the divine can be.

tamil: மன்றன் மணக்கு மொற்றிநகர் வாண ராகு மிவர்தமைநா
னின்றன் பொடுங்கை யேந்தனத்தை யேற்றோர் கலத்திற் கொளுமென்றே
னன்றன் புடையா யெண்கலத்தி னாங்கொண் டிடுவே மென்றுசொலி
யென்றன் முலையைத் தொடுகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: maṉṟaṉ maṇakku moṟṟinakar vāṇa rāku mivartamainā ṉiṉṟaṉ poṭuṅkai yēntaṉattai yēṟṟōr kalattiṟ koḷumeṉṟē ṉaṉṟaṉ puṭaiyā yeṇkalatti ṉāṅkoṇ ṭiṭuvē meṉṟucoli yeṉṟaṉ mulaiyait toṭukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I told this resident of Otri city, which is fragrant with blossoms, "Accept the alms I hold in my hand with love today, and take it in one vessel." He said, "O good loving one, we will take it in eight vessels," and he touches my breasts. What is this, my friend?
commentary: The heroine offers food to the wandering Lord, asking him to receive it in his single begging bowl. He replies with a pun on the word for vessel, changing her innocent offering into an excuse to touch her intimately. The poem portrays the divine as a playful lover.

tamil: கோமாற் கருளுந் திருவொற்றிக் கோயி லுடையா ரிவரைமத
மாமாற் றியநீ ரேகலவி மகிழ்ந்தின் றடியேன் மனையினிடைத்
தாமாற் றிடக்கொண் டேகுமென்றேன் றாவென் றார்தந் தாலென்னை
யேமாற் றினையே யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: kōmāṟ karuḷun tiruvoṟṟik kōyi luṭaiyā rivaraimata māmāṟ ṟiyanī rēkalavi makiḻntiṉ ṟaṭiyēṉ maṉaiyiṉiṭait tāmāṟ ṟiṭakkoṇ ṭēkumeṉṟēṉ ṟāveṉ ṟārtan tāleṉṉai yēmāṟ ṟiṉaiyē yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I told this Lord of the holy Otri temple who grants grace to the king, "You who dispelled the great illusion of pride, rejoice in union today and come to my house to relieve my distress." He said, "Give it." When I gave it, he says, "You have deceived me!" What is this, my friend?
commentary: She invites the Lord home to relieve her distress and enjoy their union. He demands a gift, and when she yields, he playfully accuses her of deceiving him. That tension mirrors the soul's desperate longing for God, and the grace that always arrives in ways she did not expect.

tamil: அம்மா லயனுங் காண்பரியீர்க் கமரும் பதிதான் யாதென்றே
னிம்மா லுடையா யொற்றுதற்கோ ரெச்ச மதுகண் டறியென்றார்
செம்மா லிஃதொன் றென்னென்றேன் றிருவே புரிமேற் சேர்கின்ற
வெம்மான் மற்றொன் றென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: ammā layaṉuṅ kāṇpariyīrk kamarum patitāṉ yāteṉṟē ṉimmā luṭaiyā yoṟṟutaṟkō recca matukaṇ ṭaṟiyeṉṟār cemmā liḵtoṉ ṟeṉṉeṉṟēṉ ṟiruvē purimēṟ cērkiṉṟa vemmāṉ maṟṟoṉ ṟeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked, "You who are rare for Vishnu and Brahma to see, what is the town where you abide?" He said, "O infatuated one, find the word remaining after Otri and know it." I asked, "What is this perfect greatness?" He says, "O beautiful one, it is another of our deer joining the town." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks where he lives. He tells her, in a riddle, to find the word that comes after Otri (meaning ūr, the word for town, which completes the city name Otriyur). When she praises his greatness, he puns again on the deer he traditionally holds in his hand and keeps her off balance with his wit.

tamil: கண்கள் களிப்ப வீண்டுநிற்குங் கள்வ ரிவரூ ரொற்றியதாம்
பண்க ளியன்ற திருவாயாற் பலிதா வென்றார் கொடுவந்தேன்
பெண்க டரலீ தன்றென்றார் பேசப் பலியா தென்றேனின்
னெண்கண் பலித்த தென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: kaṇkaḷ kaḷippa vīṇṭuniṟkuṅ kaḷva rivarū roṟṟiyatām paṇka ḷiyaṉṟa tiruvāyāṟ palitā veṉṟār koṭuvantēṉ peṇka ṭaralī taṉṟeṉṟār pēcap paliyā teṉṟēṉiṉ ṉeṇkaṇ palitta teṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: He stands here delighting the eyes, a thief whose town is Otri. With his divine mouth naturally suited for melodies, he said, "Give alms." I brought it. He said, "This is not what women should give." I said, "Talking will not bear fruit." He says, "Your intention has borne fruit." What is this, my friend?
commentary: He asks for alms, she brings food, and he tells her this is not the gift a woman should give. She complains that talking with him yields no fruit. His pun comes right back: her secret desire for him has already borne fruit. God sees past the offering to the love hidden in the soul.

tamil: ஆரா மகிழ்வு தருமொருபே ரழக ரிவரூ ரொற்றியதா
நேராய் விருந்துண் டோவென்றார் நீர்தான் வேறிங் கிலையென்றேன்
வாரார் முலையாய் வாயமுது மலர்க்கை யமுது மனையமுது
மேரா யுளவே யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: ārā makiḻvu tarumorupē raḻaka rivarū roṟṟiyatā nērāy viruntuṇ ṭōveṉṟār nīrtāṉ vēṟiṅ kilaiyeṉṟēṉ vārār mulaiyāy vāyamutu malarkkai yamutu maṉaiyamutu mērā yuḷavē yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This great beauty who gives endless joy says his town is Otriyur. He directly asked, "Is there a feast?" I told him, "There is nothing else for you here." He replies, "O woman with bound breasts, the nectar of your mouth, the nectar of your flower-like hands, and the nectar of your house are all beautifully present here." What is this, my friend?
commentary: He arrives at her door asking for a feast. She has no ordinary food to give, and he answers that her sweet presence and her devotion are the only feast he wants. This is a traditional poetic way of saying God desires the devotee's total love above any physical offering.

tamil: அடுத்தார்க் கருளு மொற்றிநக ரைய ரிவர்தா மிகத்தாகங்
கடுத்தா மென்றார் கடிதடநீர் கண்டீ ரையங் கொளுமென்றேன்
கொடுத்தாய் கண்ட திலையையங் கொள்ளு மிடஞ்சூழ்ந் திடுங்கலையை
யெடுத்தாற் காண்பே மென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: aṭuttārk karuḷu moṟṟinaka raiya rivartā mikattākaṅ kaṭuttā meṉṟār kaṭitaṭanīr kaṇṭī raiyaṅ koḷumeṉṟēṉ koṭuttāy kaṇṭa tilaiyaiyaṅ koḷḷu miṭañcūḻn tiṭuṅkalaiyai yeṭuttāṟ kāṇpē meṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This Lord of Otriyur, who grants grace to those who approach him, said, "My thirst is very severe." I told him, "See the water in the pot, please take some." He replies, "You offered it, but I have not seen it. If you lift the garment wrapped around the place where one takes it, we shall see it." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She offers the thirsty Lord water from a household pot. He teases her, pretending he cannot see it, and asks her to lift the cloth covering it. Vallalar borrows the bold language of a flirtatious lover to describe the startling intimacy between God and the soul.

tamil: இந்தா ரிதழி யிலங்குசடை யேந்த லிவரூ ரொற்றியதாம்
வந்தார் பெண்ணே யமுதென்றார் வரையின் சுதையிங் குண்டென்றே
னந்தார் குழலாய் பசிக்கினும்பெண் ணாசை விடுமோ வமுதின்றே
லெந்தா ரந்தா வென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: intā ritaḻi yilaṅkucaṭai yēnta livarū roṟṟiyatām vantār peṇṇē yamuteṉṟār varaiyiṉ cutaiyiṅ kuṇṭeṉṟē ṉantār kuḻalāy pacikkiṉumpeṇ ṇācai viṭumō vamutiṉṟē lentā rantā veṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This Lord with shining matted hair adorned with a cool garland of konrai flowers says his town is Otriyur. He came and asked, "O woman, give me nectar." I told him, "There is mountain nectar here." He replies, "O woman with beautiful hair, even if one is hungry, does the desire for a woman ever leave? If there is no nectar, give me your beautiful garland." What is this, my friend?
commentary: He asks for nectar, and she takes him literally, offering sweet mountain honey. He turns the talk back to love. If she cannot give him the nectar of her affection, then let him have the garland she wears. The passionate longing of lovers mirrors the bond between the divine and the devotee.

tamil: தன்னந் தனியா யிங்குநிற்குஞ் சாமி யிவரூ ரொற்றியதா
மன்னந் தருவீ ரென்றார்நா னழைத்தே னின்னை யன்னமிட
முன்னம் பசிபோ யிற்றென்றார் முன்னின் றகன்றே னிவ்வன்ன
மின்னந் தருவா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: taṉṉan taṉiyā yiṅkuniṟkuñ cāmi yivarū roṟṟiyatā maṉṉan taruvī reṉṟārnā ṉaḻaittē ṉiṉṉai yaṉṉamiṭa muṉṉam pacipō yiṟṟeṉṟār muṉṉiṉ ṟakaṉṟē ṉivvaṉṉa miṉṉan taruvā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This Lord standing here all alone says his town is Otriyur. He asked, "Will you give me food?" I invited him inside to serve a meal. He said, "My hunger is already gone." I stood before him and then moved away. He says, "You must give me this swan once again." What is this, my friend?
commentary: Everything turns on annam (a term meaning both food and a graceful swan). She offers a meal, he says his hunger has vanished, and he asks instead for the beautiful swan standing before him. No material gift will do. God is seeking the devotee herself.

tamil: மாறா வழகோ டிங்குநிற்கும் வள்ள லிவரூ ரொற்றியதாம்
வீறா முணவீ யென்றார்நீர் மேவா வுணவிங் குண்டென்றேன்
கூறா மகிழ்வே கொடுவென்றார் கொடுத்தா லிதுதா னன்றென்றே
யேறா வழக்குத் தொடுக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: māṟā vaḻakō ṭiṅkuniṟkum vaḷḷa livarū roṟṟiyatām vīṟā muṇavī yeṉṟārnīr mēvā vuṇaviṅ kuṇṭeṉṟēṉ kūṟā makiḻvē koṭuveṉṟār koṭuttā litutā ṉaṉṟeṉṟē yēṟā vaḻakkut toṭukkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This benevolent Lord standing here with unfading beauty says his town is Otriyur. He asked, "Give me excellent food." I told him, "There is food here that will not suit you." He replied, "Give me unspoken joy." When I offered it, he said, "This is not right" and picks an unjustifiable argument. What is this, my friend?
commentary: He turns down ordinary food and demands unspoken joy. When she tries to offer that deep devotion, he rejects it too, only to draw her into a lover's quarrel. The divine pulls the soul closer in ways that can confuse her, and always in ways that are deeply personal.

tamil: வண்மை யுடையார் திருவொற்றி வாண ரிவர்தாம் பலியென்றா
ருண்மை யறிவீர் பலியெண்மை யுணர்கி லீரென் னுழையென்றேன்
பெண்மை சிறந்தாய் நின்மனையிற் பேசும் பலிக்கென் றடைந்ததுநா
மெண்மை யுணர்ந்தே யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vaṇmai yuṭaiyār tiruvoṟṟi vāṇa rivartām paliyeṉṟā ruṇmai yaṟivīr paliyeṇmai yuṇarki līreṉ ṉuḻaiyeṉṟēṉ peṇmai ciṟantāy niṉmaṉaiyiṟ pēcum palikkeṉ ṟaṭaintatunā meṇmai yuṇarntē yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: The generous resident of Otriyur asked for alms. I said, "You who know the truth, do you not realize how meager the alms are at my place?" He says, "O excellent woman, we came for the alms spoken of in your house, fully aware of that meagerness." What is this, my friend?
commentary: He asks for alms, and she warns him there is very little to give at her house. He answers that he knew exactly how meager it was before he came. God wants the simple love of the devotee and accepts it fully, however small or humble it looks.

tamil: திருவை யளிக்குந் திருவொற்றித் தேவ ரீர்க்கென் விழைவென்றேன்
வெருவ லுனது பெயரிடையோர் மெய்நீக் கியநின் முகமென்றார்
தருவ லதனை வெளிப்படையாற் சாற்று மென்றேன் சாற்றுவனே
லிருவை மடவா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: tiruvai yaḷikkun tiruvoṟṟit tēva rīrkkeṉ viḻaiveṉṟēṉ veruva luṉatu peyariṭaiyōr meynīk kiyaniṉ mukameṉṟār taruva lataṉai veḷippaṭaiyāṟ cāṟṟu meṉṟēṉ cāṟṟuvaṉē liruvai maṭavā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked the Lord of Otriyur who grants wealth, "What is your desire?" He replied, "Do not fear, it is your face, with one consonant removed from the middle of your name." I said, "I will give it, just state it plainly." He says, "If I state it, you will remain seated, O naive girl." What is this, my friend?
commentary: Asked what he desires, the Lord answers with a riddle about her name. When she begs him to speak plainly, he teases that the true answer would freeze her where she sits. The banter shows how intimate the bond is, with God acting as a mysterious, teasing lover.

tamil: முந்தை மறையோன் புகழொற்றி முதல்வ ரிவர்தம் முகநோக்கிக்
கந்தை யுடையீ ரென்னென்றேன் கழியா வுன்றன் மொழியாலே
யிந்து முகத்தா யெமக்கொன்றே யிருநான் குனக்குக் கந்தையுள
திந்த வியப்பென் னென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: muntai maṟaiyōṉ pukaḻoṟṟi mutalva rivartam mukanōkkik kantai yuṭaiyī reṉṉeṉṟēṉ kaḻiyā vuṉṟaṉ moḻiyālē yintu mukattā yemakkoṉṟē yirunāṉ kuṉakkuk kantaiyuḷa tinta viyappeṉ ṉeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: Looking at the face of this Primal Lord of Otriyur praised by the ancient creator Brahma, I asked, "Why do you wear a rag?" He says, "O moon-faced girl, going by your own unfailing words, we have only one rag while you have eight. What is this wonder?" What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks why he wears a beggar's rag. He turns the question back on her with a pun, claiming she wears eight rags to his one. Read spiritually, God wears only a single cloth of detachment, while the human soul is weighed down by eight heavy layers of worldly illusion.

tamil: துன்ன லுடையா ரிவர்தமைநீர் துன்னும் பதிதான் யாதென்றே
னென்ன லிரவி லெமைத்தெளிவா னின்ற நினது பெயரென்றா
ருன்ன லுறுவீர் வெளிப்படவீ துரைப்பீ ரென்றே னுரைப்பேனே
லின்ன லடைவா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: tuṉṉa luṭaiyā rivartamainīr tuṉṉum patitāṉ yāteṉṟē ṉeṉṉa liravi lemaitteḷivā ṉiṉṟa niṉatu peyareṉṟā ruṉṉa luṟuvīr veḷippaṭavī turaippī reṉṟē ṉuraippēṉē liṉṉa laṭaivā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked this Lord who wears stitched garments, "What is the town you inhabit?" He replied, "It is your name, which stands making us clear in the night." I said, "You who think deeply, tell me this plainly." He says, "If I say it, you will suffer distress." What is this, my friend?
commentary: A simple question about his hometown gets another poetic riddle. He hints that his town shares a name with something about her that brings light in the darkness, like a lamp or the moon. He won't say it outright, joking that the real answer would only bring her trouble.

tamil: சிமைக்கொள் சூலத் திருமலர்க்கைத் தேவர் நீரெங் கிருந்ததென்றே
னெமைக்கண் டளவின் மாதேநீ யிருந்த தெனயா மிருந்ததென்றா
ரமைக்கு மொழியிங் கிதமென்றே னாமுன் மொழியிங் கிதமன்றோ
விமைக்கு மிழையா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: cimaikkoḷ cūlat tirumalarkkait tēvar nīreṅ kiruntateṉṟē ṉemaikkaṇ ṭaḷaviṉ mātēnī yirunta teṉayā miruntateṉṟā ramaikku moḻiyiṅ kitameṉṟē ṉāmuṉ moḻiyiṅ kitamaṉṟō vimaikku miḻaiyā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked the Lord who holds the towering trident in his beautiful lotus hand, "Where were you?" He replied, "O lady, as soon as you saw us, where you were is where we were." I said, "Your composed words are pleasing here." He says, "Were our previous words not pleasing here, O girl with blinking eyes?" What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks where he has been. He says he was right beside her from the very moment she looked at him. God is present the instant a person turns their attention to him. Then he playfully questions her compliment, just to keep the banter going.

tamil: நடங்கொள் பதத்தீர் திருவொற்றி நங்கள் பெருமா னீரன்றோ
திடங்கொள் புகழ்க்கச் சூரிடஞ்சேர்ந் தீரென் றேனின் னடுநோக்காக்
குடஞ்சேர்ந் ததுமாங் கஃதென்றார் குடம்யா தென்றே னஃதறிதற்
கிடங்கர் நடுநீக் கென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: naṭaṅkoḷ patattīr tiruvoṟṟi naṅkaḷ perumā ṉīraṉṟō tiṭaṅkoḷ pukaḻkkac cūriṭañcērn tīreṉ ṟēṉiṉ ṉaṭunōkkāk kuṭañcērn tatumāṅ kaḵteṉṟār kuṭamyā teṉṟē ṉaḵtaṟitaṟ kiṭaṅkar naṭunīk keṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord with dancing feet, are you not our Lord of Otriyur? Have you reached the highly praised town of Kaccur?" I asked. He looked at my waist and replied, "A pot has also reached there." I asked, "What is this pot?" He said, "To know that, remove the middle of the word for crocodile." What is this, my friend?
commentary: Now they speak entirely in riddles. She asks whether he has visited the town of Kaccur, and he answers with a Tamil word puzzle built on the word for crocodile, teasing her about the shape of her waist. This bond with the divine is intimate and full of humor, far from formal ritual.

tamil: சங்க மருவு மொற்றியுளீர் சடைமே லிருந்த தென்னென்றேன்
மங்கை நினது முன்பருவ மருவு முதனீத் திருந்ததென்றார்
கங்கை யிருந்த தேயென்றேன் கமலை யனையாய் கழுக்கடையு
மெங்கை யிருந்த தென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: caṅka maruvu moṟṟiyuḷīr caṭaimē lirunta teṉṉeṉṟēṉ maṅkai niṉatu muṉparuva maruvu mutaṉīt tiruntateṉṟār kaṅkai yirunta tēyeṉṟēṉ kamalai yaṉaiyāy kaḻukkaṭaiyu meṅkai yirunta teṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of Otriyur where conches gather, what rests on your matted hair?" I asked. He said, "O young woman, it is your previous stage of youth with its first letter removed." I said, "It is the river Ganges." He replied, "O woman resembling Lakshmi, the trident is also in my hand." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks what rests in his matted hair, already knowing it is the river goddess Ganges. Siva turns the Tamil words for the stages of a woman's life into a clever puzzle. Once she solves it, he reminds her that he also carries a sharp trident, and the banter stays lively and unpredictable.

tamil: துதிசே ரொற்றி வளர்தரும துரையே நீர்முன் னாடலுறும்
பதியா தென்றே னம்பெயர்முற் பகரீ ரெழுத்தைப் பறித்ததென்றார்
நிதிசேர்ந் திடுமப் பெயர்யாது நிகழ்த்து மென்றே னீயிட்ட
தெதுவோ வதுகா ணென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: tuticē roṟṟi vaḷartaruma turaiyē nīrmuṉ ṉāṭaluṟum patiyā teṉṟē ṉampeyarmuṟ pakarī reḻuttaip paṟittateṉṟār niticērn tiṭumap peyaryātu nikaḻttu meṉṟē ṉīyiṭṭa tetuvō vatukā ṇeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord residing in praise-filled Otriyur, what is the town where you danced before?" I asked. He replied, "It is our name with the first two letters removed." I asked, "What is that name filled with wealth? Tell me." He said, "It is whatever name you bestowed." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She tries to make him name the famous town where he performs his cosmic dance. Siva won't answer directly and turns her own praise into a puzzle about his many titles. The divine cannot be easily pinned down or defined by human language.

tamil: உடற்கச் சுயிரா மொற்றியுளீ ருமது திருப்பேர் யாதென்றேன்
குடக்குச் சிவந்த பொழுதினைமுன் கொண்ட வண்ண ராமென்றார்
விடைக்குக் கருத்தா வாநீர்தாம் விளம்பன் மிகக்கற் றவரென்றே
னிடக்குப் புகன்றா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: uṭaṟkac cuyirā moṟṟiyuḷī rumatu tiruppēr yāteṉṟēṉ kuṭakkuc civanta poḻutiṉaimuṉ koṇṭa vaṇṇa rāmeṉṟār viṭaikkuk karuttā vānīrtām viḷampaṉ mikakkaṟ ṟavareṉṟē ṉiṭakkup pukaṉṟā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of Otriyur who is the life of the body, what is your holy name?" I asked. He replied, "I possess the color of the time when the western sky turns red." I said, "O Lord of the bull, you are indeed highly learned in the art of speaking." He said, "You speak with mockery." What is this, my friend?
commentary: This time she asks his holy name outright. He describes the red sky of the setting sun, hinting at the name Siva, which means the red one. Theirs is a constant battle of wits, where even a compliment is quickly treated as mockery.

tamil: பிணங்கேஞ் சிறிது நில்லுமென்றேன் பிணங்கா விடினு நென்னலென
வணங்கே நினக்கொன் றினிற்பாதி யதிலோர் பாதி யாகுமிதற்
கிணங்கேஞ் சிறிது மென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: maṇaṅkē takaivāṉ ceyumoṟṟi vaḷḷalivarai valviraivēṉ piṇaṅkēñ ciṟitu nillumeṉṟēṉ piṇaṅkā viṭiṉu neṉṉaleṉa vaṇaṅkē niṉakkoṉ ṟiṉiṟpāti yatilōr pāti yākumitaṟ kiṇaṅkēñ ciṟitu meṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I hurried swiftly to the generous Lord of Otriyur who makes the sky fragrant with screwpine flowers. I said, "We will not quarrel, please stay for a little while." He said, "Even if we do not quarrel, O beautiful woman, yesterday you were half of one thing, and half of that. I will not consent to this even a bit." What is this, my friend?
commentary: At last she asks him to stay, promising they will not argue. He refuses and slips away behind another complex riddle, this one about fractions and how she behaved the day before. The soul's longing for God is lived here as a romantic, playful game of hide and seek.

tamil: ஒற்றி நகரா ரிவர்தமைநீ ருவந்தே றுவதிங்கி யாதென்றேன்
மற்றுன் பருவத் தொருபங்கே மடவா யென்றார் மறைவிடையீ
திற்றென் றறிதற் கரிதென்றே னெம்மை யறிவா ரன்றியஃ
தெற்றென் றறிவா ரென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: oṟṟi nakarā rivartamainī ruvantē ṟuvatiṅki yāteṉṟēṉ maṟṟuṉ paruvat torupaṅkē maṭavā yeṉṟār maṟaiviṭaiyī tiṟṟeṉ ṟaṟitaṟ kariteṉṟē ṉemmai yaṟivā raṉṟiyaḵ teṟṟeṉ ṟaṟivā reṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked this Lord of Otriyur, "What is it you gladly ride here?" He said, "O innocent girl, it is a fraction of your age." I replied, "It is hard to understand this hidden answer." He says, "Who but those who know us can understand what it is?" What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks what mount he rides, and he answers with a playful riddle about her age. The divine often speaks in mysteries that baffle the ordinary mind. To understand the ways of God, a person must first truly know God through direct inner experience.

tamil: கண்ணின் மணிபோ லிங்குநிற்குங் கள்வ ரிவரூ ரொற்றியதாம்
பண்ணின் மொழியாய் நின்பாலோர் பறவைப் பெயர்வேண் டினம்படைத்தான்
னெண்ணி யறிநீ யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: kaṇṇiṉ maṇipō liṅkuniṟkuṅ kaḷva rivarū roṟṟiyatām paṇṇiṉ moḻiyāy niṉpālōr paṟavaip peyarvēṇ ṭiṉampaṭaittāṉ maṇṇiṉ micaiyōr paṟavaiyatā vāḻvāyeṉṟā reṉṉeṉṟē ṉeṇṇi yaṟinī yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: The town of this thief, who stands here like the pupil of my eye, is Otriyur. He said, "O girl with words like music, we need the name of a bird from you. The Creator made you live as a bird on this earth." I asked him what he meant. He says, "Think and figure it out yourself." What is this, my friend?
commentary: He calls her a bird, praising her musical voice, and hands her another riddle. God plays the intimate, playful companion here, nothing like a distant judge. He wants the soul to use its own thought and discernment to uncover hidden spiritual truths.

tamil: சேடார் வளஞ்சூ ழொற்றிநகர் செல்வப் பெருமா னிவர்தமைநா
னோடார் கரத்தீ ரெண்டோள்க ளுடையீ ரென்னென் றுரைத்தேனீ
கோடா கோடி முகநூறு கோடா கோடிக் களமென்னே
யீடா யுடையா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: cēṭār vaḷañcū ḻoṟṟinakar celvap perumā ṉivartamainā ṉōṭār karattī reṇṭōḷka ḷuṭaiyī reṉṉeṉ ṟuraittēṉī kōṭā kōṭi mukanūṟu kōṭā kōṭik kaḷameṉṉē yīṭā yuṭaiyā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I spoke to this wealthy Lord of Otriyur, a town surrounded by great abundance. I said, "You hold a skull in your hand and have eight shoulders. What is this?" He says, "You possess millions of faces and hundreds of millions of necks in equal measure. What is that?" What is this, my friend?
commentary: She questions his fearsome appearance, the eight shoulders and the skull he carries. He turns it around and teases her by exaggerating her own countless worldly traits and adornments. Reverence and affectionate banter blend easily in this intimacy between the soul and God.

tamil: துருமஞ் செழிக்கும் பொழிலொற்றித் தோன்றா லிங்கு நீர்வந்த
கருமஞ் சொலுமென் றேனிவண்யாங் கடாதற் குன்பா லெம்முடைமைத்
தருமம் பெறக்கண் டாமென்றார் தருவ லிருந்தா லென்றேனில்
லிருமந் தரமோ வென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: turumañ ceḻikkum poḻiloṟṟit tōṉṟā liṅku nīrvanta karumañ columeṉ ṟēṉivaṇyāṅ kaṭātaṟ kuṉpā lemmuṭaimait tarumam peṟakkaṇ ṭāmeṉṟār taruva liruntā leṉṟēṉil liruman taramō veṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked this Lord of Otriyur, a town of lush tree-filled groves, "Tell me your purpose in coming here." He said, "We came here to receive from you the charity that rightfully belongs to us." I told him I would give it if I had it. He says, "Do you have two Mandara mountains in your house?" What is this, my friend?
commentary: He arrives asking for alms, in his traditional role as the divine beggar. When she offers what she has, he praises her beauty with the poetic image of two Mandara mountains. In this tradition of devotional poetry, human romance and divine longing speak the same language. The charity God seeks is the soul's total surrender of love.

tamil: ஒருகை முகத்தோர்க் கையரெனு மொற்றித் தேவ ரிவர்தமைநான்
வருகை யுவந்தீ ரென்றனைநீர் மருவி யணைதல் வேண்டுமென்றேன்
றருகை யுடனே யகங்காரந் தனையெம் மடியார் தமைமயக்கை
யிருகை வளைசிந் தென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: orukai mukattōrk kaiyareṉu moṟṟit tēva rivartamaināṉ varukai yuvantī reṉṟaṉainīr maruvi yaṇaital vēṇṭumeṉṟēṉ ṟarukai yuṭaṉē yakaṅkāran taṉaiyem maṭiyār tamaimayakkai yirukai vaḷaicin teṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I spoke to this God of Otriyur, the father of the elephant-faced Lord. I said, "I rejoice at your arrival. You must embrace me." He says, "Surrender your ego immediately, let go of the delusion that clouds our devotees, and cast off the bangles from your two hands." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She openly asks for his embrace, and he sets firm spiritual conditions. She must surrender her ego completely and abandon every worldly delusion. Casting off her bangles means throwing away earthly attachments. The soul has to be entirely empty of self before it can merge with the divine.

tamil: திருத்த மிகுஞ்சீ ரொற்றியில்வாழ் தேவ ரேயிங் கெதுவேண்டி
வருத்த மலர்க்கா லுறநடந்து வந்தீ ரென்றேன் மாதேநீ
ணிருத்த வடைந்தே மென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: tirutta mikuñcī roṟṟiyilvāḻ tēva rēyiṅ ketuvēṇṭi varutta malarkkā luṟanaṭantu vantī reṉṟēṉ mātēnī yaruttan teḷintē niruvāṇa mākavuṉṟa ṉakattaruṭka ṇirutta vaṭaintē meṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked: "O God who dwells in greatly renowned Otriyur, what did you want here that you came walking, causing pain to your flower-like feet?" He replies: "O lady, we came to perform the dance of grace in your heart so that you may clearly understand the truth and attain liberation." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks why he took the trouble of walking all this way on flower-soft feet. His answer goes straight past her worry. He has come to perform the dance of grace inside her own heart, and that inner dance brings clear understanding of the truth and final liberation.

tamil: வளஞ்சே ரொற்றி மாணிக்க வண்ண ராகு மிவர்தமைநான்
குளஞ்சேர்ந் திருந்த துமக்கொருகண் கோலச் சடையீ ரழகிதென்றேன்
களஞ்சேர் குளத்தி னெழின்முலைக்கண் காண வோரைந் துனக்கழகீ
திளஞ்சேல் விழியா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vaḷañcē roṟṟi māṇikka vaṇṇa rāku mivartamaināṉ kuḷañcērn tirunta tumakkorukaṇ kōlac caṭaiyī raḻakiteṉṟēṉ kaḷañcēr kuḷatti ṉeḻiṉmulaikkaṇ kāṇa vōrain tuṉakkaḻakī tiḷañcēl viḻiyā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I told the ruby-hued Lord of fertile Otriyur: "O Lord with beautiful matted hair, it is a beauty that one of your eyes is resting in a pond." He replies: "O girl with eyes like young fish, it is beautiful that you have five eyes on your lovely breast of the pond joined with a neck." What is this, my friend?
commentary: The two trade playful riddles about each other's features. She teases him by likening his divine eye to a blossom resting in a pond. He answers with a knottier puzzle about her own form and turns the tease right back on her.

tamil: பலஞ்சே ரொற்றிப் பதியுடையீர் பதிவே றுண்டோ நுமக்கென்றே
வலஞ்சே ரிடைத்தவ் வருவித்த மலைகா ணதனின் மம்முதல்சென்
றிலஞ்சேர்ந் ததுவு மென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: palañcē roṟṟip patiyuṭaiyīr pativē ṟuṇṭō numakkeṉṟē ṉulañcēr veṇpoṉ malaiyeṉṟā ruṇṭō nīṇṭamalaiyeṉṟēṉ valañcē riṭaittav varuvitta malaikā ṇataṉiṉ mammutalceṉ ṟilañcērn tatuvu meṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked: "O Lord of fruitful Otriyur, do you have another home?" He said: "The solid white mountain." I asked: "Is there a long mountain?" He replies: "Look at the mountain that creates a waterfall right in its midst, and see how its first letter 'ma' leaves and 'ila' joins it." What is this, my friend?
commentary: Asked whether he has another home, he names the sacred white mountain of Kailash. Then he plays with the Tamil word for mountain. Swap its first syllable as he instructs, and the word becomes praise of her own slender beauty.

tamil: வயலா ரொற்றி வாணரிவர் வந்தார் நின்றார் வாய்திறவார்
செயலார் விரல்கண் முடக்கியடி சேர்த்தீ ரிதழ்கள் விரிவித்தார்
மயலா ருளத்தோ டென்னென்றேன் மறித்தோர் விரலா லென்னுடைய
வியலார் வடிவிற் சுட்டுகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vayalā roṟṟi vāṇarivar vantār niṉṟār vāytiṟavār ceyalār viralkaṇ muṭakkiyaṭi cērttī ritaḻkaḷ virivittār mayalā ruḷattō ṭeṉṉeṉṟēṉ maṟittōr viralā leṉṉuṭaiya viyalār vaṭiviṟ cuṭṭukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: He came, the Lord of Otriyur surrounded by fields. He stood and would not open his mouth. He folded his active fingers, joined his feet, and widened his lips into a smile. With a heart full of infatuation, I asked: "What is this?" Bending one finger, he points at my naturally beautiful body. What is this, my friend?
commentary: The Lord appears as a silent yogi, speaking only through gestures and a quiet smile. When she asks what his posture means, he points one finger at her. She is the reason he stands there captivated.

tamil: பேர்வா ழொற்றி வாணரிவர் பேசா மௌன யோகியராய்ச்
சீர்வாழ் நமது மனையினிடைச் சேர்ந்தார் விழைவென் செப்புமென்றே
னோர்வா ழடியுங் குழலணியு மொருநல் விரலாற் சுட்டியுந்தம்
மேர்வா ழொருகை பார்க்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: pērvā ḻoṟṟi vāṇarivar pēcā mauṉa yōkiyarāyc cīrvāḻ namatu maṉaiyiṉiṭaic cērntār viḻaiveṉ ceppumeṉṟē ṉōrvā ḻaṭiyuṅ kuḻalaṇiyu morunal viralāṟ cuṭṭiyuntam mērvā ḻorukai pārkkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: The Lord of renowned Otriyur came into our excellent house as a silent yogi who does not speak. I asked: "Tell me, what is your desire?" He points with one fine finger at the foot and the hair ornament, and then he looks at his own handsome hand. What is this, my friend?
commentary: Still no words. He points to her foot and to her hair ornament, then looks at his own hand, taking in her whole form from head to toe. That is a traditional poetic way of asking for her hand and claiming her completely as his own.

tamil: பெருஞ்சீ ரொற்றி வாணரிவர் பேசா மௌனம் பிடித்திங்கே
விரிஞ்சீர் தரநின் றுடன்கீழு மேலு நோக்கி விரைந்தார்யான்
வருஞ்சீ ருடையீர் மணிவார்த்தை வகுக்க வென்றேன் மார்பிடைக்கா
ழிருஞ்சீர் மணியைக் காட்டுகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: peruñcī roṟṟi vāṇarivar pēcā mauṉam piṭittiṅkē viriñcīr taraniṉ ṟuṭaṉkīḻu mēlu nōkki viraintāryāṉ varuñcī ruṭaiyīr maṇivārttai vakukka veṉṟēṉ mārpiṭaikkā ḻiruñcīr maṇiyaik kāṭṭukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: He is the Lord of Otriyur of great glory. Maintaining strict silence, He stood radiating greatness, immediately looked down and up, and then hurried away. I said to Him, "O Lord of coming glory, please speak a precious word." He simply pointed to the magnificent gemstone on His chest. What is this, my friend?
commentary: The soul speaks as a young woman trying to read a lover who will not talk. She begs for a precious word, and he teases her by pointing to the gemstone on his chest. The whole exchange is a game of signs, full of playful intimacy between the soul and God.

tamil: வலந்தங் கியசீ ரொற்றிநகர் வள்ள லிவர்தாம் மௌனமொடு
கலந்திங் கிருந்த வண்டசத்தைக் காட்டி மூன்று விரனீட்டி
நலந்தங் குறப்பின் னடுமுடக்கி நண்ணு மிந்த நகத்தொடுவா
யிலந்தங் கரத்தாற் குறிக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: valantaṅ kiyacī roṟṟinakar vaḷḷa livartām mauṉamoṭu kalantiṅ kirunta vaṇṭacattaik kāṭṭi mūṉṟu viraṉīṭṭi nalantaṅ kuṟappiṉ ṉaṭumuṭakki naṇṇu minta nakattoṭuvā yilantaṅ karattāṟ kuṟikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This Lord of the glorious city of Otriyur where greatness abides stood in utter silence. He pointed to an egg here, extended three fingers, bent His middle finger, and then pointed to His nail and mouth with His beautiful hand. What is this, my friend?
commentary: An egg, three fingers, a bent middle finger, the nail, the mouth. The sequence leaves her completely confused. The divine often communicates in ways the human mind cannot easily decipher.

tamil: தேனார் பொழிலா ரொற்றியில்வாழ் தேவ ரிவர்வாய் திறவாராய்
மானார் கரத்தோர் நகந்தெரித்து வாளா நின்றார் நீளார்வந்
தானா ருளத்தோ டியாதென்றேன் றங்கைத் தலத்திற் றலையையடி
யேனா டுறவே காட்டுகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: tēṉār poḻilā roṟṟiyilvāḻ tēva rivarvāy tiṟavārāy māṉār karattōr nakanterittu vāḷā niṉṟār nīḷārvan tāṉā ruḷattō ṭiyāteṉṟēṉ ṟaṅkait talattiṟ ṟalaiyaiyaṭi yēṉā ṭuṟavē kāṭṭukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This Lord living in Otriyur of honey-filled groves refuses to open His mouth. Flicking a fingernail on His hand that holds the deer, He stood in silence. With a heart full of deep longing, I asked Him what this meant. He showed His head resting on His hand, gesturing for me to seek Him. What is this, my friend?
commentary: Her questions grow desperate, and he still answers only with his body. Resting his head heavily on his hand, he signals his own longing. It is a striking picture of God as a lover waiting patiently for the soul to seek him out.

tamil: செச்சை யழகர் திருவொற்றித் தேவ ரிவர்வாய் திறவாராய்
மெச்சு மொருகாற் கரந்தொட்டு மீண்டு மிடற்றக் கரம்வைத்தார்
பிச்ச ரடிகேள் வேண்டுவது பேசீ ரென்றேன் றமைக்காட்டி
யிச்சை யெனையுங் குறிக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: ceccai yaḻakar tiruvoṟṟit tēva rivarvāy tiṟavārāy meccu morukāṟ karantoṭṭu mīṇṭu miṭaṟṟak karamvaittār picca raṭikēḷ vēṇṭuvatu pēcī reṉṟēṉ ṟamaikkāṭṭi yiccai yeṉaiyuṅ kuṟikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This beautiful Lord of Otriyur adorned with ixora flowers refuses to open His mouth. First He touched His foot with His hand, and then He placed that hand on His throat. I said, "O mad Lord, please tell me what You desire." Pointing to Himself, He signaled His desire for me. What is this, my friend?
commentary: The pantomime turns into a direct declaration of love. After the cryptic movements from foot to throat, he points straight at himself and then at her. The mystery dissolves into a simple truth: God desires the soul just as deeply as the soul desires God.

tamil: மன்றார் நிலையார் திருவொற்றி வாண ரிவர்தா மௌனமொடு
நின்றா ரிருகை யொலியிசைத்தார் நிமிர்ந்தார் தவிசி னிலைகுறைத்தார்
நன்றா ரமுது சிறிதுமிழ்ந்தார் நடித்தா ரியாவு மையமென்றே
னின்றா மரைக்கை யேந்துகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: maṉṟār nilaiyār tiruvoṟṟi vāṇa rivartā mauṉamoṭu niṉṟā rirukai yoliyicaittār nimirntār tavici ṉilaikuṟaittār naṉṟā ramutu ciṟitumiḻntār naṭittā riyāvu maiyameṉṟē ṉiṉṟā maraikkai yēntukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This Lord of Otriyur who abides in the dancing hall stood in silence. He clapped His hands, stood tall, stepped down from His seat, spat out a little sweet nectar, and danced. When I told Him that all of this was a mystery to me, He extended His beautiful lotus hand as if asking for alms. What is this, my friend?
commentary: He claps and dances, then holds out his open lotus hand to the baffled woman like a wandering beggar. In that beggar's form, God asks the soul to surrender everything it has to him.

tamil: வாரா விருந்தாய் வள்ளலிவர் வந்தார் மௌன மொடுநின்றார்
நீரா ரெங்கே யிருப்பதென்றே னீண்ட சடையைக் குறிப்பித்தா
ரூரா வைத்த தெதுவென்றே னொண்கை யோடென் னிடத்தினில்வைத்
தேரார் கரத்தாற் சுட்டுகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vārā viruntāy vaḷḷalivar vantār mauṉa moṭuniṉṟār nīrā reṅkē yiruppateṉṟē ṉīṇṭa caṭaiyaik kuṟippittā rūrā vaitta tetuveṉṟē ṉoṇkai yōṭeṉ ṉiṭattiṉilvait tērār karattāṟ cuṭṭukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This generous Lord came as a rare guest. He stood in silence. I asked, "Who are you and where do you dwell?" He pointed to his long matted hair. I asked, "What is your town?" He placed his bright hand on my left side and points with his handsome hand. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks the silent Lord to name his hometown, and he points to her left side, where her heart lies. His true home is the inner space of the devotee.

tamil: செங்கேழ் கங்கைச் சடையார்வாய் திறவா ராக வீண்டடைந்தா
ரெங்கே யிருந்தெங் கணைந்ததுகா ணெங்கள் பெருமா னென்றேனென்
னங்கே ழருகி னகன்றுபோ யங்கே யிறைப்போ தமர்ந்தெழுந்தே
யிங்கே நடந்து வருகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: ceṅkēḻ kaṅkaic caṭaiyārvāy tiṟavā rāka vīṇṭaṭaintā reṅkē yirunteṅ kaṇaintatukā ṇeṅkaḷ perumā ṉeṉṟēṉeṉ ṉaṅkē ḻaruki ṉakaṉṟupō yaṅkē yiṟaippō tamarnteḻuntē yiṅkē naṭantu varukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: The Lord with reddish matted hair bearing the Ganges arrived here without opening his mouth. I asked, "Our Lord, from where did you come and where are you going?" He moved away from my beautiful side, sat there for a moment, stood up, and comes walking back here. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks where he has come from and where he is going. He answers by walking a few steps away, sitting for a moment, and coming straight back to her. The divine never truly departs from the soul.

tamil: கொடையா ரொற்றி வாணரிவர் கூறா மௌன ராகிநின்றார்
தொடையா ரிதழி மதிச்சடையென் துரையே விழைவே துமக்கென்றே
னுடையார் துன்னற் கந்தைதனை யுற்று நோக்கி நகைசெய்தே
யிடையாக் கழுமுட் காட்டுகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: koṭaiyā roṟṟi vāṇarivar kūṟā mauṉa rākiniṉṟār toṭaiyā ritaḻi maticcaṭaiyeṉ turaiyē viḻaivē tumakkeṉṟē ṉuṭaiyār tuṉṉaṟ kantaitaṉai yuṟṟu nōkki nakaiceytē yiṭaiyāk kaḻumuṭ kāṭṭukiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This generous Lord of Otri stood in unspoken silence. I asked, "My Master with the crescent moon and cassia garland in your matted hair, what is your desire?" He stared closely at the stitched rag he wears, smiled, and points to the sharp thorn at his waist. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks what he desires. He looks at his patched rag, smiles, and points to the sharp thorn at his waist. No romantic answer comes; he is playfully reminding her that he is the ultimate ascetic who needs nothing at all.

tamil: பொன்னைக் கொடுத்தும் புணர்வரிய புனித ரிவரூ ரொற்றியதா
முன்னைத் தவத்தா லியாங்காண முன்னே நின்றார் முகமலர்ந்து
மின்னிற் பொலியுஞ் சடையீரென் வேண்டு மென்றே னுணச்செய்யா
ளின்னச் சினங்கா ணென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: poṉṉaik koṭuttum puṇarvariya puṉita rivarū roṟṟiyatā muṉṉait tavattā liyāṅkāṇa muṉṉē niṉṟār mukamalarntu miṉṉiṟ poliyuñ caṭaiyīreṉ vēṇṭu meṉṟē ṉuṇacceyyā ḷiṉṉac ciṉaṅkā ṇeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This pure Lord, whom it is hard to embrace even if one gives gold, belongs to Otri. Because of my past penance, he stood before me with a blossoming face so I could see him. I asked, "You with matted hair shining like lightning, what do you want?" He says, "See the sweet anger of the lady who does not feed me." What is this, my friend?
commentary: Now he plays the wandering beggar, grumbling about a lady who angrily refuses to feed him. Under the complaint is a request for her total devotion. He frames his longing for her love as a beggar's simple wish for a meal.

tamil: வயலார் சோலை யெழிலொற்றி வாண ராகு மிவர்தமைநான்
செயலா ரடியர்க் கருள்வீர்நுஞ் சிரத்து முரத்துந் திகழ்கரத்தும்
வியலாய்க் கொண்ட தென்னென்றேன் விளங்கும் பிநாக மவைமூன்று
மியலாற் காண்டி யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vayalār cōlai yeḻiloṟṟi vāṇa rāku mivartamaināṉ ceyalā raṭiyark karuḷvīrnuñ cirattu murattun tikaḻkarattum viyalāyk koṇṭa teṉṉeṉṟēṉ viḷaṅkum pināka mavaimūṉṟu miyalāṟ kāṇṭi yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: This Lord dwells in beautiful Otri surrounded by fields and groves. I told him, "You bestow grace on your true devotees. What are these vast things you bear on your head, your chest, and your shining hands?" He replies, "Look at them in their true nature: they are three shining snakes." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks about the grand ornaments on his head, chest and hands. He tells her plainly that they are snakes, three of them. With that he strips away the illusion of worldly wealth and shows his fierce, untamed nature.

tamil: பொதுநின் றருள்வீ ரொற்றியுளீர் பூவுந் தியதென் விழியென்றே
னிதுவென் றறிநா மேறுகின்ற தென்றா ரேறு கின்றதுதா
னெதுவென் றுரைத்தே னெதுநடுவோ ரெழுத்திட் டறிநீ யென்றுசொலி
யெதிர்நின் றுவந்து நகைக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: potuniṉ ṟaruḷvī roṟṟiyuḷīr pūvun tiyateṉ viḻiyeṉṟē ṉituveṉ ṟaṟinā mēṟukiṉṟa teṉṟā rēṟu kiṉṟatutā ṉetuveṉ ṟuraittē ṉetunaṭuvō reḻuttiṭ ṭaṟinī yeṉṟucoli yetirniṉ ṟuvantu nakaikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of Otriyur who stands in public and grants grace! There is a flower in my eye," I said. "Know this: it is what we mount," he said. "What is it that mounts?" I asked. "Put a letter in the middle of the word 'which' and know," he said. Standing before me, he laughs joyfully. What is this, my friend?
commentary: The Lord answers in riddles to reveal who he is. When she mentions a flower in her eye, he hints at his mount, the bull. By telling her to add a single letter to the Tamil word for 'which', he playfully spells out the word for 'bull'. Banter this light shows how intimate and playful the bond between the soul and God can be.

tamil: இட்டங் களித்த தொற்றியுளீ ரீண்டிவ் வேளை யெவனென்றேன்
சுட்டுஞ் சுதனே யென்றார்நான் சுட்டி யறியச் சொலுமென்றேன்
பட்டுண் மருங்குற் பாவாய்நீ பரித்த தன்றே பாரென்றே
யெட்டுங் களிப்பா லுரைக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: iṭṭaṅ kaḷitta toṟṟiyuḷī rīṇṭiv vēḷai yevaṉeṉṟēṉ cuṭṭuñ cutaṉē yeṉṟārnāṉ cuṭṭi yaṟiyac columeṉṟēṉ paṭṭuṇ maruṅkuṟ pāvāynī paritta taṉṟē pāreṉṟē yeṭṭuṅ kaḷippā luraikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of Otriyur who granted joy! Who is here at this time?" I asked. "It is the pointed out son," he said. "Tell me so I may point him out and know," I said. "O lady with a waist wrapped in silk, look at what you wear," he said. Filled with supreme joy, he speaks. What is this, my friend?
commentary: More riddles, this time about identity and clothing. She wants to pin down exactly who he is and asks him to point out his true form. He gives no direct answer, only joyful, elusive hints about the silk she wears, and the mystery of his presence stays where it was.

tamil: பாற்றக் கணத்தா ரிவர்காட்டு ப் பள்ளித் தலைவ ரொற்றியினின்
றாற்றப் பசித்து வந்தாரா மன்ன மிடுமி னென்றுரைத்தேன்
சோற்றுக் கிளைத்தோ மாயினும்யாஞ் சொல்லுக் கிளையேங் கீழ்ப்பள்ளி
யேற்றுக் கிடந்தா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: pāṟṟak kaṇattā rivarkāṭṭu p paḷḷit talaiva roṟṟiyiṉiṉ ṟāṟṟap pacittu vantārā maṉṉa miṭumi ṉeṉṟuraittēṉ cōṟṟuk kiḷaittō māyiṉumyāñ colluk kiḷaiyēṅ kīḻppaḷḷi yēṟṟuk kiṭantā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "The Lord of the forest who holds a host of eagles stands in Otriyur! He has come with unbearable hunger, serve him rice," I said. "Though we grow weary for rice, we do not grow weary for words. You lie accepting the lower bed," he says. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She sees him as a wandering beggar in terrible hunger and, out of compassion, tells someone to feed him rice. He turns her concern into a joke. People grow tired looking for food, he says, but he never grows tired of words. Then he teases her about her worldly position. Human worries about bodily comfort do not touch him.

tamil: குருகா ரொற்றி வாணர்பலி கொள்ள வகையுண் டோவென்றே
வருகா விரிப்பொன் னம்பலத்தே வந்தாற் காட்டு கின்றாம்வீ
ழிருகா லுடையா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: kurukā roṟṟi vāṇarpali koḷḷa vakaiyuṇ ṭōveṉṟē ṉorukā leṭuttīṇ ṭuraiyeṉṟā rorukā leṭuttukkāṭṭumeṉṟēṉ varukā virippoṉ ṉampalattē vantāṟ kāṭṭu kiṉṟāmvī ḻirukā luṭaiyā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of Otriyur surrounded by birds! Is there a way to receive alms?" I asked. "Bring it up once and speak here," he said. "Lift one foot and show me," I said. "If you come to the Golden Hall where the Kaveri river flows, we will show you, O lady who possesses two falling feet," he says. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks him to lift one foot, the foot of his famous cosmic dance, and show his true form. He refuses to do it on the spot. Come to the Golden Hall at Chidambaram, he tells her, and see the dancing foot there. Then he teases her for her two ordinary, earthbound feet. Mortal limits and divine freedom stand side by side.

tamil: வேலை ஞாலம் புகழொற்றி விளங்குந் தேவ ரணிகின்ற
மாலை யாதென் றேனயன்மான் மாலை யகற்று மாலையென்றார்
சோலை மலரன் றேயென்றேன் சோலை யேநாந் தொடுப்பதென
வேல முறுவல் புரிகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vēlai ñālam pukaḻoṟṟi viḷaṅkun tēva raṇikiṉṟa mālai yāteṉ ṟēṉayaṉmāṉ mālai yakaṟṟu mālaiyeṉṟār cōlai malaraṉ ṟēyeṉṟēṉ cōlai yēnān toṭuppateṉa vēla muṟuval purikiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O shining Lord of Otriyur praised by the sea-encircled earth! What is the garland you wear?" I asked. "It is the nature that dispels the delusion of Brahma and Vishnu," he said. "Is it not made of flowers from the grove?" I asked. "Why would we string a grove together?" he says with a fragrant smile. What is this, my friend?
commentary: Everything turns on a double meaning, since the Tamil word for a flower garland also means delusion. Asked about his garland, the Lord says he wears the supreme power that clears away the illusions of even the greatest gods. She tries to bring him back to flowers from the grove. He takes her literally and laughs, lifting her ordinary words into spiritual truth.

tamil: உயிரு ளுறைவீர் திருவொற்றி யுடையீர் நீரென் மேற்பிடித்த
வயிர மதனை விடுமென்றேன் வயிரி யலநீ மாதேயாஞ்
செயிர தகற்றுன் முலையிடங்கொள் செல்வ னலகாண் டெளியென்றே
யியல்கொண் முறுவல் புரிகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: uyiru ḷuṟaivīr tiruvoṟṟi yuṭaiyīr nīreṉ mēṟpiṭitta vayira mataṉai viṭumeṉṟēṉ vayiri yalanī mātēyāñ ceyira takaṟṟuṉ mulaiyiṭaṅkoḷ celva ṉalakāṇ ṭeḷiyeṉṟē yiyalkoṇ muṟuval purikiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I said, "O You who dwell within lives, O Lord of Otriyur, let go of this enmity You hold against me." He replied, "You are no enemy, O lady. Understand clearly that We are the wealthy one who removes your sorrow and claims the space on your breasts." Saying this, He smiles naturally. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She begs the Lord to drop the hostility she thinks he holds against her. He answers as an intimate lover would, promising to wipe away her sorrow and claim her embrace. Her longing is met with a closeness she never expected.

tamil: தண்கா வளஞ்சூழ் திருவொற்றித் தலத்தி லமர்ந்த சாமிநுங்கை
யெண்கார் முகமாப் பொன் னென்றே னிடையிட் டறித லரிதென்றார்
மண்கா தலிக்கு மாடென்றேன் மதிக்குங் கணைவி லன்றென்றே
யெண்கா ணகைசெய் தருள்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: taṇkā vaḷañcūḻ tiruvoṟṟit talatti lamarnta cāminuṅkai yeṇkār mukamāp poṉ ṉeṉṟē ṉiṭaiyiṭ ṭaṟita lariteṉṟār maṇkā talikku māṭeṉṟēṉ matikkuṅ kaṇaivi laṉṟeṉṟē yeṇkā ṇakaicey taruḷkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked, "O Lord seated in the shrine of Otriyur surrounded by cool, fertile groves, is the great gold in Your hand eight measures?" He replied, "It is hard to know by weighing it." I said, "It is the wealth the earth desires." He replied, "It is not the esteemed bow and arrow." He smiles, gracing me with a thoughtful look. What is this, my friend?
commentary: Wealth and weapons get traded back and forth in double meanings. She asks about the golden wealth in his hand, and he teases her by treating her words as questions about his legendary golden bow. A relationship with room for jokes like this is affectionate and alive.

tamil: செய்காண் வளஞ்சூ ழொற்றியுளீர் திருமான் முதன்முத் தேவர்கட்கு
மைகாணீரென் றேனிதன்மே லணங்கே நீயே ழடைதி யென்றார்
மெய்கா ணதுதா னென்னென்றேன் விளங்குஞ் சுட்டுப் பெயரென்றே
யெய்கா ணுறவே நகைக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: ceykāṇ vaḷañcū ḻoṟṟiyuḷīr tirumāṉ mutaṉmut tēvarkaṭku maikāṇīreṉ ṟēṉitaṉmē laṇaṅkē nīyē ḻaṭaiti yeṉṟār meykā ṇatutā ṉeṉṉeṉṟēṉ viḷaṅkuñ cuṭṭup peyareṉṟē yeykā ṇuṟavē nakaikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I said, "O Lord of Otriyur surrounded by fertile fields, You are imperceptible even to the three primary gods beginning with Vishnu." He replied, "Upon this, O lovely lady, you reach the seven." I asked, "What is the truth of that?" He replied, "It is a shining demonstrative pronoun." He laughs piercingly. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She praises him as a mystery beyond the reach of the greatest gods. Her reverence gets a smiling grammatical riddle about numbers and pronouns in return. Deflections like these draw her closer, until the search for his true nature takes hold of her completely.

tamil: விண்டு வணங்கு மொற்றியுளீர் மென்பூ விருந்தும் வன்பூவில்
வண்டு விழுந்த தென்றேனெம் மலர்க்கை வண்டும் விழுந்ததென்றார்
தொண்டர்க் கருள்வீர் மிகவென்றேன் றோகாய் நாமே தொண்டனென
வெண்டங் குறவே நகைக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: viṇṭu vaṇaṅku moṟṟiyuḷīr meṉpū viruntum vaṉpūvil vaṇṭu viḻunta teṉṟēṉem malarkkai vaṇṭum viḻuntateṉṟār toṇṭark karuḷvīr mikaveṉṟēṉ ṟōkāy nāmē toṇṭaṉeṉa veṇṭaṅ kuṟavē nakaikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I said, "O Lord of Otriyur whom Vishnu worships, even while soft flowers are here, the bee has fallen on a hard flower." He replied, "Our flower-like hand, which is also a bee, has fallen." I said, "You bestow great grace upon Your devotees." He replied, "O lady with the grace of a peacock, We ourselves are the devotee." He smiles, revealing His white teeth. What is this, my friend?
commentary: Her image of a bee landing on a hard flower hints that the Lord has placed his attention unwisely. He turns her words around and claims that he is the devoted servant, the one worshipping her. With that reversal the distance between the almighty Creator and the human soul melts.

tamil: மட்டார் மலர்க்கா வொற்றியுளீர் மதிக்குங் கலைமேல் விழுமென்றே
னெட்டா மெழுத்தை யெடுத்ததுநா மிசைத்தே மென்றா ரெட்டாக
வுட்டா வுறுமவ் வெழுத்தறிய வுரைப்பீ ரென்றே னந்தணரூர்க்
கிட்டார் நாம மென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: maṭṭār malarkkā voṟṟiyuḷīr matikkuṅ kalaimēl viḻumeṉṟē ṉeṭṭā meḻuttai yeṭuttatunā micaittē meṉṟā reṭṭāka vuṭṭā vuṟumav veḻuttaṟiya vuraippī reṉṟē ṉantaṇarūrk kiṭṭār nāma meṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I said, "O Lord of Otriyur with fragrant flower groves, it will fall upon the esteemed garment." He replied, "We took the eighth letter and sounded it." I asked, "Speak so I may know that letter which stands inwardly as the number eight." He replies, "It is the name given to the town of the Brahmins." What is this, my friend?
commentary: Now the puzzle runs through the Tamil alphabet. In traditional Tamil script, the first letter 'A' is also the symbol for the number eight. Riddles about letters and village names keep her mind entirely fixed on him.

tamil: ஒற்றி நகரீர் மனவசிதா னுடையார்க் கருள்வீர் நீரென்றேன்
பற்றி யிறுதி தொடங்கியது பயிலு மவர்க்கே யருள்வதென்றார்
மற்றி துணர்கி லேனென்றேன் வருந்தே லுள்ள வன்மையெலா
மெற்றி லுணர்தி யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: oṟṟi nakarīr maṉavacitā ṉuṭaiyārk karuḷvīr nīreṉṟēṉ paṟṟi yiṟuti toṭaṅkiyatu payilu mavarkkē yaruḷvateṉṟār maṟṟi tuṇarki lēṉeṉṟēṉ varuntē luḷḷa vaṉmaiyelā meṟṟi luṇarti yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I said, "Lord of Otri city, you grant grace to those who master their minds." He replied, "I grant grace to those who practice what begins when grasping ends." I said, "I do not understand this." He says, "Do not worry. How else will you realize all your inner strength?" What is this, my friend?
commentary: Forcing the mind into submission does not bring grace. The Lord teaches that spiritual life begins only when the soul lets go of its clinging to worldly attachments. She admits she is confused, and he reassures her gently. Wrestling with spiritual truth, he explains, is exactly how the soul discovers its own inner strength.

tamil: வான்றோய் பொழில்சூ ழொற்றியுளீர் வருந்தா தணைவே னோவென்றே
னூன்றோ யுடற்கென் றார்தெரிய வுரைப்பீ ரென்றே னோவிதுதான்
சான்றோ ருமது மரபோர்ந்து தரித்த பெயர்க்குத் தகாதென்றே
யேன்றோர் மொழிதந் தருள்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vāṉṟōy poḻilcū ḻoṟṟiyuḷīr varuntā taṇaivē ṉōveṉṟē ṉūṉṟō yuṭaṟkeṉ ṟārteriya vuraippī reṉṟē ṉōvitutāṉ cāṉṟō rumatu marapōrntu taritta peyarkkut takāteṉṟē yēṉṟōr moḻitan taruḷkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked, "Lord in Otri surrounded by sky-reaching groves, will I embrace you without suffering?" He replied, "That is for the flesh-bound body." I said, "Speak so I can understand." Saying, "Oh, this ignorance does not suit the name the wise gave you after knowing your heritage," he graciously offers a fitting word. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She longs to merge with God without enduring the pain of separation. Comfort without suffering, he replies, belongs to the physical body and its worldly desires. When she asks for a plainer answer, he chides her playfully. Missing the deeper meaning does not suit someone of her noble heritage and wisdom.

tamil: தீது தவிர்க்கு மொற்றியுளீர் செல்ல லறுப்ப தென்றென்றே
னீது நமக்குத் தெரிந்ததென்றா ரிறையா மோவிங் கிதுவென்றே
னோது மடியார் மனக்கங்கு லோட்டு நாமே யுணரன்றி
யேது மிறையன் றென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: tītu tavirkku moṟṟiyuḷīr cella laṟuppa teṉṟeṉṟē ṉītu namakkut terintateṉṟā riṟaiyā mōviṅ kituveṉṟē ṉōtu maṭiyār maṉakkaṅku lōṭṭu nāmē yuṇaraṉṟi yētu miṟaiyaṉ ṟeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked, "Lord in Otri who dispels evil, when will you sever my distress?" He replied, "We already know this." I said, "Is this a proper reply?" He says, "Only we who drive away the darkness in the minds of praising devotees truly understand. Nothing else is proper." What is this, my friend?
commentary: The heart aches to know exactly when its suffering will end. His answer is short: he already knows her pain. She asks whether so brief a reply is fair. He reminds her of his nature, the one who drives the darkness of ignorance from the worshipper's mind, and only he holds the right timing and the understanding of how to save them.

tamil: ஒண்கை மழுவோ டனலுடையீ ரொற்றி நகர்வா ழுத்தமர்நீர்
வண்கை யொருமை நாதரென்றேன் வண்கைப் பன்மை நாதரென்றா
றெண்சொன் மணிதந் தருள்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: oṇkai maḻuvō ṭaṉaluṭaiyī roṟṟi nakarvā ḻuttamarnīr vaṇkai yorumai nātareṉṟēṉ vaṇkaip paṉmai nātareṉṟā reṇkaṇaṭaṅkā vaticayaṅkā ṇeṉṟēṉ poruḷaṉ ṟivaiyataṟkeṉ ṟeṇcoṉ maṇitan taruḷkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I said, "You hold a battle-axe and fire in your bright hands. You are the supreme being living in Otri city. You are the generous Lord of singularity." He replied, "I am the generous Lord of plurality." I said, "This is a wonder beyond measure." He says, "These words do not carry that meaning." He graciously gives a gem of an eight-lettered word. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She praises God as the absolute one, the single reality behind everything. He replies that he is also Lord of the many, fully present in the endless variety of creation. When she marvels at this, he tells her she is misreading his words. Then he blesses her with a sacred eight-letter mantra, steering her away from intellectual puzzles and toward direct spiritual practice.

tamil: ஒருவ ரெனவா ழொற்றியுளீ ருமக்கம் மனையுண் டோவென்றே
னிருவ ரொருபே ருடையவர்கா ணென்றா ரென்னென்றே னெம்பேர்
மருவு மீறற் றயலகரம் வயங்கு மிகர மானதென்றே
யிருவு மொழிதந் தருள்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: oruva reṉavā ḻoṟṟiyuḷī rumakkam maṉaiyuṇ ṭōveṉṟē ṉiruva rorupē ruṭaiyavarkā ṇeṉṟā reṉṉeṉṟē ṉempēr maruvu mīṟaṟ ṟayalakaram vayaṅku mikara māṉateṉṟē yiruvu moḻitan taruḷkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked, "Lord in Otri who lives as the peerless One, do you have a mother?" He replied, "Two share a single name." I asked, "What is it?" He says, "The letter 'a' near the end of our name has become a shining 'i'." Saying this, he graciously offers a word of mystery. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks the supreme Lord something tender and human, whether he has a mother. He answers with a riddle about shifting a single letter in a name. Behind the wordplay sits a truth about his nature. God holds both masculine and feminine principles, two halves of a single identity.

tamil: பேரா ரொற்றி யீரும்பைப் பெற்றா ரெவரென் றேனவர்தம்
மேரார் பெயரின் முன்பினிரண் டிரண்டா மெழுத்தா ரென்றாரென்
னேரா யுரைப்பீ ரென்றேனீ நெஞ்ச நெகிழ்ந்தா லுரைப்பாமென்
றேரா யுரைசெய் தருள்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: pērā roṟṟi yīrumpaip peṟṟā revareṉ ṟēṉavartam mērār peyariṉ muṉpiṉiraṇ ṭiraṇṭā meḻuttā reṉṟāreṉ ṉērā yuraippī reṉṟēṉī neñca nekiḻntā luraippāmeṉ ṟērā yuraicey taruḷkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "Lord of renowned Otriyur, who gave birth to you?" I asked. He replied, "They are the ones whose beautiful names consist of the two and two letters before and after." I said, "Tell me directly." He beautifully replies, "If your heart melts, we will tell you." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks the Lord who his parents are, and he answers with a riddle about letters. He will give the plain truth only when her heart melts with devotion. Love has to come first. Mere curiosity gets a riddle.

tamil: தளிநான் மறையீ ரொற்றிநகர் தழைக்க வாழ்வீர் தனிஞான
வொளி நா வரசை யைந்தெழுத்தா லுவரி கடத்தி னீரென்றேன்
களிநா வலனை யீரெழுத்தாற் கடலின் வீழ்த்தி னேமென்றே
யெளியேற் குவப்பின் மொழிகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: taḷināṉ maṟaiyī roṟṟinakar taḻaikka vāḻvīr taṉiñāṉa voḷi nā varacai yainteḻuttā luvari kaṭatti ṉīreṉṟēṉ kaḷinā valaṉai yīreḻuttāṟ kaṭaliṉ vīḻtti ṉēmeṉṟē yeḷiyēṟ kuvappiṉ moḻikiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "Lord of the four cool Vedas, you live so that the city of Otriyur flourishes. You helped the king of speech, filled with the light of peerless wisdom, cross the ocean using the five letters," I said. He replies to poor me with joy, "We cast the joyful poet into the sea using two letters." What is this, my friend?
commentary: She praises the Lord by recalling a famous story of a saint. Thrown into the ocean tied to a heavy stone, he floated to safety by chanting God's five-letter name. The Lord answers with a pun. He says he threw the poet into the sea "using two letters", meaning the Tamil word for the stone (kal) that became his float.

tamil: ஓமூன் றுளத்தீ ரொற்றியுளீ ருற்றோர்க் களிப்பீ ரோவென்றேன்
றாமூன் றென்பார்க் கயன்மூன்றுந் தருவே மென்றா ரம்மமிகத்
தேமூன் றினநும் மொழியென்றேன் செவ்வா யுறுமுன் னகையென்றே
யேமூன் றுறவே நகைக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: ōmūṉ ṟuḷattī roṟṟiyuḷī ruṟṟōrk kaḷippī rōveṉṟēṉ ṟāmūṉ ṟeṉpārk kayaṉmūṉṟun taruvē meṉṟā rammamikat tēmūṉ ṟiṉanum moḻiyeṉṟēṉ cevvā yuṟumuṉ ṉakaiyeṉṟē yēmūṉ ṟuṟavē nakaikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "Lord of Otriyur whose heart holds the Om, will you grant gifts to those who approach you?" I asked. He said, "To those who ask for three, we will give the three of the Creator." I said, "Ah, your words are exceedingly sweet like the three types of honey." Saying "It is the smile forming on your red lips," he smiles, making my bewilderment grow. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks whether he grants gifts to those who seek him, and he answers with a riddle built on the number three. When she calls his words as sweet as three kinds of honey, he turns the compliment back on her smile. His teasing leaves her bewildered and draws her deeper into devotion.

tamil: மன்னி விளங்கு மொற்றியுளீர் மடவா ரிரக்கும் வகையதுதான்
முன்னி லொருதா வாமென்றேன் முத்தா வெனலே முறையென்றா
ரென்னி லிதுதா னையமென்றே னெமக்குந் தெரியு மெனத்திருவா
யின்ன லமுத முகுக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: maṉṉi viḷaṅku moṟṟiyuḷīr maṭavā rirakkum vakaiyatutāṉ muṉṉi lorutā vāmeṉṟēṉ muttā veṉalē muṟaiyeṉṟā reṉṉi litutā ṉaiyameṉṟē ṉemakkun teriyu meṉattiruvā yiṉṉa lamuta mukukkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "Lord who shines eternally in Otriyur, the way women beg is simply to say 'give'," I said. He replied, "The proper way is to say 'give a kiss'." I said, "To me, this is asking for alms." Saying "We know that too," his holy mouth pours forth sweet nectar. What is this, my friend?
commentary: The simplest way to ask for his grace, she tells him, is just to say "give". He twists it at once and says the proper way to beg is to ask for a kiss. When she steers back to asking for spiritual alms, he smiles knowingly. He uses this romantic banter to test her longing and deepen it.

tamil: வளஞ்சே ரொற்றி யீரெனக்கு மாலை யணிவீ ரோவென்றேன்
லுளஞ்சேர்ந் தடைந்த போதேநின் னுளத்தி லணிந்தே முணரென்றே
யிளஞ்சீர் நகைசெய் தருள்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vaḷañcē roṟṟi yīreṉakku mālai yaṇivī rōveṉṟēṉ kuḷañcēr moḻippeṇ pāvāyniṉ kōlamaṉaikka ṇāmakiḻvā luḷañcērn taṭainta pōtēniṉ ṉuḷatti laṇintē muṇareṉṟē yiḷañcīr nakaicey taruḷkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "Lord of fertile Otriyur, will you place a garland on me?" I asked. He said, "O young woman with sweet words, know that the very moment we joyfully joined our hearts and entered your beautiful house, we placed a garland in your heart." He graces me with a beautiful youthful smile. What is this, my friend?
commentary: In Tamil tradition, placing a garland on someone marks marriage and eternal union. She asks whether the Lord will claim her this way. He says it is already done. From the very moment he entered her life, the true, invisible garland of their union was placed in her heart.

tamil: வீற்றா ரொற்றி நகரமர்ந்தீர் விளங்கு மலரே விளம்புநெடு
மாற்றா ரென்றே னிலைகாணெம் மாலை முடிமேற் பாரென்றார்
சாற்றாச் சலமே யீதென்றேன் சடையின் முடிமே லன்றென்றே
யேற்றா தரவான் மொழிகின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: vīṟṟā roṟṟi nakaramarntīr viḷaṅku malarē viḷampuneṭu māṟṟā reṉṟē ṉilaikāṇem mālai muṭimēṟ pāreṉṟār cāṟṟāc calamē yīteṉṟēṉ caṭaiyiṉ muṭimē laṉṟeṉṟē yēṟṟā taravāṉ moḻikiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "You reside in the majestic city of Otri," I said. "Are you the great enemy of the shining flower?" He said, "See our state. Look at the garland on our crown." I said, "This is unspoken deceit." He said, "It is not on the crown of matted hair." He speaks with eager affection. What is this, my friend?
commentary: The god of love shoots arrows made of flowers, so when she asks whether the Lord is the great enemy of the shining flower, she is teasing him as that god's foe. He answers her riddle with another and points to the flower garland he wears himself. Banter in verse like this shows how close and playful the bond between the soul and the divine can be.

tamil: புயப்பா லொற்றி யீரச்சம் போமோ வென்றே னாமென்றார்
வயப்பா வலருக் கிறையானீர் வஞ்சிப் பாவிங் குரைத்ததென்றேன்
வியப்பா நகையப் பாவெனும்பா வெண்பா கலிப்பா வுரைத்துமென்றே
யியற்பான் மொழிதந் தருள்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: puyappā loṟṟi yīraccam pōmō veṉṟē ṉāmeṉṟār vayappā valaruk kiṟaiyāṉīr vañcip pāviṅ kuraittateṉṟēṉ viyappā nakaiyap pāveṉumpā veṇpā kalippā vuraittumeṉṟē yiyaṟpāṉ moḻitan taruḷkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of Otri with strong shoulders, will fear depart?" I asked. He said, "Yes." I said, "You are the Lord of mighty poets. You have spoken a deceitful verse here." He said, "We will also speak the wondrous verse of laughter, the verse of 'appā', veṇpā, and kalippā." He speaks with natural grace. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She accuses him of speaking a deceitful verse, and the Tamil word she uses also names a poetic meter. He catches the pun and reels off other traditional meters, the veṇpā and kalippā among them. Warm humor and quick wit run all through the exchange.

tamil: தண்ணம் பொழில்சூ ழொற்றியுளீர் சங்கங் கையிற்சேர்த் திடுமென்றேன்
றிண்ணம் பலமேல் வருங்கையிற் சேர்த்தோ முன்னர் தெரியென்றார்
வண்ணம் பலவிம் மொழிக்கென்றேன் மடவா யுனது மொழிக்கென்றே
யெண்ணங் கொளநின் றுரைக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: taṇṇam poḻilcū ḻoṟṟiyuḷīr caṅkaṅ kaiyiṟcērt tiṭumeṉṟēṉ ṟiṇṇam palamēl varuṅkaiyiṟ cērttō muṉṉar teriyeṉṟār vaṇṇam palavim moḻikkeṉṟēṉ maṭavā yuṉatu moḻikkeṉṟē yeṇṇaṅ koḷaniṉ ṟuraikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of Otri surrounded by cool groves, place the conch bangles on my hand," I said. He said, "Did we place them on the hand that comes upon the firm stage? Know this first." I said, "There are many meanings to this word." He said, "O foolish girl, that applies to your word." He stands and speaks, capturing my thoughts. What is this, my friend?
commentary: In Tamil love poetry, a woman pining for the divine grows thin with longing, and her conch bangles slip from her wrists. She asks the Lord to put them back. He answers with a mysterious riddle about a dancing stage, and the two fondly accuse each other of speaking with hidden meanings.

tamil: உகஞ்சே ரொற்றி யூருடையீ ரொருமா தவரோ நீரென்றேன்
முகஞ்சேர் வடிவே லிரண்டுடையாய் மும்மா தவர்நா மென்றுரைத்தார்
சுகஞ்சேர்ந் திடுநும் மொழிக்கென்றேன் றோகா யுனது மொழிக்கென்றே
யிகஞ்சேர் நயப்பா லுரைக்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: ukañcē roṟṟi yūruṭaiyī rorumā tavarō nīreṉṟēṉ mukañcēr vaṭivē liraṇṭuṭaiyāy mummā tavarnā meṉṟuraittār cukañcērn tiṭunum moḻikkeṉṟēṉ ṟōkā yuṉatu moḻikkeṉṟē yikañcēr nayappā luraikkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of Otri where ages gather, are you a single great ascetic?" I asked. He said, "O you with two sharp spears on your face, we are three great ascetics." I said, "Joy gathers in your word." He said, "O girl like a peacock, that applies to your word." He speaks with worldly charm. What is this, my friend?
commentary: Is he a single great ascetic, she asks. Calling her beautiful eyes two sharp spears, he says he is actually three. That hints at the supreme one who holds the powers of creation, preservation and destruction. Their teasing turns the deepest spiritual truths into a joyful game of numbers.

tamil: ஊரா மொற்றி யீராசை யுடையே னென்றே னெமக்கலது
நேரா வழக்குத் தொடுக்கின்றாய் நினக்கே தென்றார் நீரெனக்குச்
சேரா வணமீ தென்றேன்முன் சேர்த்தீ தெழுதித் தந்தவர்தாம்
யாரார் மடவா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: ūrā moṟṟi yīrācai yuṭaiyē ṉeṉṟē ṉemakkalatu nērā vaḻakkut toṭukkiṉṟāy niṉakkē teṉṟār nīreṉakkuc cērā vaṇamī teṉṟēṉmuṉ cērttī teḻutit tantavartām yārār maṭavā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: "O Lord of the town of Otri, I have a claim," I said. He said, "You are filing an unjust lawsuit against us. What claim do you have?" I said, "This is a deed that does not bind you to me." He said, "O foolish girl, who are the ones who previously wrote and gave this deed?" He speaks. What is this, my friend?
commentary: She frames her longing as a lawsuit, claiming he owes her his presence. He asks, playfully, who wrote the original deed between them. The question points back to how old the bond between God and the soul is, an ancient and eternal claim.

tamil: வருத்தந் தவிரீ ரொற்றியுளீர் மனத்தி லகாத முண்டென்றே
னிருத்தந் தொழுநம் மடியவரை நினைக்கின் றோரைக் காணினது
வுருத்தன் பெயர்முன் னெழுத்திலக்க முற்றே மற்ற வெல்லையகன்
றிருத்த லறியா யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: varuttan tavirī roṟṟiyuḷīr maṉatti lakāta muṇṭeṉṟē ṉiruttan toḻunam maṭiyavarai niṉaikkiṉ ṟōraik kāṇiṉatu vuruttaṉ peyarmuṉ ṉeḻuttilakka muṟṟē maṟṟa vellaiyakaṉ ṟirutta laṟiyā yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I said, 'Lord of Otri who does not dispel my sorrow, is there an unfathomable depth in your heart?' He says, 'If we see those who think of our devotees who worship our dance, that word takes the numerical value of its first letter and expands beyond the limit of eight leagues, do you not know how it stays?' What is this, my friend?
commentary: She asks the Lord of Otriyur whether his heart is an unfathomable abyss. He answers with a clever riddle drawn from Tamil itself. The first letter of the word for abyss also stands for the number eight, and the rest of the word means a measure of distance. So he twists her question around: his grace reaches out eight leagues to welcome those who love his devotees.

tamil: மைய லகற்றீ ரொற்றியுளீர் வாவென் றுரைப்பீ ரோவென்றேன்
செய்ய வதன்மேற் சிகரம்வைத்துச் செவ்வ னுரைத்தா லிருவாவென்
றுய்ய வுரைப்பே மென்றார்நும் முரையென் னுரையென் றேனிங்கே
யெய்யுன் னுரையை யென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: maiya lakaṟṟī roṟṟiyuḷīr vāveṉ ṟuraippī rōveṉṟēṉ ceyya vataṉmēṟ cikaramvaittuc cevva ṉuraittā liruvāveṉ ṟuyya vuraippē meṉṟārnum muraiyeṉ ṉuraiyeṉ ṟēṉiṅkē yeyyuṉ ṉuraiyai yeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I asked, 'Lord of Otri who does not dispel my infatuation, will you say "Come"?' He said, 'If you place a crest on it and say it correctly, we will say "Sit and come" to save you.' I asked, 'Is your word my word?' He says, 'Shoot your word here.' What is this, my friend?
commentary: She longs for him to invite her with a simple "Come". He gives her a teasing puzzle instead, about adding marks to letters and joining words. In this poetic tradition the divine romance often speaks through riddling talk like this between the soul and God.

tamil: தாவென் றருளு மொற்றியுளீர் தமியேன் மோக தாகமற
வாவென் றருள்வீ ரென்றேனவ் வாவின் பின்னர் வருமெழுத்தை
மேவென் றதனிற் சேர்த்ததிங்கே மேவி னன்றோ வாவென்பே
னேவென் றிடுகண் ணென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
translit: tāveṉ ṟaruḷu moṟṟiyuḷīr tamiyēṉ mōka tākamaṟa vāveṉ ṟaruḷvī reṉṟēṉav vāviṉ piṉṉar varumeḻuttai mēveṉ ṟataṉiṟ cērttatiṅkē mēvi ṉaṉṟō vāveṉpē ṉēveṉ ṟiṭukaṇ ṇeṉkiṉṟā ritutāṉ cēṭi yeṉṉēṭī.
translation: I said, 'Lord of Otri who grants grace, will you say "Come" to dispel my lonely thirst of desire?' He says, 'If you take the letter that follows that "Vaa", join it there, and if it arrives here, I will say "Come", O you with eyes like arrows!' What is this, my friend?
commentary: Again she begs for a word of welcome to quench her spiritual thirst. He sets another teasing riddle on the Tamil alphabet and promises to invite her only once she solves it. The light banter of young lovers carries the soul's deep yearning for his presence.

tamil: என்மே லருள்கூர்ந் தொற்றியுளீ ரென்னை யணைவா னினைவீரேற்
பொன்மேல் வெள்ளி யாமென்றேன் பொன்மேற் பச்சை யாங்கதன்மே
லன்மேற் குழலாய் சேயதன்மே லலவ னதன்மேன் ஞாயிறஃ
தின்மே லொன்றின் றென்கின்றா ரிதுதான் சேடி யென்னேடீ.
